18/9/2026 (s7) — [idx-rmw-de] Indexed word RMW drops the BC address park.
            ADR 0093 (supersedes ADR 0088's "no emitter change" call).
            histbench/predbench rows only, NOT a full matrix regeneration.
================================================================================
ADR 0088 sized this site (`bins[idx]++`'s A→HL word-load reader stranding the
address, parked to BC and rebuilt) and declined to ship: 8 cells, 5 B/site,
too small on its own. Shipped now as a narrow 10-line text match in the same
`ir_lower.c` backward-liveness pass as `inc-mem`/`de-widen`/`z80n-add-a`
(pattern + B/C/D/E-all-dead-after gate), not a lowering change — same reason
it stays small.

Ran `gen_bench_matrix3.py histbench predbench` (all 11 CPUs, both frame
modes) against bin/z88dk-80cc md5 73ea5839f8c87df9b59c48eaedccd596, built from
HEAD 16caa4beed plus this uncommitted rung. NOT a full matrix regeneration —
every other bench/CPU cell in the table is untouched.

    bench       CPU    old fp/sp bytes      new fp/sp bytes      ticks (fp/sp)
    histbench   z80    4012 / 4053          4007 / 4048          -0.90M / -0.90M
    histbench   z180   3928 / 3969          3923 / 3964          -0.85M / -0.85M
    histbench   8080   —    / 4598          —    / 4593           —    / -1.20M

-5 B/cell, matching ADR 0088's original estimate exactly (the earlier
hand-count of -6 from the raw instruction text was off by one — `ld bc,hl`/

z80n TEXT-MATCHES the same 10-line pattern but the rung correctly declines to
fire there: traced live with a temporary debug probe, DE is live after the
sequence on z80n and dead on z80/z180/8080, all four proven by the SAME
backward pass on the SAME source. ADR 0088's static census had counted z80n
as an affected cell (5 B, 1 sp + 1 fp); the live liveness check disagrees, and
the live check is authoritative — the census was a text/reader-shape survey,
not a per-line liveness proof. ez80/r2ka/r4k/kc160/8085/gbz80/vm1 rows are
unaffected as before (do not reach this A→HL reader shape at all).

17/9/2026 (s5) — [shr arc]: the A-chain WIDENED, a dead L store REMOVED, and the
            masked shift finally reaches the site adr/0090 was written for.
            720-cell corpus scan, NOT a full matrix regeneration.
            THREE rungs. adr/0090 CORRECTED, adr/0091, adr/0092.
================================================================================
adr/0090 as committed carried two false claims. Both are now corrected in the
ADR, and both were invisible for the same reason: THE RUNG HAD NO OPT-OUT, so
its A/B had to compare two built binaries and could not be repeated later.

  1. "The full compile-only corpus size scan was unchanged" — FALSE.
     `IR_OFF=shr-a-chain` costs +44 B over 10 cells. It was worth -44 B on z80
     all along; the original scan could not isolate it.
  2. "4 bytes larger than the six-byte left-align route" — compares against a
     route the rung NEVER REACHES. The top-byte lowering is chosen earlier in
     gen_shr, so the A-chain only ever saw FULL-WIDTH `x >> n`. Its intended
     site, histbench `bins[(seed >> 3) & BMASK]++`, was never touched.

AGENTS.md now requires an opt-out on every code-changing rung, in the same
commit, because the opt-out IS the A/B mechanism. check_options.sh cannot catch
a rung that never had a gate.

SIZE — `src/80cc/scripts/corpus_sizescan.sh`, 30 benches x 12 CPUs x sp/fp,
       720 cells, against a PRESERVED HEAD binary (md5 51b6cfbaed…, verified
       identical to the installed 1c5e90a246 build).

    CPU        bytes   smaller  larger
    ez80_z80     -46       10       0
    kc160        -42       10       0
    gbz80        -40       10       4
    z180         -32       10       4
    z80          +12        3       4
    TOTAL       -148       43      12

  Separated by gate, each rung against the same build:
    shr-a-chain widening (z180/ez80/gbz80/kc160)   -178 B / 40 cells / 0 larger
    shr-dead-l  (the dead `ld l,a; ld a,l` pair)    -18 B / 14 cells / 0 larger
    shr-tbac    (the loop-gated trade)              +48 B / 12 cells  DELIBERATE

  The 12 larger cells are histbench and predbench ONLY, on the three enabled
  CPUs in both frame modes, +4 B each. The trade, in full view and nowhere else.

TICKS — the trade INVERTS on two CPUs, and this is the section's real lesson.

    CPU      histbench   predbench   shipped?
    z180       -4.202 %    -1.000 %   yes
    z80        -2.968 %    -0.692 %   yes
    gbz80      -0.618 %    -0.135 %   yes, marginal
    ez80       +2.438 %    +0.644 %   NO — slower
    kc160      +4.632 %    +0.900 %   NO — slower

  Same +4 bytes in all ten cells. On ez80/kc160 `add hl,hl` is about a cycle
  while the CB ops carry prefix cost, so five shifts beat three `srl h; rra`
  pairs and the rung spends bytes to LOSE ticks. An aggregate over the five
  CB-shift CPUs would have hidden this behind z80 and z180 and shipped a
  regression on two targets. REPORT A TRADE PER CPU; NEVER AVERAGE ONE.

  15 likely benches were A/B'd; only histbench and predbench move at all. The
  other 13 are byte- and tick-identical. crcbench and localbench run to a tick
  cap, so their totals are limit-bound either way and prove nothing.

TWO TRAPS WORTH THE NEXT SESSION'S TIME

  copt runs AFTER 80cc and removes the chain's `ld a,l`. The final asm shows
  only one of the pair, which reads as if the other was never emitted — it was.
  An emitted trace settled it; no IR dump could have, and `-O0` did not either.
  The first shr-dead-l matched `ld l,a` + chain and silently never fired.

  `BB.loop_depth` IS A DEAD FIELD. ir.c zeroes it, nothing assigns it, and the
  allocator keeps its own private bb_loop_depth[]. A loop-pressure test written
  against it answers "not in a loop" with a clean build and no warning — which
  is exactly how the first shr-tbac prototype failed. `pred[]` is also empty at
  lowering time, so bb_in_loop reads back edges off `succ[]`. Both now carry a
  warning at the field and a row in AGENTS.md.

GATES — long_ir 842/842 sp AND fp (was 832; +10 = the new targets), 454
        binaries, 0 failed. The only build error in either log is
        longshl_vm1.bin / mbf32_vm1.lib, the pre-existing VM1 float gap.
        New: long_ir/shrdeadl.c (5 variants), long_ir/shrtbac.c (5 variants).
        shrtbac carries the NEGATIVE cases too — `cold3` (same expression, no
        loop) and `deep4` (n==4, past the crossover) must NOT change, which is
        what stops the loop gate rotting into an unconditional rewrite.
        check_options.sh 130 names OK; check_gates.sh 43 listed live OK.

THE FOUR COMMITS SEPARATE CLEANLY BY CPU AND FRAME MODE
--------------------------------------------------------
The changed-cell pattern attributes itself, which is why no gate-on/gate-off
re-run was needed to tell them apart:

    ez80 fp, 32 of 32 cells        adr/0087 lea-frame-prologue. EVERY bench
        moved and ONLY in fp. ez80 sp moved on three benches only, and those
        three are the de-widen/shift benches below. -131 B, the largest single
        contribution after gbz80. Per-bench it is a flat -2 to -6 B (the dead
        `ld hl,-N; add hl,sp` pair), with divbench -17 B fp.

    gbz80 sp, 30 of 30 cells       adr/0086 regcopy-flow. EVERY bench moved.
        gbz80 has no IX so fp == sp and the column reads `= sp (no IX)`;
        the -250 B is therefore one frame mode, not two. Prior 720-cell
        code_compiler figure was -232 B; the extra 18 B is whole-binary.

    divbench + shiftbench + widthbench, ALL CPUs    adr/0085 de-widen, and on
        z80 also adr/0090. These are the only benches that move outside the
        two single-CPU sweeps above. divbench is the biggest mover on every
        CPU (-6 to -19 B), shiftbench next (-4 to -11 B).

    z80/z80n ticks on divbench and shiftbench carry BOTH adr/0085 and
    adr/0090, and this matrix CANNOT separate them — adr/0090 shipped as a
    tick trade with no compile-only size change, so its share of the -74 B
    z80 byte delta is zero by construction and its share of the tick win is
    not isolated here. adr/0090's own A/B was 60 z80 cells, 10 changed, all
    faster, -2,140,848 ticks. The z80 divbench tick move in this table
    (66.08M -> 64.80M fp, 68.18M -> 66.90M sp) is the two commits together.

    bitfieldbench, callbench, fixedbench move on z80 and ez80 fp only — the
    ez80 half is adr/0087, the z80 half is adr/0085.

================================================================================
17/9/2026 (s3) — [regcopy-flow]: GBZ80 skips an HL restore before a local
            loop back-edge whose target immediately reloads HL. ADR 0086.
            720-cell code_compiler scan, NOT a full matrix regeneration.
================================================================================
Census before building: final asm from 30 bench sources, z80-fp has 660
`ex de,hl` (373 in md5); gbz80-sp has 125 `ex de,hl`, 645 `ld de,hl`, and
270 `ld hl,de`. These are RAW counts, not recoverable bytes. Z80's common
`ex de,hl; adc hl,bc; ex de,hl` is required by the 32-bit carry path.
The selected GBZ80 rung is the dead `ld hl,de` after a slot store, followed
only by BC stepping and an unconditional jump to a local label that reloads
HL before any read. The direct regression asm diff deletes exactly that line.

SIZE — `src/80cc/scripts/corpus_sizescan.sh`, 30 benches x 12 CPUs x sp/fp
       `IR_OFF=regcopy-flow` as baseline, 720 cells on each side, no X:
    total -232 B    46 cells smaller    0 larger    all 660 non-GBZ80 cells equal

needs a `%` or a mask by a power of two feeding an accumulator that holds a BC
home, and outside those three benches the corpus does not do that. It ships

0 larger, 0 slower — which is what separates it from adr/0078's refused
`add hl,nn`, where concentration mattered because that rule was size-neutral.

THE CENSUS THAT CLOSED THE VEIN (the more useful half — full detail in adr/0085)
    166 zero-extension sites in bench + real, 442-499 over the whole asm dump,
    and the count barely moves with the CPU (z80 442, ez80 442, r2ka 450,
    gbz80 441, 8080 499). Most are at the z80 encoding floor already. Five more
    shapes sized and REFUSED, ~110 B over five separate rungs:
      dead `ld h,0`                    32 whole dump / 5 bench / 0 real =  10 B
      fastcall byte arg, 1-byte callee  8 sites                        =  16 B
      push hl/pop iy -> ld iyl,a        7 sites, 6 of them in enigma   =   7 B
      zero-ext byte vs 16-bit constant 12 sites, 8 in two files        =  48 B
      ld l,n + ld h,m -> ld hl,mn      19 sites whole dump             =  19 B
    Against [de-park]'s single rung for 98 B. Zero-extension is not one lever,
    it is five fifteen-byte ones. The gap against ez80clang is real but its
    cause is the HL bus, not a lowering pattern — that is vein 3.

================================================================================
16/9/2026 (escape audit) — the adr/0082 hole in FOUR more places. adr/0083
            CORRECTNESS, not gated. long_ir 809/809 sp+fp (7 new targets)
================================================================================
Two of the four are wrong on plain C with no address of a local anywhere:

    *p = a + x;  t = a + x;      ->  t = THE POINTER   (was 2028, want 7)
    t1 = a+x; *p = 5; t2 = a+x;  ->  t2 = t1           (was 55,   want 58)

Root cause: OP_ASSIGN's left is an ADDRESS, a compound assignment's left is an
LVALUE, and the two spellings collide on (deref (lv=p)). One reader served both.

    site                     shape that broke it
    ast_cse record           OP_ASSIGN (deref (lv=p)) read as "a write of p"
    ast_cse env              ...so beliefs about what p POINTS AT survived
    ir_opt_cse               a call holding &a writes a's SLOT, defines no vreg
    ast_cse_synthesize       hoisted over an indirect store (no sym written)
    ast_licm                 same, in a loop body

THE DIAGNOSIS WAS RIGHT AND THE CURE WAS NOT. The cause is real and reproducible
(RC_DE_ACC takes the best IY candidate, cannot keep it, and denies it to
ir_iy_reduction_pack — see the previous section). Everything that followed from
it failed.

ATTEMPT 1 — `iy-yield-idx2`. In fp mode idx2 IS IY, so the idx2 pool and the pack
want one register and the pack runs later. Yield when the pack's candidate has a
higher idx_ben.
  REFUTED ON SIZE: -1415 B against -1807 B without it, 13 larger vs 8.
  recordbench fp +80..+98 on FIVE CPUs (z80 353 -> 433).
>> WHY: idx_ben is the SAME UNIT for both candidates but a DIFFERENT MODEL. The
   idx2 pool wants IY as a plain index home; the pack wants it for `add iy,de`
   accumulation. Matching units is necessary and NOT sufficient — adr/0038's trap
   wearing a new face. THE PACK'S GAIN HAS NO COMPARABLE NUMBER; producing one is
   the prerequisite for any future attempt here.

ATTEMPT 2 — `iy-late-home`. ir_alloc_word_home_reject restores a WHOLE-ARRAY
snapshot taken at DE-pick time, erasing homes decided after it — including the
pack's. alloc_note_late_home already existed for exactly this (the call-split's
ranged BC home). Made the IY packs use it.
  MEASURED -1807 B / 56 smaller / 8 larger over 720 cells, and it FIXED sp
  listbench outright (16908133 against a 16929343 reference).
  >> THEN long_ir WENT RED: sp 718/727, fp 714/727. callsplit, idxbase,
     idxderef, slotaddr, rabmul, test.bin.
>> WHY IT IS UNSOUND: the snapshot CAN ALREADY HOLD AN IY HOME FOR ANOTHER VREG.
   Mirroring the pack's IY in does not remove that one, so the revert restores
   BOTH and two vregs own IY. The whole-array memcpy is not a blunt instrument
   by accident — restoring a CONSISTENT plan is the point, and a late decision
   preserved into a restored plan is by definition inconsistent with it.

ATTEMPT 3 — `de-yield-iy` alone (the DE pool yields a candidate the IY pack wants
when the pack's fallback is strictly worse).
  Sound-looking, and -788 B / 20 smaller / 4 larger over 720 cells.
  >> ALSO FAILS long_ir: sp 772/774, fp 768/774 (idxbase, idxderef, test.bin).
  >> AND IT DOES NOT FIX listbench ON ITS OWN: with the inline on, sp is back to
     18668129, the original +10.3%. The fix needed attempt 2, which miscompiles.

NET: IR_RABBIT_MUL stays OPT-IN for exactly the reason it already was.

>> PROCESS FAILURES WORTH MORE THAN THE CODE:
   (1) `make -C src/80cc PREFIX=$(pwd)` RUN FROM test/suites. src/80cc does not
       exist there, the && chain swallowed it, and bin/ kept a STALE BINARY that

16/9/2026 (later still) — THE listbench +10..13% IS AN ORDERING BUG, TRACED.
            RC_DE_ACC takes the best IY candidate and cannot keep it. Fix it and
            IR_RABBIT_MUL's measured -1.568% flips on by changing one default.
================================================================================
The IY pick is the loop-carried accumulator pack, and it changes WINNER:

    default (helper)      IY_ACC v0 bb22 score=17
    inline  (call-free)   IY_ACC v3 bb3  score=16

A LOWER-scoring candidate wins once more candidates become eligible — and the
selection is a plain use_count maximum, so v0 is not losing, it is ABSENT.

UPSTREAM CAUSE. idx2_home_available() returns 1 as soon as the function is
call-free, which admits the RC_DE_ACC pool, and that pool takes v0 FIRST:

    ALLOCMAP default   v0 phys=IY   home=[0,101]
    ALLOCMAP inline    v0 phys=DE   home=[0,101]   <- claimed by DE
                       v3 phys=IY                   <- the IY pack's consolation

The IY pack then skips it (`if (v == exclude) continue;`).

>> AND DE DOES NOT KEEP IT. v0 is live [0,101] — the WHOLE FUNCTION — and DE is
   the binop staging register, so it spills anyway. The pool took the best IY
   candidate in the function (idxben=251, against v3's 46 and v40's 79), could
   not realise it, and denied it to the register that could.

PROOF BY CONSTRUCTION — with the DE pool off, the call-free build makes the SAME
pick as the helper build:

    IR_RABBIT_MUL=1 IR_OFF=word-resident  ->  IY_ACC v0 bb22 score=17

>> THIS IS IN BOUNDS. It is NOT a missing cost term, which the index forbids —
   it is one pool admitting a candidate it cannot realise, ahead of a pool that
   could, and the two NEVER COMPARE. interval_benefit(..., GR_IX) already
   supplies the number to compare against; it is what IR_RANKDUMP prints as
   idxben.

NEXT: make RC_DE_ACC decline a candidate whose idxben beats its own realisable
benefit, or arbitrate the two pools together rather than in sequence. Then re-run
the 180-cell Rabbit matrix with IR_RABBIT_MUL=1 and expect listbench's +10..13%
to go.

incl. kc160, both frame modes:

16/9/2026 (later, CORRECTION) — THE PREMISE OF THE SECTION BELOW IS WRONG.
            l_mult ON RABBIT IS ALREADY THE HARDWARE `mul`. What ships is a copt
            store-reload fold, −138 B / −0.105 % / 0 larger. Inlining the
            multiply is now OPT-IN `IR_RABBIT_MUL=1`. adr/0075 rewritten.
================================================================================
CAUGHT BY THE MAINTAINER, not by any gate here. libsrc/l/sccz80/4-r2ka/l_mult.asm
(r2ka/r3k/r4k/r6k via r2ka.lst) is:

    l_mult:
    l_mult_u:
        ld  bc,hl
        mul             ; hlbc = bc * de
        ld  hl,bc
        ret

So "Rabbit never emits its mul" was FALSE, and the strength-reducer comment that
looked like a bug ("targets with a hardware multiply keep the helper") was
CORRECT. The 60-vs-5 l_mult census below is a real number that means something
ELSE: the 5 are what survives strength reduction on CPUs whose helper is a real
loop; Rabbit's 60 were each three instructions behind a `call`.

>> READ THE HELPER THE CALL ACTUALLY REACHES, ON THAT CPU, before concluding an
   instruction is un-mined. The opcodes.dat sweep tells you what the COMPILER
   emits, not what the LIBRARY does.

THE COST WAS THE CALL, NOT THE MULTIPLY. `call l_mult` is an opaque IR_HCALL, so
the product went through a frame slot at every site:

    call l_mult
    ld (sp+0),hl      ; store
    ld hl,(sp+0)      ; dead reload — 3 bytes, in histbench's hot loop

FIX 1, REFUTED AND IT CANNOT WORK — describe the helper's clobbers truthfully.
Rabbit's l_mult writes only HL and BC (mul sets no flags; nothing touches DE, A
or memory) where the preserves-index-alt tier charges HL|DE|BC|A|F|MEM. Making
it exact measured **+0 bytes over 180 cells**, byte-identical even on a shape
built to hold a value in DE across the call.

>> THE REASON GENERALISES TO EVERY CPU AND IS WORTH KEEPING: **DE IS THE
   MULTIPLY'S SECOND ARGUMENT.** The lowering loads src1 into DE immediately
   before the call, so nothing can be live in DE across an l_mult for a truthful
   clobber set to preserve. Same for A and F. DO NOT RE-ATTEMPT.

FIX 2, SHIPPED — elide the dead reload. 80cc_rules.1 already folds this defect
three times (#R2 for (hl), #G1 for gbz80 `ld hl,sp+N`, #S1/#S2 for the
two-instruction `ld hl,N; add hl,sp`) and NONE can match Rabbit's ONE-instruction
`ld (sp+N),hl`. The family simply had no Rabbit member. 23 sites, sp mode only
(fp goes through (ix+d), already covered by #R4); volatile carries a ;volatile
stamp so it cannot match.

    size    -138 B     63 smaller   0 LARGER
    ticks   -0.105 %   63 faster    3 slower (<=+0.31%, and those benches are
                                    BYTE-IDENTICAL — the movement is framework code)
    leak    every non-Rabbit CPU byte-identical, both frame modes
    long_ir 774/774 sp, 774/774 fp (SERIAL)

    >> CHECK THAT FOLD FAMILY FOR OTHER GAPS. It is per-ADDRESSING-FORM, so every
       CPU with its own slot spelling needs its own member.

THE THREE-WAY MEASUREMENT, 180 Rabbit cells, both modes:

    A  copt fold only        -138 B   -0.105 %   0 larger   3 slower (<=0.31%)
    B  inline only           -721 B   -1.568 %  21 larger  15 slower
    C  both                  -721 B   -1.568 %  21 larger  15 slower

>> C == B EXACTLY. All 23 dead reload pairs come from l_mult sites, so A and B
   are two fixes for the SAME defect. B additionally removes the call — which is
   where both its extra win AND its regression come from.

WHY B IS OPT-IN. listbench +10..13 % on every Rabbit, both modes. Cause
IDENTIFIED, not guessed: removing the call makes the function CALL-FREE, a
different set of proposers runs, and IR_HOMEMAP shows v0 phys=IY home=[0,101]
before, spilled after. That is backwards — call-free should ENABLE homing — and
it is a PROPOSER/ADMISSION question, not a cost-term one, so it is in bounds.
Answer it and a measured -1.568 % flips on by changing one default.

THE COPT RULE THE INLINE EXPOSED (gate KEPT even though the default no longer
emits the shape). rabbit_rules.1 folded `pop bc ; push hl` -> `ld (sp+0),hl`,
sound only when the popped BC is DEAD — it reads pop bc as sccz80's discard-TOS
idiom. Under IR_RABBIT_MUL=1 the BC bracket emits a real restore; the fold
dropped it AND scribbled on a parked word, and enigma on r2ka printed nothing
instead of RXSEC. %notcompiler 80cc. Costs 0 BYTES and ~0.3 % on callbench's
three fp cells (the one folded site there has BC dead). Kept because the rule is
unsound for 80cc generally — 80cc emits real `pop bc` restores elsewhere (the
z80n barrel-shift bracket) and only luck keeps them apart on Rabbit today — and
correctness must not depend on remembering to edit a rules file when flipping an
env gate. The kc160 copies are LEFT ALONE: gating them costs a byte where BC is
genuinely dead, and no 80cc kc160 shape needs it. Recorded, not paid for.

16/9/2026 — VEIN 1 OF THE CPU SWEEP PAYS: the Rabbit has a one-byte hardware
            multiply (`mul`, F7) and the backend has never emitted it. SHIPPED
            default-on, `--opt-disable=rabbit-mul`. adr/0075.
================================================================================
THE SWEEP. Diffed every CPU's declared instruction set against what 80cc's
lowerer actually emits, from src/z80asm/dev/cpu/opcodes.dat (the authoritative
asm/CPU/synth table) against a full-corpus asm dump per CPU, both frame modes.
Only 8085 and gbz80 had ever been swept. vm1 came out CLEAN — all four of its
CPU_HAS_* macros are consulted.

THE FIND. build_muldiv_integer skips constant-multiply strength reduction on
Rabbit, and the comment says exactly why:

    Skipped on targets with a hardware multiply (Rabbit `mul`), which keep the
    helper.

Nothing ever emitted `mul`. So Rabbit got NEITHER the shift-add chain NOR the
instruction, and every 16-bit multiply was a bit-serial `call l_mult`:

    call l_mult sites, corpus, sp mode
    r2ka 60   r4k 60   r6k 60      <-- the outlier
    z80 5     z80n 5   z180 5   ez80 5   8085 5   gbz80 5   vm1 5
    kc160 0                           <-- has mul de,hl, uses it

`mul` is HL:BC = BC * DE, signed 16x16 -> 32, ONE byte, 12 cycles. Low 16 bits
of a product are sign-agnostic, so one instruction serves both signednesses —
the same argument kc160 already relies on.

RESULTS, 240-cell size matrix + 240-cell tick matrix (r2ka/r4k/r6k/kc160 x sp/fp),
against d2c2265e:

    size    -724 B      118 smaller   21 larger   0 aborts
    ticks   -1.389 %    129 faster    17 slower   0 failures
    leak    z80 z80n z180 ez80 8085 8080 gbz80 vm1 ALL BYTE-IDENTICAL, both modes
    long_ir 739/739 sp, 739/739 fp before rabmul.c; 774/774 both modes with it
            (SERIAL — see the trap below)
    behav   enigma/clisp/adv_a/sorter/fib OK on r2ka and kc160, both modes

    biggest tick wins    histbench -18.3%  divbench -8.8%  predbench -6.9%
                         vecbench -7.6%    callbench -5.2%  bitfieldbench -4.7%
    the 17 slower        listbench +10..13% (every Rabbit, both modes)
                         structbench r6k +7.3 / +12.2%

>> THE SLOWER CELLS ARE NOT THE MULTIPLY. Replacing an HCALL with an IR_MUL makes
   the function CALL-FREE, so a different set of proposers runs and listbench's
   IY index home is not re-picked (IR_HOMEMAP: v0 phys=IY home=[0,101] in the
   reference, phys=spill after). The multiply itself is 3 instructions against a
   helper call. This is the allocator capture gap (adr/0036-0038) reacting to a
   changed IR shape, not a cost this rung can price.

TWO BUGS THE SHAPE FOUND, both of which would have shipped silently:

(1) DISPATCHING ON WIDTH FIRST IS WRONG ON RABBIT. Rabbit has no 8x8 multiply, so
    a narrowed byte operand must take the 16x16 arm too. `if (width == 2)` first
    dropped them into the 8x8 packing path, which emits `mlt hl` — not a Rabbit
    instruction. structbench/fixedbench failed to assemble. The Rabbit test now
    precedes the width dispatch.

(2) A RESIDENT BC TENANT NEEDS THE push/pop BRACKET. BC is the multiplicand, so
    without it a BC word home dies. It aborts loudly (require_slot), which is the
    one piece of luck here.

>> AND THE ONE THAT WAS NOT SILENT, BUT WAS INVISIBLE. copt's rabbit_rules.1 folds

       pop bc ; push hl   ->   ld (sp+0),hl

   which is sound ONLY when the popped BC is DEAD — the rule reads `pop bc` as
   sccz80's discard-TOS idiom. The new bracket is the first 80cc Rabbit `pop bc`
   that is a real restore; when the product then went to a stack transient the
   two landed adjacent, the fold dropped the restore AND scribbled on the parked
   word, and enigma on r2ka printed nothing instead of RXSEC.

   THE COMPILER'S OWN ASM WAS CORRECT AT EVERY STAGE. `z88dk-80cc` direct output
   had `pop bc; push hl`; only `zcc -a` — which has been through copt — showed
   the pop gone. The IR dumps see none of this. THIS IS ALREADY IN THE INDEX AS A
   TRAP AND IT STILL COST AN HOUR.

   Gated `%notcompiler 80cc`. The same rule is in kc160_rules.1 twice (already
   gated off sdcc); both gated off 80cc too. It fires exactly ONCE on the kc160
   corpus, in callbench, on genuine argument cleanup where BC really is dead —
   so that gate costs 1 byte and +0.10% on two kc160 tick cells, and closes the
   same latent class.

>> MEASUREMENT TRAP, NEW ONE: `make -k -j4` on long_ir GARBLES THE LOG. Concurrent
   writes interleave mid-line ("ile1 run, 1 passed"), so the summed run count is
   NONDETERMINISTIC and UNDER-counts: 712 and 728 on two runs of the same binary
   set, against a true 739 serially. The binary set was identical both times
   (376 targets, verified). Count from a SERIAL run or the number is fiction.

>> AND THE OLD ONE, AGAIN: the corpus size scan leaves a stale /tmp/*.o when a
   compile fails, so the row reports the PREVIOUS file's size. That is what
   "structbench r2ka sp 375->750" and "fixedbench 404->765" were — not a
   regression, a failed compile reporting a neighbour's number. A doubled figure
   is a symptom, not a discovery.

REGRESSION test/suites/long_ir/rabmul.c, 7 targets incl. rabmul_r2ka_keep (rung
off) and rabmul_8080 (no `mul`, a control). Its enigma case is a CONDENSED
examples/console/enigma.c because FIVE SMALLER SHAPES WERE TRIED FIRST and none
reproduced the copt fold — each left an instruction between the pop and the push.
Verified to FAIL with the copt gate removed, and to FAIL TO COMPILE with the BC
bracket removed.

Generator: test/suites/gen_bench_matrix3.py (run it — the absolute source paths
are load-bearing, 30 B through __FILE__ in the framework's assert strings).
Cells are `bytes / ticks(millions)` of the whole -create-app binary.
sccz80 runs on every CPU; xcc is a z80-only toolchain so its columns stay z80.

WHAT MOVED since the 13/9 (s5) table
------------------------------------

1. TRUTHFUL HOME INTERVALS, default-on (ADR 0027, `470685c83c`). Stage 1 of the
   ranging arc. Every register home now narrows from whole-function to the
   value's true live range.
     720 size cells: 20 smaller, ZERO larger, -136 B.
     660 tick cells (11 CPUs x sp/fp): -0.0410%, 20 faster, ZERO slower.
   Bytes and cycles move together and on the SAME 20 cells — a truthful window
   lets a point query serve a value from its register where the whole-function
   window said "spilled". `--opt-disable=tight-homes` opts out byte-identically.

   It had been parked as "refuted" and was not. Two bugs had to go first, and
   both were one confusion in opposite directions — NARROWED versus NARROWER
   THAN:
     - `frameless_ok` rejected every parameter, because `ir_home_is_ranged`
       cannot tell a home narrowed to the live range (value DEAD outside,
       harmless) from one narrower than it (value SLOTTED outside, the real
       hazard). Fixed with `ir_home_covers_live_range` (`5d142bf57b`).
     - the step WIDENED an already-ranged home: it assigned the live range
       instead of clamping to it, so a call-split window [12,36] became [1,75]
       and the lowerer believed BC held a value that was slotted. A LATENT
       MISCOMPILE, not a size regression — it surfaced as +14 B only because the
       path that ran reloaded from the slot anyway (`9e1a6ae31b`).
   Progression as each landed: 35 cells larger -> 24 -> 0.

2. 8085 LDSI SLOT ADDRESSES (ADR 0039, `7211272b43`). `ld hl,N; add hl,sp`
   (4 B / 20 T) becomes `ld de,sp+N; ex de,hl` (3 B / 14 T), as a
   liveness-gated rewrite in the emitted-text post-pass.
     8085: -366 B, 46 cells smaller, ZERO larger.
     8085 ticks: -0.948%, 46 faster, ZERO slower.
     No leak: every non-8085 cell of 720 byte-identical.
   Three guards, each a real hazard: D and E dead (`ex de,hl` is a SWAP, so DE
   returns holding the old HL), F dead (`add hl,sp` WRITES CARRY, the LDSI pair
   does not), and N in 0..255 (LDSI's operand is one unsigned byte). The 1574
   DE-live sites are left alone: 2 T at equal size is not worth a third form.

WHAT WAS REFUSED, with numbers
------------------------------

3. ADR 0036 — charging a param eviction for the framelessness it costs.
   Measured -229 B / 0 larger and was WRONG: the term fired in sp mode, where
   `frameless_ok` returns 0 on its second line. Correctly guarded it is INERT
   (0 cells). `long_ir/leaimm` caught it at +17 B — a file OUTSIDE the 720-cell
   matrix. A size claim must name the file set it covers.

4. ADR 0037 — pricing the BC eviction in the arbiter's own denomination.
   +2 B (38 smaller / 22 larger) and +0.118% ticks (24 faster / 29 slower).
   A margin sweep (100/125/150/175/200/300%) does not rescue it; the best is
   125% at -16 B with 12 cells still larger and ticks still net worse.

5. ADR 0038 — pricing the 8085 correctly. The 8085 falls through to the z80 row
   in BOTH cost tables and is not a z80: measured, a word slot is 33 cycles
   against the charged 45, write 26 vs 41, step 65 vs 92; bytes 5/4/9/10 against
   8/7/9/16. Correcting it is WORSE on both axes: +44 B (6 larger, 0 smaller),
   +0.037% ticks. A home's modelled benefit is slot-cost minus register-cost, so
   a cheaper slot cuts every 8085 home's value by 32% and the allocator opens
   fewer. The measured rows are recorded in the ADR so nobody re-measures them.
   NB the first attempt priced the STEP at 36 by assuming LDSI holds the address
   in DE across a read-modify-write. It does not — all 804 `ld (de),hl` sites
   sit exactly one line after their own `ld de,sp+N`. That wrong step measured
   -104 B and ran lexbench +4.3% SLOWER WHILE SHRINKING, which is the same
   symptom on the same bench the Z80 cost row already records from the last time
   someone assumed address reuse.

THE QUESTION THAT CLOSED
------------------------

6. `bc-evict`'s modelled benefit DOES NOT EXIST. Three attempts to price the
   eviction better all failed (3,4,5 above). A realisation verifier joined
   against IR_HOMEMAP settled why: on matrixbench/stencil z80-sp the eviction
   frees BC, packs two more values into it, and LOSES TWO IY HOMES doing it —
   total register homes 19 -> 19. It is a SWAP, not a gain. Across six benches
   the pass changes total register homes by +0, +1, +0, +2, +0, +0.
   So do not tune `bc-evict`. If it is revisited the question is whether it
   should exist at all, and the measurement is TOTAL RESIDENCY via an
   IR_HOMEMAP class census — not BC occupancy, and not a cost term.
   Method note: the per-function summary showed NO change on the regressing CPU
   while 12 of 22 per-vreg rows differed. A coarse probe hid the answer.

Also this session: a static DE-clean proof now runs with no ambient lowering
point (`5406b1073b`), taking window rejections across the corpus from 26 to 0;
and 11 shipped optimisations gained ADRs 0040-0050 with their bench figures
moved out of code comments.

13/9/2026 (s5) — FULL MATRIX at HEAD `3116e6a6b7` (branch 80cc-index-residency,
            tree-identical to `7a493cf450`). **330 rows, 30 benches x
            11 CPUs.** Regenerated whole, not spliced. TEN commits; see below.
            **330 rows, 30 benches x 11 CPUs.** Regenerated whole, not spliced.

Generator: test/suites/gen_bench_matrix3.py (run it — the absolute source paths
are load-bearing, 30 B through __FILE__ in the framework's assert strings).
Cells are `bytes / ticks(millions)` of the whole -create-app binary.
sccz80 runs on every CPU; xcc is a z80-only toolchain so its columns stay z80.

WHAT MOVED since the 13/9 (s4) table: ONE change in two halves plus the cost
term that makes them pay — 80cc's index home stops being a VALUE CARRIER and
becomes an ADDRESSING MODE.

  `idx-deref` (idx_deref_reg, ir_lower_ops.inc.c) — a MEM_VREG access whose
  base is homed in IX/IY now reads or writes its field AT A DISPLACEMENT
  instead of coming back through `push iy;pop hl`. Byte through A, word as two
  displaced moves, plus a PR_DE destination form. Before this the corpus held
  ZERO `(iy+d)` accesses against sdcc's 47.

  `deref-offset` (ir_opt_deref_offset, ir_opt.c) — folds `t = p + K; *t` into
  `*(p + K)`, which is what puts K in mem.offset where the rung can spell it.
  ►► MEASURED ALONE IN THE PREVIOUS SESSION AT z80 +77 B. It only pays when the
  offset is FREE, so it is aimed rather than general: a width-2 read-only
  pointer PARAMETER (no def in the function, so no dominance argument is
  needed), never stepped, dereferenced at 2+ sites counted THROUGH the temps,
  every folded displacement inside the index byte.

  ►► **THE COST TERM IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART, NOT THE LOWERING.**
  g0_deref_offset_bytes/_cost (ir_alloc.c) charge the walk to a field: free for
  IX/IY, the HL copy plus the walk for BC/DE, the walk alone for a slot. Split
  by `IR_IDXPRICE=0` (rung on, term off) the rung alone is worth **-67 B** and
  the term **-466 B**. Without it the model rated a BC home and an index home
  ALIKE for a struct pointer read at four offsets; BC ranks first, took the
  pointer, and the index home fell to a scalar that pays at every read —
  bitfieldbench's reg_set had the VALUE in IX and the POINTER in BC.
  NB the CYCLE row was already right: `IX deref 19` IS `ld a,(ix+d)`. The table
  was not mispriced, the LOWERING was missing. Only the offset was unpriced.

RESULT, measured as gate-off -> gate-on with the SAME compiler (see the note
below on why the s4 table is NOT the baseline). Over the four benches that move
x 11 CPUs x sp/fp = 88 whole-binary cells:

  **-2422 B and -4.276 % ticks**, 44 cells smaller / 2 larger, 44 faster /
  2 slower. The two are the IY save, which is not optional.

  bitfieldbench  z80 sp 4522 -> 4484 (-4.34 % ticks), z180 sp -38 B (-6.54 %),
                 ez80 sp -53 B (-6.47 %), z80n sp -34 B (-4.17 %)
  recordbench    z180 sp 3914 -> 3776 (-138 B, -41.00 % ticks), fp -107 B (-32.35 %)
                 kc160 sp -67 B / -24.6 % (see the revisit below — it was the
                 WORST cell at +9.6 % before that landed)
  ptrbench       r4k fp -22 B (-5.33 %), r2ka fp -18 B (-5.34 %), kc160 -14/-15 B
  structbench    ez80 fp -8 B (-11.53 %)

  Static section-size scan over the WHOLE corpus (29 benches x 8 CPUs x sp/fp,
  464 cells, `code_compiler` only), measured TWO ways:

    every opt gate off -> on, with the IY save in both:  **-2272 B, 65 cells
        smaller, 0 LARGER** — this is what the optional work is worth.
    against the pre-session REFERENCE compiler:          **-2139 B, 49 smaller,
        20 larger** — the 20 are the IY save (+133 B), which is not optional and
        is the price of code that was previously WRONG.

►► **A THIRD COMMIT: `idx2-revisit`, a LATENT ARBITRER BUG this exposed.**
The worst cell was recordbench kc160 at **+7 B AND +9.6 % ticks**, and it was
not the term being wrong. The term correctly made `churn`'s struct pointer the
TOP index candidate in the function (idxben 0 -> 288). Then unified_arbitrate's
param-yields-to-a-waiting-counter rule deferred it — and the counter went on to
take **BC** from the BC arm later in the same loop, after which its own IDX2
candidate was skipped as already-placed. **Nobody ever claimed the index
register**, and the pointer, whose BC benefit the same term had just cut from
112 to 28, fell to a frame SLOT. Zero `(ix+d)` emitted, hot 68-use pointer in
memory. The deferral was never revisited.

  kc160 recordbench   off 3544B/1.43M   term-on 3551B/1.57M   +revisit 3477B/1.08M

►► The revisit is **INERT ON ITS OWN**: +0 B across all 464 corpus cells and
byte-identical to the pre-change compiler across 348 asm files. It only ever
fires where the offset term first makes a param the top index candidate. That is
what a latent bug looks like. `--opt-disable=idx2-revisit` opts out.
It takes the change from -533 B / 6 larger to **-728 B / 4 larger**.

►► **A FOURTH COMMIT: `idx-fill` (`c73062fac5`) — and it needed a TICKS FIX
under it.** The last slow cell was bitfieldbench ez80 fp (+7.43 % ticks at -8 B).
Two separate causes, both now closed:

  (a) FILLING the home. The model prices ACCESSES and charges NOTHING for
      filling a home, so on ez80 fp — where filling BC is the native
      `ld bc,(ix+6)` and filling IY was not — an index home looked free:

        before:  ld hl,12 / add hl,sp / ld a,(hl+) / ld h,(hl) / ld l,a
                 / push hl / pop iy
        after:   ld iy,(ix+6)

      Maintainer's tip. `ld iy,(ix+d)` is one 3-byte instruction on ez80 AND
      kc160; ez80 also has `ld iy,(hl)` (2 B) for the sp-mode path, and kc160
      has `ld iy,(sp+n)` (3 B) which ez80 does NOT (z80asm rejects it) — hence
      three helpers, not one CPU test.

  (b) THE WORD DEREF, which is what actually dominated. Every function on ez80
      fp got SMALLER and ticks still rose, because the rung emitted
      `ld l,(iy+0); ld h,(iy+1)` where **ez80, kc160 AND Rabbit all have
      `ld hl,(iy+d)` as ONE 3-byte instruction**. On z80/z180 that form is 6 B —
      z80asm synthesising the very two moves the rung writes by hand — so the
      explicit pair stays there. DE has the single form on ez80/kc160 only
      (`ld de,(iy+6)` is 6 B synthetic on Rabbit), so the PAIR is part of the
      test, not just the CPU.

►► **THE TICKS BUG UNDERNEATH (`6993194ff1`).** Emitting `ld iy,(ix+d)` for
kc160 produced a WRONG answer, which looked like a miscompile and was an
EMULATOR fault. `kc160_ld_xy_ixysd` wrote xl/xh in BOTH arms of its dest test,
and — the larger fault — both xy handlers decoded the BASE register with the
**rr** family's nibble offsets. Assembled ground truth:

    ld ix,(iy+d) ed 88 | ld ix,(ix+d) ed 89 | ld ix,(sp+d) ed 8a
    ld iy,(iy+d) ed 98 | ld iy,(ix+d) ed 99 | ld iy,(sp+d) ed 9a   base 8/9/a
    ld (iy+d),ix ed 80 | ld (ix+d),ix ed 81 | ld (sp+d),ix ed 82   base 0/1/2
    ld bc,(iy+d) ed 8c | ld bc,(ix+d) ed 8d                        base c/d/e

so the loads needed `- 0x08` (not `- 0x0c`) and the stores `- 0x00` (not
`- 0x04`); everything landed on SP instead. Also `case 0x90` (LD (IY+d),IY) had
no `iskc160()` branch at all, and `0x91`'s comment said (IY+d) where it is
(IX+d). All seven forms now verify under z88dk-ticks on ez80, kc160, r2ka and
r4k. NB `case 0x89` was NOT missing — it falls through into 0x99.

►► **A FIFTH COMMIT: `206a8f0cd1` — an fp function homing a value in IY never
SAVED the caller's IY.** In fp mode the idx2 spare IS IY (`ir_idx2_reg`: frame
IX -> spare IY) and the fp ABI treats it as callee-saved, but
`frame_has_saved_iy` only ever asked about `idx3_reg`, which is sp-mode. So the
save was never emitted. `frame_has_saved_ix` tests the PhysReg directly and had
no such hole; the IY side now matches it.

►► **PRE-EXISTING, and live in the reference compiler** — intbench `mix_table`,
queenbench, sortbench, listbench, localbench, structbench, all fp. It stayed
latent while fp idx2 homes were rare; idx-deref made every read-only pointer
param a candidate and it became reproducible. Cost: **+133 B** over 464 cells,
34 functions x ~4 B, and the save is conditional on a vreg actually being homed
there (verified: zero functions save IY without using it).

►► **TWO TRAPS IT TAUGHT, both of which fooled me first.**
  1. A "does this function save IY?" TEXT SCAN MUST NOT TREAT `push iy` AS A
     SAVE. `emit_idx_word_to_reg` READS an IY home with `push iy; pop rr` on
     CPUs with no cheaper form, so every buggy function scans as clean — which
     is exactly what I reported before catching it.
  2. `long_ir` targets are PER TEST. `idxderef.c` was registered for z80 sp/fp
     + 8080 + gbz80 only, so the suite passed 725/725 while **ez80-fp
     miscompiled**. Any test covering an index-register feature needs ez80,
     z180, kc160 and both Rabbits in BOTH frame modes — now 12 targets.

►► **REFUTED: pricing the index home's OPEN cost.** The allocator charges for
ACCESSES and nothing for opening a home, so it will still hand out an IY home
that cannot repay its own 4-byte prologue — the 23 larger cells are all this.
Three variants were built and measured against the un-charged model's -1162 B:

    save + full param fill      -1015 B  (43 smaller, 16 larger)
    save + pair-write delta       -849 B  (28 smaller, 25 larger)
    save only                     -967 B  (36 smaller, 25 larger)
    NO open cost (shipped)      **-1162 B** (38 smaller, 23 larger)

ALL THREE LOSE. Only the harshest cuts the regressed-cell count (23 -> 16) and
it pays 147 B for it, by refusing homes that do pay — bitfieldbench z80 sp went
1005 -> 1041, straight back to baseline, because reg_get's idxben fell 162 -> 67
under BC's 156. The first cut also charged the WHOLE fill to IX/IY, which is
plain wrong: a BC home for a param reads the caller slot too, so only the
callee-save push/pop is genuinely asymmetric. Correcting that made it WORSE
(-849), which is the real finding: the arbiter's rankings are near-ties across
many candidates and a flat per-candidate penalty shuffles allocations far beyond
the cases it targets. ►► The 23 cells are not bad decisions — they are the
correct price of saving IY in functions where the home is still net-positive,
+133 B against -1162 B. Do not re-attempt this as a flat term.

►► **A SIXTH COMMIT: `82e695119d` — the arbiter never priced the PAIRING.**
`unified_arbitrate` is isolation-priced greedy: it walks candidates in rank
order, gives each its own best class, and lets whatever is left take what
remains. BC and an index home are NOT interchangeable in the same direction:

    a VALUE in BC is `ld a,c`             (1 B,  4 T)
    a VALUE in IX/IY is `push iy;pop hl`  (4 B, 25 T) — it cannot feed the ALU
    a BASE  in IX/IY is `(iy+d)`          (3 B, 19 T) at ANY offset
    a BASE  in BC is `ld a,(bc)`          (1 B,  7 T) at offset 0 ONLY

so a pointer prefers BC only narrowly while a value prefers it hugely — and the
greedy order hands BC to the pointer. bitfieldbench reg_set, z80 fp, by the
arbiter's OWN numbers: v0 pointer BC 226 / IX 217, v1 value BC 150 / IX 65;
greedy = 291, swapped = **367**. xcc makes the swapped choice, which is why it
needed 73 instructions for reg_set where 80cc needed 136.

The swap pass is deliberately narrow — one BC tenant, one index tenant, both
already placed, each admissible in the other's class, and the swap must WIN on
the same interval_benefit the loop ranked by. `--opt-disable=home-swap`.
►► IT GENERALISES WELL PAST THE BENCH THAT FOUND IT: corpus **-833 B, 12 cells
smaller, 0 larger**, and on ticks recordbench ez80 sp **-62.4 %**, z80 sp
-31.6 %, r2ka sp -38.4 % — aggregate **-4.9 %** over 22 cells. recordbench is
"stationary struct-pointer field churn", the purest form of the shape.

►► **A SEVENTH: `7a493cf450` — duplicate masks, as a COPT rule not an IR fold.**
`and N; and N` is idempotent. The IR-level mask FOLDING was refuted (+40 B,
lengthens the masked value's live range); these two are ADJACENT after register
allocation, so removing one cannot move a live range at all. `%check 0 <= %1 <=
255` pins the operand to an 8-bit LITERAL, which is what makes it airtight — it
excludes `and (hl)`/`and (ix+d)`, where two consecutive reads are not
interchangeable if the location is volatile. Corpus **-144 B, 16 cells, 0
larger**, every CPU including 8080/gbz80. Source: the bitfield extract-then-
insert pair emits the field-width mask twice.

BITFIELDBENCH, the bench that drove all of this, z80:

    sccz80      4207 B / 57.80 M
    80cc s4     4582 B / 42.45 M   <- session start
    80cc now    4453 B / 37.95 M   <- -10.6 % ticks, -129 B
    xcc -Of     4103 B / 27.02 M

►► **WHY IT WAS WORTH CHASING.** Normalised across CPUs, bitfieldbench's
ez80/kc160 lead (4.25x / 6.01x over z80) is DEAD AVERAGE — those CPUs are simply
~4-5x faster per instruction, and reading a codegen story into that is a trap.
The real signal is different: 80cc's speed lead over sccz80 is 2.19x (z80) /
2.88x (ez80) / 1.83x (kc160) across 30 benches, but on bitfieldbench it was
1.36x / 1.92x / 1.23x — BELOW the median on every CPU, second-weakest of 30.
(switchbench is weakest at 1.22x and is NOT a defect: sccz80 and 80cc use the
same table-driven algorithm, so convergence is expected.)

►► **NEXT LEVER, sized but NOT built: byte temps go to FRAME SLOTS.**
`ld (ix-6),a … or (ix-6)` where xcc holds the value in E — ~30 of the 36
instructions still separating reg_set (109) from xcc (73). 183 byte-slot ops
across 148 corpus functions, ceiling about -366 B. ►► RELAXING THE EXISTING BYTE
HOME IS REFUTED: `byte_home_realizable` wants `use_count >= 8` and these temps
are read ONCE, but lowering the gate gives +0 B at 4 and 2 (use_count counts
READS; write-once/read-once scores 1) and **+307 B / 49 cells larger at 1**. The
E home is SLOT-BACKED — only the single-BB C home is slotless — so homing a
single-use temp there does not remove the slot, it adds traffic on top. It is
also one-per-function. The lever is a DIFFERENT mechanism: a slotless
multi-tenant byte scratch packer over disjoint ranges, the byte analogue of
`ir_bc_pack`. Interval machinery reusable; lowerer belief-tracking is the
unknown, and `IR_PR_D`/`IR_PR_B` are declared headroom with 4-6 references each.

►► **THE REAL LESSON, and it is the opposite of the VM1 one.** `ld iy,(ix+d)`,
`ld iy,(hl)`, `ld iy,(sp+n)` and `ld hl,(iy+d)` ALL ASSEMBLE ON EVERY CPU —
z80asm silently synthesises the missing ones at 2-4x the size. A missing CPU
gate is NOT a build error, it is a quiet size regression. Contrast the VM1's
`ld a,(hl'+d)`, which is a hard syntax error. Gate every index-pair memory form
on the CPUs that really have it and CHECK THE BYTE COUNT with
`z80asm -m<cpu> -b`; do not trust the assembler to refuse.

►► **THE DEAR-SLOT GATE WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED.** The precedent a few lines
away in unified_arbitrate — `deref_gap >= 15`, "the yield only pays where a
deref-base's BC-exclusive `ld a,(bc)` beats a DEAR slot deref" — would exclude
ez80, kc160 and rabbit. It gives up bitfieldbench ez80 sp (-53 B / -6.47 %),
structbench ez80 fp (-11.53 %), ptrbench r2ka/r4k (-5.3 % each), ptrbench kc160
(-14/-15 B) and the whole kc160 recordbench win. **The cheap-slot CPUs are where
this change earns MOST, not least.** Leave the term uniform.

►► **LOWERING TIP FOR THE FILL COST (maintainer, 13/9): ez80 has
`ld iy,(ix+d)`.** Verified by assembling — and it is better than it looks:

    ld iy,(ix+6)   ez80 3B   kc160 3B   | z80 12B  z180 12B  r4k 14B  <- SYNTHETIC
    ld (ix+6),iy   ez80 3B   kc160 3B   | z80 12B  z180 12B  r4k 14B  <- SYNTHETIC
    ld iy,(hl)     ez80 2B              | everything else 9B          <- SYNTHETIC

So on ez80 AND kc160 an index home can be FILLED from, and SPILLED to, an fp
frame slot in ONE 3-byte instruction, against the `ld hl,d; add hl,sp; ld hl,(hl);
push hl; pop iy` the lowerer emits today. That is precisely the missing setup
cost, on precisely the two CPUs where it bites — so the right fix is a LOWERING
rung, not a cost-model patch.
►► **BUT THE SYNTHETIC IS A FOOTGUN.** z80asm ACCEPTS all three forms on every
CPU and silently expands them to 12-14 bytes where the hardware lacks them. A
rung that emits `ld iy,(ix+d)` without a CPU gate would assemble clean and be a
large SIZE regression on z80/z180/rabbit with nothing to show for it. Gate on
IS_EZ80() || IS_KC160() and assert the byte count.

REAL FILES (`code_compiler`, z80n, both frame modes): emu.c, adv_a and clisp
are **BYTE-IDENTICAL**. An index home needs a CALL-FREE function and those
files are call-heavy, so the whole win sits in the bench corpus. Do not claim a
real-file gain for this.

GATE-OFF IS BYTE-IDENTICAL: `--opt-disable=idx-deref,deref-offset` reproduces
the pre-change compiler across 348 asm files (28 benches x 6 CPUs x sp/fp),
diffed against a reference binary built from `d541a1a469`. The cost term is
gated on `idx-deref` too, so switching the rung off restores the old
ALLOCATION as well as the old codegen.

►► **THE VM1 TRAP, and why the guard is a PhysReg test.** `ir_idx2_reg` returns
IR_PR_HL_ALT on the KR580VM1 — h'l' is a full-pair index home for allocation
purposes — and `idx_pr_name` spells it `hl'`. The obvious guard
(`if (!idx_pr_name(pr)) return NULL;`) therefore ADMITS it, and `ld a,(hl'+0)`
is not an instruction. idx_deref_reg tests the PhysReg instead:
`if (pr != IR_PR_IX && pr != IR_PR_IY) return NULL;`
Verified by breaking it. With the name test in place of the PhysReg test the
corpus does not change — but only because unified_arbitrate SEPARATELY refuses
a PARAMETER the h'l' home, and IR_IDX2BASE only admits a deref base that is a
read-only param, so the two exclusions compose by accident. Remove BOTH and the
leak is immediate: 18 displaced forms across bitfieldbench and ptrbench
(`ld l,(hl'+0)`, `ld h,(hl'+2)`, `ld l,(hl'+3)`), and z80asm rejects every one
of them — `error: syntax error ^---- ld a,(hl'+0)`, no binary. A leak is LOUD,
at every displacement including zero (`%+d` prints `+0`). Restoring only the
rung's guard, with the arbiter exclusion still off, gives zero displaced forms
and a clean passing vm1 binary.
►► So on the VM1 the PhysReg test is the SOLE line of defence. The fold's
`IS_808x()` exclusion does NOT help: the offsets in that leak came from
ir_opt_lea_offset and the frontend, not from ir_opt_deref_offset.

FAILURES BY COLUMN: 80cc-fp 0, 80cc-sp 0, sccz80 0, xcc -Os 1, xcc -Of 1,
sdcc 46 — identical to the s4 table, so the non-80cc columns reproduced exactly.

►► **THE s4 TABLE IS NOT THE BASELINE FOR THIS CHANGE.** It was taken at
`57885673e1`; `IR_IDX2BASE` (`d541a1a469`) landed in between and moved cells of
its own. Diffing the two tables would credit its wins here. Every delta above is
gate-off vs gate-on with ONE compiler, which is the only honest attribution; the
table below is the fresh ABSOLUTE state.

GATES (re-run with the revisit in). long_ir **725/725 in BOTH frame modes** (721 + the 4 new idxderef
targets); the one make error in each run is the pre-existing `mbf32_vm1.lib`
missing-product gap, not this change. enigma RXSEC sp+fp. emu.c `On The Path`
x2 sp+fp. No aborts: 464/464 size cells and 348/348 asm files, none empty.

`long_ir/idxderef.c` is the regression test, PROVED against three deliberately
broken builds: a wrong word high displacement fails at bf_get, a missing
displacement-range guard fails at far_get, and a missing def-count gate in the
fold fails at hoisted_base. ►► TWO GUARDS ARE NOT COVERED AND SAY SO: the
rung's post_step rejection (unreachable while IDX2_BASE_STEPPED refuses a
stepped base an index home) and the VM1 PhysReg test (unreachable without also
breaking the arbiter). Both were verified inert by removal. Whoever lifts
either exclusion must re-prove them.

►► MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE, learned the hard way twice this session. Two matrix
runs and one long_ir fp run were VOIDED because a background scan was still
swapping `bin/z88dk-80cc` after it looked stopped. `nohup ... &` survives a
task being marked complete. Do all compiler-swapping work FIRST, then run the
long measurement with nothing else in flight, and check `md5sum bin/z88dk-80cc`
before believing a number. This is the `AGENTS.md` "don't swap bin/ mid-loop"
rule in a new form.

`IR_*` opt-out that is byte-identical to the pre-change compiler.

  `IR_SLOTADDR` (7cff0f3a92) — the sp-mode slot-address cache existed only for
  BYTE accesses. The word load/store paths recomputed `ld hl,nn; add hl,sp`
  (4 B) even when HL already pointed a byte or two away, and threw the address
  away after, although a two-byte walk provably leaves HL on the slot's HIGH
  byte. Widened to consume and to publish.

  `IR_SHRMASK` (561e988822) — a right shift whose result is masked back inside
  a byte narrows even when the SOURCE does not fit a byte. Three pieces: the
  mask proof; lowering it as a ROTATE (`rrca`/`rlca` x min(n,8-n), no clean-up
  mask, cheaper in bytes AND cycles); and the straddling case via the top-byte
  identity `(x>>n)&M == high byte of (x<<(8-n))`, which is `add hl,hl` x (8-n)
  and needs no scratch register. ►► 808x gains most: it has no CB page, so it
  was excluded outright — but it CALLS `l_asr_u`, a runtime loop (41 such calls
  in the corpus, ZERO on z80), and `rrca`/`rlca` are base-page.

  `57885673e1` — the miscompile the two above shipped with; see below.

RESULT over the 80cc columns: **133 cells changed across 23 of 30 benches and
all 11 CPUs, -753 B sp / -292 B fp, ZERO cells larger.** Ticks 99 cells faster,
**0 slower**, -0.245 % aggregate; bitfieldbench on 8080 and vm1 is -8.5 %, which
is the `l_asr_u` call being removed. `code_compiler` corpus, gates off -> on:
z80 -103, 8080 -84, 8085 -16, gbz80 -59, ez80 -112, z180 -103; 0 larger.

FAILURES BY COLUMN: 80cc-sp 0, 80cc-fp 0, sccz80 0, xcc -Os 1, xcc -Of 1,
sdcc 46 (ez80 BUILD on every bench, gbz80 and z80n WRONG on several). The sdcc
gaps are sdcc's own and are recorded rather than skipped so they stay visible.
Every sccz80/xcc/sdcc cell reproduced EXACTLY across three separate full runs.

►► **REGENERATING THIS TABLE FOUND A MISCOMPILE.** `IR_SLOTADDR` published an
address belief that could outlive the HL it described — a caller's
`push hl ... pop hl` preserve region, or an `ex de,hl`, destroys the address and
left the belief behind, which then rode the cross-BB carry into a branch target
as an `inc/dec hl` walk from a garbage base. It showed here as three WRONG cells
on vm1 (maskbench, queenbench, searchbench) and NOWHERE ELSE: `long_ir` passed
**716/716 in BOTH frame modes** with it present and the z80 corpus was
byte-clean. It reproduces on z80, 8080, z180 and rabbit too — vm1 is merely
where the corpus happened to hold the shape. Fixed at `57885673e1` (cost: 0 B).
vm1 was a coverage hole: absent from `corpus_sizescan.sh` (now added) and its
only long_ir target cannot build (`mbf32_vm1.lib` has never been built — that
is a missing library PRODUCT, not "vm1 has no assembler" as earlier notes say).
`long_ir/slotaddr.c` now carries the reduced shape with a vm1 variant.

REAL FILES, `code_compiler` only, measured with BOTH compilers built from
source (base = `3eb2fb8d16`, the 12/9 HEAD):

  clisp  sp 12972 -> 12971      fp 12862 -> 12862
  adv_a  sp  2828 ->  2828      fp  2827 ->  2827

►► **CORRECTION.** The 12/9 table recorded `clisp sp 14040 -> 11879 (-15.4 %)`.
Neither figure reproduces: that commit's own compiler gives **12972**, and no
combination of `IR_TAILMERGE` / `IR_BLAYOUT` / `IR_JR` yields 14040 or 11879.
Treat the old real-file line as unsound. These two changes move clisp by 1 byte
and adv_a by 0 — those files hold few masked bitfield shifts or sp-mode word
slot accesses, and the corpus gains do not carry over to them.

`emu.c` is NOT in this tree, so its rows in the 12/9 table could not be
re-measured and are deliberately not carried forward.

================================================================================
12/9/2026 (s32-35) — FULL MATRIX at HEAD `3eb2fb8d16`. **330 rows, 30 benches x
            11 CPUs.** vm1 and md5 were both MISSING and are now in.
================================================================================
Generator: test/suites/gen_bench_matrix3.py (run it — the absolute source paths
are load-bearing, 30 B through __FILE__ in the framework's assert strings).
Cells are `bytes / ticks(millions)` of the whole -create-app binary.
sccz80 runs on every CPU; xcc is a z80-only toolchain so its columns stay z80.

►► TWO GAPS FIXED IN THE GENERATOR, both of which had been silently narrowing
this table:
  - **vm1 was not in the CPU list.** It builds and ticks cleanly for 80cc and
    sccz80 (30/30 benches); only sdcc has no vm1 port, so that column reads `—`.
    Added to NO_IX too: vm1's index home is the RS-prefixed h'l', not IX/IY, so
    -fframe-pointer is a no-op there exactly as on 8080/8085/gbz80.
  - **md5 was not in BENCHES** — and adding it naively would have reported a
    FALSE `WRONG` on every cell. `md5sum.c` does `MDFile("md5test.bin")`, an
    open() relative to the CWD, and the generator ran binaries from test/suites.
    The run now happens in the BENCH directory (`cwd=`), which is the same fix
    corpus_tickscan.sh already carries. md5 matters: it is where 80cc's inlined
    32-bit arithmetic beats sdcc 17461 vs 29359 on z80, and it is the single row
    that pulls the corpus TOTAL below 1.0x while the median sits at ~1.17x.

80cc columns are the DEFAULT configuration at HEAD: tail merging (`220fa681f5`)
and block layout (`cc19e1194b`) both default-on, plus the label reuse
(`b265f13a65`), the gbz80 SLOT+BC cost row and `[home-rearb]` (`3eb2fb8d16`).
Against the previous table (tail merging only): -7279 B over the 80cc columns,
ZERO cells larger.

FAILURES BY COLUMN: 80cc-sp 0, 80cc-fp 0, sccz80 0, xcc -Os 1, xcc -Of 1,
sdcc 46 (ez80 BUILD on every bench, gbz80 and z80n WRONG on several). The sdcc
gaps are sdcc's own and are recorded rather than skipped so they stay visible.

REAL FILES at HEAD, `code_compiler` only (gates off -> default):
  clisp  sp 14040 -> 11879  (-15.4 %)     fp 13603 -> 11799  (-13.3 %)
  emu.c  sp 23233 -> 21662  ( -6.8 %)     fp 22746 -> 21100  ( -7.2 %)

12/9/2026 (s28) — A SECOND STRUCTURAL GAP, same family: **TAIL MERGING /
            CROSS-JUMPING**. 80cc duplicates block tails 1.8-4.2x more than clang
            (clisp 29.2 % vs 6.9 %). ~600 B on clisp (4 %). NO evidence of an
            "algorithm rewrite" gap — that was checked and is clean.
================================================================================
WHAT WAS CHECKED FOR ALGORITHM-LEVEL REWRITING, and found EVEN or 80cc-favourable:
    block-copy idiom (ldir/lddr)  80cc 5 in emu | clang 2 clisp + 1 ptrbench — a wash
    machine outlining             ZERO in both
    loop unrolling                no evidence (clang's instruction count is HIGHER)
    multiply/divide               80cc inlines (0 helper calls); clang calls 5-6
  So the gap is NOT algorithmic. It is CFG SHAPE.

DUPLICATED 4-INSTRUCTION BLOCK TAILS (cross-jumping opportunity):
    emu      80cc 121 (11.8 %)   clang 68 ( 6.4 %)
    clisp    80cc 139 (29.2 %)   clang 35 ( 6.9 %)   <- 4.2x
    enigma   80cc   1 ( 1.4 %)   clang  0

THE ACTUAL DUPLICATES IN clisp, and they are very concrete:
    x40:  pop bc / push de / push hl / jp L_f16_bb_21
    x34:  ld d,a / ld sp,ix / pop ix / ret
    x31:  ld de,65535 / ld sp,ix / pop ix / ret

  - REPEATED EPILOGUES: a function with several `return` statements emits
    `ld sp,ix / pop ix / ret` (5 B) at EVERY exit. One merged epilogue costs a 3 B
    `jp` and saves 2 B per site; 71 sites in clisp alone.
  - THE x40 CASE IS NEARLY FREE: forty blocks do the identical 3-instruction shuffle
    AND ALREADY JUMP TO THE SAME LABEL. Retarget the existing jump to a point before
    the shuffle — 3 instructions saved per site at ZERO cost, ~117 B.

  ~139 merges x ~3 instructions net = **~600 B on clisp (4 %)**, the same league as
  the block-layout finding (s27).

►► THE TWO STRUCTURAL GAPS TOGETHER ARE THE SESSION'S BEST LEADS:
     1. block layout / loop rotation   2.7-9.6x more unconditional jumps (~570 B emu)
     2. tail merging / cross-jumping   1.8-4.2x more duplicated tails   (~600 B clisp)
   Both are SIZE optimisations — exactly where 80cc's deficit is. Both are PURE CFG
   transformations: no allocator change, no lowering-contract change. They compose
   with each other and with the existing branch_relax (merge, lay out, then jp->jr).
   Contrast every architectural project declined this session.

CAVEAT AS EVER: both counts are UPPER bounds. A duplicated tail is only mergeable if
the predecessors agree on live-out state, and some unconditional jumps are
unavoidable. Probe the recoverable subset before building.

12/9/2026 (s27) — ►►► THE BEST LEAD OF THE SESSION, and it is STRUCTURAL, not
            instruction selection: **80cc has NO BLOCK-LAYOUT / LOOP-ROTATION PASS.**
            It emits 2.7-9.6x more UNCONDITIONAL jumps than clang. Worth ~1-4 % of
            code size — an order of magnitude more than anything else found today.
================================================================================
The maintainer's point: clang STRUCTURALLY REWRITES the code; the instruction-mix
censuses (s24-s26) could never see it. Measured on the CFG instead (comments
stripped first — clang labels its blocks `BB0_1:  ; %for_cond`, which defeats any
end-of-line regex; FOURTH format trap of the session):

  unconditional jumps per 1000 instructions
      enigma   80cc 36.5   clang  3.8    **9.6x**
      emu      80cc 44.0   clang 16.3    2.7x
      clisp    80cc 26.8   clang 18.3    1.5x

An unconditional jump is PURE OVERHEAD — it exists only because the block layout
does not let control fall through.

►► THE MECHANISM, confirmed by counting loop shapes:
      loops closed by an UNCONDITIONAL back-jump:  80cc **11**, clang **1**
      of those, test-at-top (unrotated):           80cc 5,      clang 0
   **80cc leaves loops as "test at top + unconditional jump back"; clang ROTATES
   them** so the conditional branch closes the loop and no unconditional jump is
   needed. That is loop rotation/inversion plus block placement for fallthrough.

►► AND 80cc HAS NO SUCH PASS. It has `ir_opt_prune_unreachable` (CFG cleanup) and
   `branch_relax` (jp->jr, which SHORTENS jumps but never removes them).
   `close_bb_with_fallthrough` (ir_build.c:75) is CFG CONSTRUCTION, not layout.

SIZED (excess unconditional jumps vs clang, at ~2.5 B each):
      enigma  +21 jumps  ~ +53 B on 1316   (4 %)
      emu     +228       ~ +570 B on 22816 (2.5 %)
      clisp   +57        ~ +143 B on 13603 (1 %)
   Compare with everything else found today: djnz ~24 B; the cost-table grounding
   -74 B. This is an ORDER OF MAGNITUDE larger.

►► WHY IT IS ALSO THE RIGHT SHAPE OF WORK. It is a pure CFG transformation: no
   allocator change, no lowering-contract change, and it COMPOSES with the existing
   branch_relax (rotate first, then jp->jr the survivors). Contrast the three
   architectural projects declined today (colouring, split-pair allocation, bus
   replacement), all of which needed to re-implement invariants.

HONEST CAVEAT: the excess-jump count is an UPPER bound on the win — some
unconditional jumps are unavoidable (switch dispatch, multi-exit loops, shared
epilogues). Probe the recoverable subset before committing, as ever.

►► ONE FACT EXPLAINS THE WHOLE SPREAD. clang lowers 32-bit operations to CALLS;
   80cc does them inline through the DEHL accumulator. Where there is no long

►► THIS RECALIBRATES EARLIER CLAIMS, INCLUDING TODAY'S. "80cc is 13-31 % smaller
   than an LLVM compiler" is really "80cc's long handling is strong". The same
   reading applies to md5 at 0.64x vs sdcc (a 32-bit CRC) and crcbench being 17 %
   faster (32-bit). **80cc's distinctive strength is 32-bit arithmetic** — exactly
   what this codebase has invested in (DEHL accumulator, ir_opt_insert_long_pushes,
   the long stack parks). Its diffuse ~19 % deficit vs sdcc is in int/byte code.

►► THE ONE GAP THAT HOLDS AT SCALE — ZERO-EXTENSION, per 1000 instructions:

►► THE WRONG GATE (genuine, independent of the measurement):
     ir_alloc.c:465   halves_ok = (c_cpu == CPU_Z80 || IS_Z80N());   /* NOT z180 */
   and ir_lower_ops.inc.c:667 justifies it with
     "ez80/kc160/rabbit/z180 — no usable index-half byte access"
   **That is FALSE for eZ80.** The index half registers are documented there,
   z88dk-z80asm assembles them for -mez80_z80 (`ld a,iyl` -> fd 7d, `ld iyl,e` ->

   exists and was not found. The gate is wrong; fixing it is NECESSARY BUT NOT
   SUFFICIENT. Reverted, nothing kept.

   ALSO NOTE, against the obvious theory: on z80-sp 80cc DOES use 10 index halves
   and STILL emits 22 zero-extends — the same count as ez80 with none. So index
   halves are NOT what lets clang avoid widening. The zero-extend gap is a separate,
   unexplained phenomenon and is the best remaining lead from this comparison.

NORMALISED against the 1.13x overall instruction ratio (80cc 11178, sdcc 9900 over

►► THE sbc hl SIGNAL IS NOT A LEVER. Sampling the sites: a pointer-bound check
   (`ld de,_mat+512 ... sbc hl,de`) and an `== -32768` overflow guard. Legitimate
   16-bit compares, not bad lowering.

►► AND THE UNIFYING THEORY WAS BACKWARDS. Hypothesis: 80cc tests loop termination by
   COMPARING where sdcc decrements to zero, which would tie sbc-hl to the djnz gap
   (s23). MEASURED, it is the reverse:
       80cc  compare-driven loops:   0 % (ptrbench, matrixbench, localbench, widthbench)
       sdcc  compare-driven loops:  78-100 %
   **80cc already terminates loops by decrement everywhere; sdcc keeps `i < n`.**
   80cc is AHEAD here. It also resolves sbc-hl the other way: sdcc is compare-driven
   but compares in 8 BITS (`cp`), while 80cc's 16-bit compares arise elsewhere.

►► METHOD, AND IT IS THE SECOND TIME TODAY. The first pass of this census reported
   "zero-extend: 80cc 103, sdcc 0" and "constants: 7.25x". Both were SPELLING
   artifacts — **sdcc writes `ld b,0x00`, 80cc writes `ld b,0`**. Corrected, the
   zero-extends are 103 vs 106 (identical) and constants 1.96x not 7.25x. The
   maintainer caught this same class of error earlier (s18, longhand `ld l,(ix+d)`).
   ANY cross-compiler scan must accept decimal OR hex and optional spaces from the
   start; the matcher in /tmp/redun2.py does.

NEXT AT THIS LEVEL (unexamined, no claim made): `ex de,hl` at 1.84x is HL-bus
shuffling and the one place the bus hypothesis might still have substance;
constant->pair at 1.74x may be deliberate rematerialisation (cheap) or a CSE gap.
