12/9/2026 (s23) — NOT A CEILING, BUT A GRIND. First look OUTSIDE the allocator found
            a real unexploited instruction in seconds — **djnz: 80cc 3, sdcc 15** —
            worth ~12-36 B. Small, which is exactly what "the gap is DIFFUSE"
            predicts. The remaining path is many small wins, not one big one.
================================================================================
THE FINDING: `djnz` needs its counter in **B**, and IR_PR_B is assigned at ZERO
sites (s21) — so the z80's dedicated loop instruction is structurally unavailable.
Meanwhile ast_opt ALREADY detects the shape: `int width8 = (info.trip_count <= 255)`
(ast_opt.c:4400) types the countdown counter `uchar`. And **58 of 73 resolvable
loops (79 %) have trip <= 255**, so candidates are everywhere.

The worst emitted form, matrixbench:
    ld l,(ix-12) / ld h,0 / dec hl / ld (ix-8),hl      ~11 B + a separate test
against `djnz L` at 2 B. The chain is: ast_opt makes an 8-bit counter -> the
allocator never homes anything in B -> it spills -> the lowerer WIDENS it back to
16 bits to decrement it.

►► BUT SIZED HONESTLY IT IS SMALL. That widened-decrement form occurs **3 times
   corpus-wide**, not 58 — most countdown tails already decrement efficiently. The
   gap is 12 missing djnz sites at ~1-3 B each = **~12-36 B**. An extrapolation from
   the one ugly example would have claimed hundreds; the corpus says tens.

►► WHY THIS ENTRY MATTERS MORE THAN ITS 24 BYTES. It is the first thing measured
   OUTSIDE the allocator all session, it took seconds to find, and it is REAL. So
   the s22 ceiling conclusion needs narrowing:
     - the ALLOCATOR is near its ceiling (8 levers, all measured out);
     - the COMPILER is not — unexploited instruction-selection gaps exist;
     - but each is worth TENS of bytes, so closing 19 % means finding ~50 of them.

   Also unexploited, already sized and set aside: **rrd/rld — 80cc emits ZERO,
   sdcc 4** (nibble-aligned bitfields; narrow, fails the one-bench rule).

►► THE MODE THAT FITS THE EVIDENCE: a standing, repeatable hunt — "what does sdcc
   emit that 80cc never does, and how often" — rather than another architectural
   project. Cheap, and it hit on the first attempt. Contrast today's architectural
   arcs (colouring, split-pair allocation, bus replacement), all declined on
   measurement.

================================================================================
12/9/2026 (s22) — ►► CORRECTION TO s21: "BC/DE are consumed STAGING for the HL bus"
            does NOT hold as a differentiator. sdcc stages the SAME share (27-38 %
            vs 80cc's 27-41 %). The gap is DIFFUSE — ~19 % more instructions spread
            across every category — not a structural excess with a lever.
================================================================================
s21 observed ptrbench `init_data` using bc/b/c 14 times as SCRATCH while no vreg was
homed there, and generalised that into "the HL-bus architecture is the root cause".
MEASURED PROPERLY, it is not:

  bench           80cc staging   sdcc staging   80cc instrs   sdcc instrs
  ptrbench           41.0 %         38.4 %          852           714
  structbench        28.3 %       **32.4 %**        205           182
  matrixbench        27.1 %         26.7 %          373           333
  bitfieldbench      34.5 %         30.7 %          624           430
  localbench         32.7 %         31.7 %          508           436
  widthbench         27.5 %         27.1 %          425           358

  (staging = register-to-register moves + push/pop + ex de,hl — shuffling that
   computes nothing. structbench: sdcc stages MORE than 80cc.)

**Register shuffling is a z80 tax BOTH compilers pay at the same rate.** What 80cc
actually does is emit MORE OF EVERYTHING: ptrbench +138 instructions (+19 %), of
which staging +75, memory +35, compute -11. Compute DENSITY is lower (22.8 % vs
28.7 %) and memory is over-represented, but nothing is structurally out of
proportion.

►► CONSEQUENCE FOR "WHAT REPLACES THE HL BUS". The textbook alternative is
   INSTRUCTION SELECTION WITH REGISTER CONSTRAINTS — each op declares which
   registers it may take operands in, and the selector picks an encoding from where
   the values already are, instead of normalising through HL. On z80 that would
   exploit: byte ALU ops are **A-centric** with a free second operand (`and r`,
   `xor r`), moves are any-to-any, `inc bc` needs no bus. Only 16-bit ARITHMETIC is
   genuinely HL-bound (`add hl,rr`).

   **DO NOT BUILD IT on current evidence.** It is a rewrite of ir_lower* (~20k lines,
   2.5x the colourer's scope) to recover a tax sdcc pays too.

THE CEILING STANDS, WITH THE REASON CORRECTED: not "the HL bus is wrong" but "the
remaining ~19 % is spread thinly across everything". That is why every lever this
session measured out near zero — there is no concentrated mechanism left to find.

================================================================================
12/9/2026 (s21) — SPLIT-PAIR BYTE ALLOCATION: REFUTED BY ITS OWN PHASE 0, and the
            root cause is not pair granularity at all — **BC/DE are consumed as
            STAGING for the HL bus**, not wasted on half-empty pairs. Probe written,
            measured, reverted; no code kept.
================================================================================
THE PROPOSAL WAS: a word value can live in two INDEPENDENTLY allocated byte
registers and be assembled on demand — `ld l,c; ld h,b` is 8 cyc / 2 B against a
measured 38 cyc / 6 B for an fp slot read, so 4.75x. IR_PR_B and IR_PR_D already
exist in the enum and the LOWERER already handles them (clobber masks, residency
checks); only the allocator never emits them. Phases: 0 probe, 1 enable B/D as byte
homes, 2 split word home, 3 half-granular spilling.

PHASE 0, MEASURED (30 benches + clisp, 216 functions):

  1. SECOND BYTE CANDIDATE — never. **0 refusals** corpus-wide at the byte arm's
     `if (byte_reg) continue`. No function has a second byte candidate to place, so
     **PHASE 1 HAS NOTHING TO DO** (this reproduces `pair-allocator-no-opportunity`).

  2. HALF-PAIR FRAGMENTATION — none. **0 functions** have 2+ free halves without a
     whole pair also free. There is no fragmentation for a split home to recover,
     so **PHASE 2 HAS NOTHING TO RECOVER** either.

  3. What the probe DID show: 38 of 216 functions had "a whole pair free" while 202
     word values sat in slots — worst ptrbench `init_data`, 34 spilled words, 36
     candidates PROPOSED, BC showing entirely free.

►► AND (3) WAS MY OWN ARTIFACT. The probe equated "no vreg HOMED in BC" with "BC is
   available". It is not. init_data is CALL-FREE and still uses bc/b/c **14 times**
   in its body — `ld bc,0`, `inc bc`, `add hl,bc`, `ld a,b`. **BC is carrying SCRATCH
   traffic for the HL bus.** The 36 candidates were declined because their ranges
   cross the lowerer's own BC clobbers, which `vreg_reg_clean` correctly tests. The
   pair was never free.

►► THE ROOT CAUSE, RESTATED. 80cc keeps fewer values in registers not because pairs
   are half-wasted (measured: they are not) but because **BC/DE are spent STAGING for
   the HL-bus model** (ADR 0002/0003: "the lowerer never asks for a scratch register
   — fixed per-op roles, Bus = HL/A, Parking = BC/DE/IX/IY"). sdcc needs less staging
   because it computes in more places. That is a LOWERING-ARCHITECTURE property, and
   changing it is far larger than either the colourer (declined at 1.5 % code) or
   this register-model proposal.

CONCLUSION FOR THE ARC: the +0.86 frame-traffic correlation (s19) is real and
correctly identifies the symptom, but all FIVE candidate mechanisms are now measured
out — redundant reloads (1 in 1260), byte-narrowing (1.2 %), loop-invariant hoisting
(needs a free register there isn't), allocation selection/proposal (66.7 % / 60.7 %,
colouring declined), and register-model granularity (this entry). **80cc is at its
practical ceiling under the HL-bus architecture.**

================================================================================
12/9/2026 (s20) — REFUTED BEFORE BUILDING: fusing the bit-test with the shift that
            produces it (the CRC idiom). The shape occurs TWICE in the corpus + all
            four real files, and BOTH are CRC. Worth ~73 B. Do not build it.
================================================================================
THE IDEA (maintainer's, with the reservation that it looked benchmark-specific): in
`crc = (crc & 1) ? ((crc >> 1) ^ POLY) : (crc >> 1)` the shift ALREADY drops the
tested bit into CARRY, so the test is free — shift first (`srl d; rr e; rr h; rr l`)
and branch on carry. The general name for it is condition-code forwarding, which is
NOT benchmark-specific in principle.

MEASURED across all 30 benches + clisp + adv_a + enigma + emu.c, both directions
(`&1` near `>>1`, `&0x8000`/`&0x80` near `<<1`):

    crcbench   8x   crc = (crc & 1UL)    ? ((crc >> 1) ^ 0xEDB88320UL) : (crc >> 1)
    intbench   8x   crc = (crc & 0x8000U)? ((crc << 1) ^ 0x1021U)      : (crc << 1)
    everything else: ZERO

Two sites, both CRC (CRC-32 and CRC-16-CCITT). Not merely benchmark-specific — CRC-
specific in this corpus.

AND THE UPSIDE IS SMALL WHERE IT LANDS. 80cc already beats sdcc on crcbench by 17 %
on TICKS (114.6M vs 138.6M), so the win there is SIZE only (~56 B of an 861/805
comparison); intbench is already 1.03x (17 B). **~73 B total, across two instances of
one idiom** — it fails the one-bench rule in spirit.

CARRY FORWARD: the narrow form (a tested bit that a neighbouring shift shifts out) is
refuted by frequency. The BROADER family — branch on the flag an operation already
set rather than recomputing the predicate, e.g. testing for zero after an op that
sets Z — was NOT measured here and is a PEEPHOLE question, not an IR one. Probe it
before believing in it; nothing in the current evidence promotes it above frame
traffic (s19, correlation +0.86).

================================================================================
12/9/2026 (s19) — FRAME TRAFFIC IS THE GAP: correlation **+0.86** across 29 benches
            between how much worse 80cc is and how much more it touches the frame.
            AND a correction: crcbench's stack parking is NOT a defect — it buys
            17 % speed for 56 bytes. Scanner kept: src/80cc/frame_traffic.py
================================================================================
MEASURED (emitted BYTES, longhand `ld l,(ix+d)`/`ld h,(ix+d+1)` pairs folded back
into one word access first — see s18; comparing by SPELLING measures the assembler):

  bench           ratio    gap B   extra frame B   frame as % of gap
  bitfieldbench    1.66      437        +165              38 %
  widthbench       1.40      250        +183              73 %
  localbench       1.37      281        +123              44 %
  matrixbench      1.37      217        +210              97 %
  ptrbench         1.33      384        +201              52 %
  structbench      1.32       97         +69              71 %
  ...
  switchbench      0.59     -637        -426                -
  recordbench      0.90      -49        -126                -
  shiftbench       0.95      -49        -168                -

►► THE SIGN FLIPS WITH THE OUTCOME. Every bench 80cc WINS touches the frame LESS
   than sdcc; every bench it loses badly touches it MORE. Aggregated over the 26
   benches where 80cc is larger, extra frame traffic is **36 % of the total gap**;
   over the 12 worst, **55 %**; excluding crcbench, **45 %**.
   **correlation(size ratio, extra frame bytes) = +0.86 over 29 benches.**

►► CORRECTION — crcbench is NOT a second disease (it was called one in s5 and s19
   draft). Measured on z80:
       80cc-fp  861 B   114.6M ticks
       sdcc     805 B   138.6M ticks
   **80cc is 17 % FASTER for 56 bytes.** The stack parking (`push de; push hl;
   srl d; rr e; rr h`) is a deliberate, profitable byte-for-cycle trade, and
   crcbench appears as a "loss" only because the 4-way table ranks on SIZE. Do not
   chase it. It is the corpus's clearest reminder that a size ratio alone
   misclassifies a good trade as a defect.

CONSEQUENCE: with crcbench reclassified, the frame-traffic story has no significant
counter-example left, and it is the ONLY lever measured this session that correlates
with the actual deficit rather than with a model number that refuses to translate.
The specific shape (s18): on ptrbench, entirely `int`, sdcc makes **4** word frame
accesses to 80cc's **51**, plus 28 GENUINE single-byte ones — it splits 16-bit values
and spills halves independently. That is where the work is, and it is upstream of
allocation, which is the second independent reason the colouring arc was right to close.

================================================================================
12/9/2026 (s18) — ►► CORRECTION TO THE "sdcc EMITS ZERO WORD FRAME ACCESSES" CLAIM
            (s5, s9, s17). It was a SYNTAX ARTIFACT — but re-measured properly the
            conclusion STANDS and is stronger: sdcc makes 4 word frame accesses on
            ptrbench against 80cc's 51, plus 28 GENUINE single-byte ones.
================================================================================
THE ERROR (maintainer's correction): sdcc does not write `ld hl,(ix+d)`. It writes
`ld l,(ix+d)` / `ld h,(ix+d+1)` LONGHAND. 80cc writes the z80asm SYNTHETIC
`ld hl,(ix+d)`, which assembles to exactly those two instructions. My scan
classified by SYNTAX — anything `ld <byte-reg>,(ix+d)` counted as a byte access — so
every sdcc word load was counted as two byte accesses and "sdcc emits ZERO word
frame accesses" was true by spelling, not by behaviour.

►► THE BYTE TOTALS WERE NEVER WRONG. Both spellings cost 3 B per prefixed access, so
the "frame traffic in bytes" figures (s5: 80cc 345 B vs sdcc 108 B on ptrbench) were
right all along. Only the WORD/BYTE ATTRIBUTION was wrong, and with it the claim
about granularity — which was the whole basis for the "byte-centric vs pair-centric"
reading.

RE-MEASURED, pairing adjacent `ld l,(ix+d)`/`ld h,(ix+d+1)` (and the de/bc forms,
and the store direction) back into ONE word access before counting:

  bench           80cc                       sdcc
  ptrbench        word=51 byte=1  = 309 B    word=4  byte=28 = 108 B
  structbench     word=14 byte=7  = 105 B    word=0  byte=12 =  36 B
  bitfieldbench   word=36 byte=7  = 237 B    word=4  byte=16 =  72 B
  strbench        word=36 byte=8  = 240 B    word=17 byte=21 = 165 B
  crcbench        word=7  byte=10 =  72 B    word=23 byte=62 = 324 B
  queenbench      word=4  byte=8  =  48 B    word=5  byte=8  =  54 B

►► THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES AND IS BETTER EVIDENCED. On ptrbench — which is entirely
`int` — sdcc makes **4** word frame accesses to 80cc's **51**, and **28 genuine
single-byte** ones. It is splitting 16-bit values and spilling/reloading HALVES
independently. That is byte-granular allocation, now measured by behaviour instead
of by spelling. structbench (0 vs 14) and bitfieldbench (4 vs 36) say the same.
crcbench is the counter-example and was already known: sdcc spends MORE frame
traffic there and is still smaller, because 80cc parks pairs on the stack instead.

METHOD, and it is the third time this session: **a measurement that keys on how a
compiler SPELLS an instruction measures the assembler, not the compiler.** The z80asm
synthetics (`ld hl,(ix+d)`, `ld hl,de`, `ld a,(hl+)`) make 80cc's output look denser
than sdcc's line-for-line. Normalise to EMITTED BYTES or to decoded instructions
before comparing anything across compilers.

================================================================================
12/9/2026 (s17) — ►► THE COLOURING ARC IS CLOSED. Reverted (761a549919) on the
            maintainer's arithmetic: 1221 retirable lines is 2 % of a 47534-line
            ir* codebase, ~500 come straight back in the colourer, so the trade is
            ~700 net lines (1.5 %) for rewriting the part of the compiler where a
            mistake is a SILENT WRONG ANSWER.
================================================================================
THE DECISION, and it is the right one on the evidence this file now carries:

  CODE:  retire 1221 lines (17 % of ir_alloc.c, 2 % of ir*) but RE-IMPLEMENT the
         invariants the dry run exposed — index prologue bookkeeping, the prepick
         snapshot protocol, and at least one more still unfound. Net ~700 lines.
  PERF:  four independent model improvements this session — grounded cycle costs,
         grounded byte costs, derived trip counts, and the colourer — each strictly
         more accurate, NONE moving bytes or ticks.
  RISK:  the reverted colourer still HUNG histbench fp with index placement off.

  A 1.5 % code reduction does not buy a rewrite of the allocator.

WHAT IS KEPT (the dry run's real output, worth more than its code):
  - an INDEX home is not a vreg_to_phys write — the function must save/restore that
    register in its prologue; 15 corpus miscompiles, bisected to exactly this;
  - occupancy must be SEEDED from vregs placed by EARLIER passes, or a new pass
    double-books a register another one owns;
  - `word_home_prepick` is a SNAPSHOT protocol (unified_arbitrate memcpy's the whole
    vreg_to_phys array after its loop), so a PRE-arbiter pass must assign directly
    and NOT via alloc_note_late_home, which is for LATE homes only.

►► WHERE THE EVIDENCE SAYS TO LOOK INSTEAD, and it was found early and never
   followed up: **sdcc emits ZERO word frame accesses anywhere** (s5). Frame traffic
   is 62-90 % of the gap on the four benches where 80cc loses to sdcc AND xcc AND
   sccz80 (structbench 90 %, strbench 81 %, ptrbench 62 %, bitfieldbench 46 %). That
   is the BYTE-CENTRIC vs PAIR-CENTRIC value model — an IR/lowering property, not an
   allocator selection property. The session was spent inside the allocator, which
   measurement says is not where the gap lives. PROBE IT FIRST; every plausible lever
   this session died on contact with measurement.

================================================================================
12/9/2026 (s16) — G2 DRY RUN: a cost-driven colourer over the existing pool, built
            and MISCOMPILED. 15 corpus cells vs 0 baseline; index homes were the
            cause (15 -> 1 when gated off); the residual HANGS. Opt-in IR_COLOUR,
            left defective on purpose. Commit 4341b92afb.
================================================================================
PURPOSE: the aim is to cut ir* code and special cases. Colouring retires the 11
realizability predicates + unified_arbitrate + the three packs = **1221 lines of
ir_alloc.c (17 %)** and ~42 allocation-policy switches. This calibrates what that
actually costs before committing to it.

BUILT (gate-off byte-identical): rank the existing pool by the best benefit any
allowed WORD class gives — BC charged the push/pop it forces per spanned call —
then greedily assign the best register free over the candidate's interval. Runs
BEFORE unified_arbitrate, which fills the rest (it already skips placed vregs and
its byte arm already scans for a BC tenant). Does two things the arbiter cannot:
index homes multi-occupant over disjoint intervals, and placement by COST rather
than by the fixed class priority order.

►► RESULT: 15 corpus cells FAILED their checksum, against ZERO in the baseline.

TWO PLAUSIBLE CAUSES FIXED THAT WERE **NOT** IT (both real bugs, worth keeping):
 1. Occupancy must be SEEDED from vregs placed by EARLIER passes (loop-ra, LRA).
    An empty map double-books a register another pass already owns.
 2. `alloc_note_late_home` must NOT be used from a pre-arbiter pass.
    `word_home_prepick` is a SNAPSHOT protocol — unified_arbitrate memcpy's the
    whole vreg_to_phys array after its loop as "the baseline the lowerer reverts
    to", so its own arms assign directly and only LATE homes (callsplit) use that
    helper.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE, found by bisecting with a placement cap (IR_COLOUR_MAX): the
SECOND placement, and it was an **INDEX** home. An index home is not just a
vreg_to_phys write — the function must SAVE/RESTORE that index register in its
prologue, and the arbiter's idx arms carry that bookkeeping. Gating index placement
off: **15 failures -> 1**.

RESIDUAL: histbench fp HANGS (24 G cycles, counter limit) rather than returning a
wrong answer, so at least one more invariant is unaccounted for. NOT chased — the
calibration question is already answered.

►► ►► WHAT IT CALIBRATES, and this is the deliverable. **The arbiter's 373 lines are
NOT all tuning.** They carry invariants the candidate POOL does not express:
prologue bookkeeping for index registers, the prepick snapshot protocol, and at
least one more. A colourer must RE-IMPLEMENT those, not inherit them. So the 1221
retirable lines are not 1221 lines of dead weight — some fraction is correctness
that has to be rebuilt inside the colourer, and the honest estimate of G2/G3 must
include it.

That is exactly why GRAPH_ALLOC_PLAN's "retire ONE predicate at a time, each gated
and gauntleted" is the right shape: every retirement has to rediscover which of its
conditions were correctness rather than heuristic. The dry run cost three build-
measure cycles to find ONE such invariant.

BEFORE THE MISCOMPILE WAS FOUND, the performance reading was: size +121 B (6 smaller,
15 larger), ticks 1 faster / 5 slower / aggregate +0.76 % — but that measurement is
VOID, taken on a build that miscompiled 15 cells.

================================================================================
11/9/2026 (s15) — ►► THE SIMPLIFICATION AIM CHANGES THE VERDICT ON COLOURING.
            Judged on size/speed the rewrite is marginal (measured, s11-s14). Judged
            on CODE it retires 1221 lines of ir_alloc.c (17 %) and subsumes ~42
            allocation-policy switches — AND it addresses BOTH halves of the benefit
            gap, which it does not on the performance axis.
================================================================================
THE AIM, stated by the maintainer: reduce the code and the special cases in ir*.
47534 lines across ir*.c/ir.h, and the gap against sdcc is ~19 % on codegen — a lot
of machinery for no quantum leap.

THE ACCUMULATION, counted:
    ir* overall        114 distinct env gates, 78 opt_disabled switches
    ir_alloc.c alone    46 env gates, 15 opt_disabled  => ~42 are ALLOCATION POLICY:
      bc-evict bc-pack byte-resident byte-tie de-home depth-weight graph-alloc
      idx2-counter iv-acc iv-resident iy-temp-pack loop-ra lra stack-spill
      word-resident | IR_BCCALLCOST IR_BCPERCAND IR_BC_STEP_PARAM IR_BYTETIE
      IR_BYTEPRESS IR_CALLSPLIT IR_CS_EVICT IR_IVACC IR_IVHOT IR_IYLONG IR_MWBC
      IR_MWBC_PRESSURE IR_OPRES IR_PREPUSH_NARROW IR_RANGED IR_TIGHT_HOMES IR_TRIPW ...
    Each is a separately-tuned placement policy patching the SAME mechanism.

WHAT A COLOURER RETIRES (G3/G4), measured by function span in ir_alloc.c:
    unified_arbitrate 373 | ir_bc_pack 144 | collect_home_candidates 137
    ir_iy_temp_pack 128 | ir_stack_spill 94 | ir_iy_reduction_pack 62
    home_realizable 53 | bc_home_realizable 53 | exx 32 | idx2 22 | idx3 21
    de_general 20 | de_operand 19 | de_acc 18 | iv 16 | byte 15 | de_ptr 14
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    **1221 lines = 17 % of ir_alloc.c**, against a colourer of perhaps 300-500.

►► AND THE POINT THAT ACTUALLY DECIDES IT. On the PERFORMANCE axis colouring
   addresses only the SELECTION half (+57956 of the +134738 headroom) and leaves
   ELIGIBILITY (+76782) untouched. On the CODE axis it addresses BOTH — because
   eligibility IS the 11 realizability predicates. There is no separate "widen
   eligibility" project once the predicates are gone; the colourer's interference
   graph decides admission. **Colouring is the better bet under the simplification
   aim than under the performance aim**, and that is the opposite of the conclusion
   reached in s14 when only bytes and ticks were being weighed.

THE BAR CHANGES WITH IT. Under a performance aim the rewrite must WIN; under a
simplification aim it must merely NOT REGRESS while deleting the machinery. Every
measurement this session says output is stubborn against model changes (grounded
cycle costs, byte costs, trip counts — all neutral), which under the old bar was
discouraging and under this one is ENCOURAGING: a near-neutral rewrite that removes
1221 lines and ~42 switches is a success.

THE RISK, and it is real: those gates encode BUGS THAT WERE ACTUALLY FOUND — the
frameless landmine, the slot-coalescing miscompile, the stale-A fold, the
param-as-invisible-def class. Deleting them wholesale would reintroduce that class of
defect. G3's own design is the protection: retire ONE predicate at a time, each
behind its own gate, each validated on the full gauntlet, with the regression tests
(long_ir/*.c) as the memory of why each existed.

11/9/2026 (s14) — THE IDEAL IS NOW LOWERING-AWARE, and that reprices the rewrite.
            Selection quality is **66.7 %**, not 50 % — a third of the gap was values
            the lowerer could never home. Selection and ELIGIBILITY are worth ROUGHLY
            THE SAME (+57956 vs +76782). Committed 5749b0e0fe.
================================================================================
The probe credited homing any deserving value in any free register. The lowerer has
FIXED per-op register roles (Bus = HL/A, Parking = BC/DE/IX/IY) and cannot home every
shape, and the realizability predicates ARE that encoding — so capture is now
reported over NOMINATED values as well as all deserving ones:

    all deserving .......... 50.1 %     (mixes in proposal coverage)
    lowerer could home it .. **66.7 %** (pure selection quality)

►► THIS PROBE HAS NOW OVERSTATED THE GAP THREE TIMES IN ONE DAY: the naive top-N
   ideal (63 % -> 43 %), the "27.6 % proposal-limited" denominator (-> 60.7 %), and
   now unreachable homes (50 % -> 66.7 %). Every correction moved the SAME direction:
   **an unreachable target makes a mechanism look worse than it is.** Any future
   "X % of achievable is unclaimed" claim gets the restricted denominator first.

►► WHAT THE REWRITE IS WORTH, both halves on one scale (achievable model benefit,
   interference-aware, call- and setup-priced):

    realised today ............................ 116285
    perfect SELECTION over the current pool ... 174241   +57956  (+50 % on realised)
    + perfect PROPOSAL, admit everything ...... 251023   +76782  (+66 % on realised)
                                                          ------
                                          both together = 2.2x realised

   **Colouring addresses the FIRST half only.** Eligibility is worth at least as
   much and is untouched by G2. Within the eligibility half, the MULTI-WRITE tail
   (60 values, 30 % of the unconsidered benefit) is ~23000 — 10-15 % of what is
   realised today. It remains the best-evidenced argument FOR colouring, because a
   value written N times and read between writes is what a write_count==1 predicate
   structurally cannot admit and a colourer handles naturally. Worth having; not the
   bulk of the prize.

   (Two caveats on the 431 census: `use_count` does NOT count a vreg used as a deref
   BASE, so its `uses=0` rows are not really unused; and 102739 is a SUM of per-value
   benefits, not an achievable assignment — 431 values cannot share 3 registers. The
   achievable figures above are the ones to quote.)

►► ►► THE CAVEAT THAT OUTRANKS EVERY NUMBER HERE. These are MODEL benefits, and
   today EVERY model-level improvement produced approximately ZERO real gain:
   grounded cycle costs (s7/s8), grounded byte costs (s9), derived trip counts (s11)
   — each strictly more accurate, none moved bytes or ticks. A 2.2x model-benefit
   headroom is not a promise of 2.2x anything.

   SO THE NEXT STEP IS NOT G2. It is to take the CHEAPEST slice of the selection
   half, ship it, and check whether REALISED benefit tracks the MODEL at all. If it
   does not, the model is still missing a term and a quarter spent on colouring will
   discover that expensively. If it does track, the case for G2 is made on evidence
   rather than on a plan written before any of this was measured.

11/9/2026 (s13) — ►► THE s12 HEADLINE WAS WRONG AND THIS CORRECTS IT. Coverage is

            are genuinely unconsidered, carrying 102739 BC benefit, and the value is

================================================================================
THE ERROR: "plausible" counted every width-2, non-escaping, accessed vreg. But every
realizability predicate opens with `vreg_to_phys != IR_PR_SPILL -> reject`, so a value
ALREADY PLACED is correctly skipped, not overlooked. Of 1832 unproposed:

    1401 ALREADY PLACED (correctly skipped)   431 genuinely SPILL and unconsidered

    => predicates nominate 666 / (666+431) = **60.7 %** of what is available to them.

►► THE METHOD LESSON, and it is the same one as the `ideal` in s6: **a denominator
that counts already-solved cases as failures makes any stage look like the

    hash_compute v45  uses=48 writes=1  ben=1440
**The write-once condition is 3 % of the rejections and a large share of the value
behind them** — the same shape §5.4 stage 2 hit (`acc = acc + t`, which clears
neither bc_home_realizable's write_count==1 nor iv_home_realizable's use_count>=8).

►► WHERE THAT LEAVES THE ROAD TO COLOURING. Four suspects have now been measured and
none is dominant: costs (grounded, no win), weights (grounded, no win), selection
displacement/time-sharing (8 refusals, 0 recoverable), proposal coverage (60.7 %).
The honest remaining suspect is **the probe's own `ideal`**: it assigns any deserving
value to any free register over disjoint intervals, while the lowerer has FIXED
per-op register roles (Bus = HL/A, Parking = BC/DE/IX/IY — see context.md) and
cannot home every shape. Until the ideal respects that, part of the 50 % target is
not real, and colouring would be aimed at a number that includes it.

NEXT, in order:
 1. Make the ideal LOWERING-AWARE — only credit a home the lowerer could realise.
    Re-read capture. This is cheap and it decides whether the gap is 50 % or much
    less, i.e. whether G2 is worth a quarter.
 2. The multi-write tail (60 values, the benefit peak): a value written N times and
    read between writes is exactly what a colourer handles naturally and what
    write-once predicates cannot. This is the best-evidenced ARGUMENT for colouring
    so far — but size it before building.

11/9/2026 (s12) — ►► CORRECTED BY s13 BELOW. The "27.6 % / proposal-limited"

"IS SPILL COST THE NEXT ITEM?" — NO, TWICE OVER:
  1. Spill cost ALREADY EXISTS. `rank_benefit` / `interval_benefit_x` IS the cost of
     leaving v in a slot. Building another would duplicate it.
  2. BC is ALREADY interval-aware in the arbiter (it overlap-tests against assigned
     BC vregs — "BC is multi-occupant"). The gap is not uniform across classes.

MEASURED, part 1 — the single-occupant classes. idx2/idx3/exx/byte are BOOLEANS, one
tenant per function, so a candidate with a DISJOINT range is refused even though BC
proves the mechanism is safe. Counting refusals that TIME-SHARING would admit, and
those where the newcomer OUT-EARNS the incumbent (ir_bc_pack's bc-evict generalised):

    refused=8   would_share=0   would_evict=0

**Eight refusals corpus-wide, nothing recoverable.** Both levers REFUTED.

MEASURED, part 2 — so why is there no contention?

    proposed=666   plausible=2416   =>  **27.6 %**   (213 functions)

The arbiter can only place what the predicates nominate. Three quarters of the
width-2, non-escaping, actually-accessed values never reach it.

►► THIS MAKES THE WHOLE SESSION CONSISTENT. Grounding the cycle costs (s7/s8), the
byte costs (s9) and the iteration weights (s11) each changed almost nothing — all
three refine how the arbiter chooses AMONG CANDIDATES IT WAS ALREADY GIVEN. And a
pool that small is barely contended, which is exactly why displacement finds only 8
refusals. One number explains four negative results.

►► THE CONSEQUENCE FOR COLOURING, and it changes the plan. G2 colours THE POOL. A
colourer over the same 27.6 % inherits the same ceiling no matter how good its spill
metric is. **Widen the proposal stage first, then colour it.** The next measurement
is the obvious one: WHICH predicate rejects the other 72 %, and how much benefit sits
behind each — the same census that turned §1 from a guess into a number, applied to
bc_home_realizable / idx2_home_realizable / de_*_realizable / byte_home_realizable /
iv_home_realizable.

CAVEAT ON "PLAUSIBLE": it is width-2, non-ADDR_TAKEN/VOLATILE, with at least one
access — deliberately generous, so 27.6 % is a LOWER bound on coverage and some of
the 72 % will be correctly excluded (a value live across an ASM block, say). The
per-predicate census is what turns it into a real number.

11/9/2026 (s11) — THE TRIP-COUNT TERM IS BUILT AND DOES NOT PAY (opt-in IR_TRIPW,
            f178e3e714). Ticks 6 faster / 3 slower, +0.038 %; size +66 B at the best
            default. ►► THAT NEGATIVE RESULT IS THE USEFUL ONE: costs are now
            measured and weights derived, and the output does not improve — so the
            bottleneck is the SELECTION, not the metric. Colouring is where the
            payoff is; the metric work was necessary but not sufficient.
================================================================================
BUILT: per loop, derive the trip count at the one point loop MEMBERSHIP is known
(the dominance scan) and fold it into every block the loop contains. The five
weighted sites — both cost_benefit scans, g0_bc_call_save, interval_benefit_x and
the BC interval scan — now read one estimate through bb_iter_weight().

THE DEFAULT IS PART OF THE FIX. A real count where known and 4 elsewhere MIXES
SCALES: a literal-bounded 1000-trip loop would outrank an unknown loop at the same
depth 250:1 for no reason but its bound being a literal. Unknown loops take one
tuned constant on the scale of the real ones (corpus median trip 63 -> default 64,
IR_TRIPW_DEF retunes).

SWEEP (corpus x z80 x sp/fp), size:
    DEF=4  +117 B | DEF=16 +117 B | DEF=64 +66 B | DEF=256 +66 B   — ALL LARGER
TICKS at DEF=64: 6 FASTER, 3 SLOWER, aggregate +0.0378 %
    ptrbench fp -1.342 %   hashbench fp -1.074 %   structbench sp -0.710 %
    ptrbench sp -0.534 %   bitfieldbench -0.23/-0.12 %
    matrixbench fp +0.141 %   lexbench sp +2.065 %   **hashbench sp +2.439 %**
    (hashbench moves in BOTH directions — fp -1.07 %, sp +2.44 % — which is itself a
     sign the decision is being made on something the model still cannot see.)

REFUTED ON THE WAY — the missing-SETUP hypothesis. The model never charged the
one-time cost of PRIMING a home, and a real trip count should expose that by scaling
the per-access side while leaving the one-off fixed. Added it: **identical bytes and
identical ticks to three decimals.** A one-off 46-cycle charge cannot move a benefit
weighted in the hundreds. Removed rather than kept as dead code.

►► THE CONCLUSION THAT REORDERS THE PLAN. Three things have now been grounded in
sequence — the cycle costs (s7/s8), the byte costs (s9), the iteration weights
(here) — and the output is unchanged-to-slightly-worse. The metric is no longer the
suspect. IR_GRAPH_PROBE says the arbiter captures ~50 % of achievable benefit and
picks the model's best candidates only ~53 % of the time under contention, because
it prices each candidate IN ISOLATION and claims registers greedily. **A better cost
cannot help a mechanism that never compares a home against the one it displaces.**

So the metric work was the right prerequisite — a colourer picks what to spill BY
COST and would have inherited a 512x weight error — but the payoff is in GRAPH_ALLOC_
PLAN.md's G2, spill-cost-driven cross-class assignment, which is still unbuilt.
KEEP IR_TRIPW OPT-IN and re-test it WITH the colourer: a term that cannot pay under
greedy selection may well pay under one that can act on it.

GATES: long_ir 484/484 sp and 465/465 fp with the gate ON; enigma RXSEC both modes;
gate-off byte-identical.

11/9/2026 (s10) — ►► THE MISSING TERM IS THE TRIP COUNT, AND IT IS SIZED.
            The allocator weights a block 4^loop_depth. 60 % of corpus loops have a
            COMPILE-TIME-DERIVABLE trip count, and 43 of those 73 are under-weighted
            by >10x, 12 by >100x, worst 512x. Error is one-directional.
            Probe committed inert (621ae66caf). BUILD THE TERM BEFORE COLOURING.
================================================================================
WHY THIS IS THE BLOCKER FOR COLOURING: a colourer decides what to SPILL by cost.
Feed it a wrong cost and a correct colourer places things wrongly, so the metric has
to be right first. `benefit = SUM over accesses of weight x (slot_cost - reg_cost)`
— s7/s8 grounded the COST half; this entry sizes the WEIGHT half.

IT ALSO EXPLAINS THE gbz80 RESULT (s9). gbz80's own MEASURED table makes histbench
**10 % slower**, which reads as "the measurement is wrong". It is not: histbench's
inner loop is REPS 50 x STREAM 1000 = **50000 iterations weighted 16**. Refining one
factor sharpens a decision whose other factor is wrong by three orders of magnitude.
**An accurate cost multiplied by a fictional frequency is still fiction** — and the
gbz80 table should be RE-TESTED once the weight is real, not written off.

PROBE (IR_TRIPPROBE, inert), 30 benches, 121 loops:
    RESOLVED 73 (60 %)     of which 38 countdown-shaped
    ratio = derived trip / model weight:
        <1x (model OVER-weights)    2
        1-10x                      28
        10-100x                    31
        100-1000x                  12      worst 512x (trip 2047 vs weight 4)
    unresolved: 44 no-const-bound, 2 no-unit-step, 2 no-const-init

►► THE SHAPE THAT MATTERS, and it took the probe from 28 % to 60 %. ast_opt rewrites
   `for (i = 0; i < N; i++)` into DECREMENT-TO-ZERO (AST_LOOP_COUNTDOWN), so there is
   NO compare against a constant anywhere in the loop:

       BB0 preheader:  LD_IMM v2 <- 1000 ; MOV v3 <- v2 ; BR_ZERO v3, exit
       BB1 body:       ... ; BR latch
       BB3 latch:      DEC v3 <- v3 ; BR_COND v3, body

   The test is **BR_COND at the LATCH**, not BR_ZERO in the header, and the counter is
   initialised through a **MOV**, not a bare LD_IMM. A probe that matches one op finds
   28 %; one that constant-propagates LD_IMM/MOV over the preheader finds 60 %. The
   loops it was missing were precisely the constant-bound ones it existed to find.

►► DESIGN HAZARD BEFORE IMPLEMENTING — do not just plug the number in. Using a real
   trip count where known and 4^depth elsewhere MIXES TWO SCALES: a known 1000-trip
   loop would outrank an unknown loop at the same depth by 250x for no reason other
   than that its bound was a literal. That is a new bias, not a fix. The weight has to
   be one consistent estimate of execution frequency — real count where derivable, a
   TUNED default (not 4) elsewhere — and the default has to be chosen against the
   corpus, not assumed.

11/9/2026 (s6) — IR_GRAPH_PROBE REBUILT (inert), and the `ideal` made ACHIEVABLE.
            The allocator captures 43.4 % of the benefit its own cost model says is
            available, and the gap is SYSTEMIC (213 of 219 functions). But the
            headline number MOVED 63 -> 30 -> 43 % as each model term landed — it is

================================================================================
WHY REBUILT: the original G0 probe (dfcbae603d) was deleted by b69a6697b6 as
"stale — questions answered". The question is live again. Two blind spots fixed:
 (1) it skipped every SPILLED vreg (`if (areg < 0) continue`), so it could only find
     values in the WRONG register, never a value that should have had one and got
     none — the direction the 4-way census actually points at;
 (2) it reported no CONCURRENCY, so it could not see pressure at all.

INERT, verified: clisp 9683 + emu.c 13126 lines byte-identical to the reference at
every step. +313 lines, all inside `getenv("IR_GRAPH_PROBE")`.

>> ►► THE NUMBER IS ONLY AS HONEST AS THE `ideal`, AND THAT IS THE REAL LESSON:

   naive top-N-by-benefit ideal .................. CAPTURE 63.0 %
   + interference (achievable assignment, time-share) ....... 30.5 %
   + call-frequency term (push/pop bc per crossed call) ..... included above
   + SETUP term (one slot read to prime a home) ............. 43.4 %
   + complete population (count homes that fail the bar) .... 43.4 %  (stable)

   **Each term moved the answer 20-30 points.** Any go/no-go on an allocator rewrite
   taken from the first number would have been taken on fiction. The last correction
   moved it 21 units in 133708 — the metric is now stable to that choice, which is
   the only reason to trust 43.4 % at all.

>> WHAT THE FINAL MODEL PRICES (all three were missing from the naive version):
   - INTERFERENCE: overlapping values cannot share a register; disjoint ones CAN and
     are credited (this is what ir_bc_pack really does). Greedy, so a LOWER bound on
     the optimum — the safe direction.
   - CALL FREQUENCY: BC/DE are caller-clobbered, -21 cyc per crossed call; IX/IY are
     callee-saved, one prologue save/restore however many calls they span. This is
     the variable GRAPH_ALLOC_PLAN.md calls "missing throughout" and the one
     MEASURED failing this session (clisp _fcall: 54 reads say home it, 117 calls
     make it a net +18 B LOSS).
   - SETUP: a home must be primed with one slot read. Without it the ideal credits
     unlimited zero-cost short tenancies, which is how the 30.5 % figure ran away.

>> THE FINDINGS THAT SURVIVE ALL OF THAT:

   CAPTURE = 43.4 % (real 133687 / ideal 307881, 219 functions).
   THE GAP IS SYSTEMIC, NOT A FEW OUTLIERS:
       top-1 function  =  4.5 % of the gap      top-20 = 47.2 %
       top-10          = 30.7 %                 top-50 = 78.0 %
       213 of 219 functions have a gap.
   PRESSURE: 115 of 309 functions have peak demand > supply; worst excess 26.
   TOP-N AGREEMENT: 55.2 % overall, **45.6 % in contended functions** — under
   contention the allocator picks the model's best candidates less than half the time.
   Only ONE function has negative realised benefit, so the allocator rarely takes an
   actively LOSING home. **The gap is homes NOT TAKEN, not bad homes taken.**

>> ►► HOW TO READ THIS FOR THE GO/NO-GO. It supports the diagnosis (greedy,
   isolation-priced ranking + 11 proposers + 4 scavenger passes leaves ~half the
   modelled benefit unclaimed, pervasively). It does NOT yet justify the rewrite,
   because the remaining unvalidated term is the model itself: `g0_word_cost` is
   grounded for READ/WRITE but DEREF/STEP are marked estimates in its own comment,
   and the 43.4 % moves with them. **Next: validate the DEREF and STEP rows by
   micro-benchmark the way the READ row was, then re-read this number.** If it
   holds near 43 % the rewrite is justified; if it collapses the way 63 % did, it is not.

  strbench        63 acc  276 B (w=29)    55 acc  165 B (w=0)     +111 B / 137 B
  bitfieldbench   55 acc  273 B (w=36)    24 acc   72 B (w=0)     +201 B / 437 B
  queenbench      13 acc   51 B (w= 4)    18 acc   54 B (w=0)       -3 B /  77 B
  crcbench        21 acc   84 B (w= 7)   108 acc  324 B (w=0)     -240 B /  56 B

>> ►► **sdcc's WORD-ACCESS COUNT IS ZERO IN ALL SIX.** Every frame touch it makes
   is a 3-byte byte move. 80cc makes 39/11/29/36 word accesses at 6 B each.
   Frame traffic is **90 % of structbench's gap, 81 % of strbench's, 62 % of
   ptrbench's, 46 % of bitfieldbench's.**

>> THE LEVER IS NOT "SPLIT THE ACCESS". Two `ld a,(ix+d)` cost the same 6 B as one
   `ld hl,(ix+d)`, and probe 1 says both halves are usually wanted. The win is that
   with the halves allocated INDEPENDENTLY, a reload touches only the half that was
   actually evicted — so sdcc's TOTAL frame bytes are 3x lower on ptrbench (345 ->
   108) even though it makes byte-sized accesses. **This is byte-granular register
   allocation** (`GRAPH_ALLOC_PLAN.md`), not a peephole and not a narrowing pass.

>> ►► AND IT IS NOT ONE DISEASE — TWO OF THE SIX GO THE OTHER WAY. On crcbench sdcc
   spends **240 B MORE** on frame traffic than 80cc and is still 56 B smaller,
   because 80cc parks pairs on the STACK (`push de; push hl; srl d; rr e; rr h`)
   instead of spilling bytes to cheap frame slots. queenbench is likewise frame-
   neutral (-3 B) with a 77 B gap. **Those two are the push/pop parking story
   (Tier 1 item 2); the other four are the byte-granularity story.** Do not merge.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLAN: Tier 2 is REAL and is the biggest single item measured
so far (roughly 240-640 B across four benches), but it is an ALLOCATOR
ARCHITECTURE change — let a 16-bit value live as two independently-allocated
bytes — not the cheap narrowing step the plan assumed. Size it before committing:
the next probe is "how many 80cc word frame accesses reload a half that was never
clobbered", which is the directly recoverable subset.

11/9/2026 (s4) — BACK TO BASICS: 80cc vs sdcc vs xcc vs sccz80 on CODEGEN ONLY
            (code_compiler section, z80, 30 benches, all four fresh on one tree).
            80cc BEATS xcc (median 0.94x) and is near sccz80 (1.07x). sdcc is the
            only real gap at 1.19x. THE DISEASE IS REGISTER PRESSURE ON WIDE
            VALUES AND ACROSS CALLS — 80cc parks where sdcc keeps registers.
================================================================================
METHOD: `zcc +test -vn -compiler=<c> -c <bench> -o x.o` then the code_compiler
section via z88dk-z80nm. This is the basis the 8/9 entry established — NOT whole
binaries, which carry the ~790 B printf-converter asymmetry. 80cc column = best of
sp/fp per bench. xcc -Os and xcc -Of were IDENTICAL in all 30 cells; collapsed.

>> MEDIAN RATIO, >1.00 = 80cc LARGER:
       vs sdcc    1.19x   (larger on 26 of 30)
       vs xcc     0.94x   (larger on only  8 of 30)
       vs sccz80  1.07x   (larger on 22 of 30)

   **80cc is the SECOND-best codegen of the four and beats xcc outright.** The
   "~19 % larger" figure is specifically an sdcc gap, not a general standing.

>> ►► THE SIX BENCHES WHERE 80cc LOSES TO ALL THREE — these are 80cc's OWN fault,
   not sdcc being strong, and they are the list to work:

       bitfieldbench   sdcc 1.66  xcc 1.36  sccz80 1.44
       ptrbench        sdcc 1.33  xcc 1.19  sccz80 1.11
       structbench     sdcc 1.32  xcc 1.11  sccz80 1.05
       strbench        sdcc 1.26  xcc 1.06  sccz80 1.07
       queenbench      sdcc 1.22  xcc 1.03  sccz80 1.02
       crcbench        sdcc 1.07  xcc 1.11  sccz80 1.12

   CONTRAST — where 80cc trails sdcc but BEATS xcc, sdcc is simply strong and the
   cell is NOT evidence of an 80cc defect: widthbench (sdcc 1.40 but xcc 0.69),
   localbench (1.37 / 0.91), matrixbench (1.37 / 0.90), fixedbench (1.19 / 0.72).
   **Do not put these on the same list.** The 8/9 "worst outliers" set mixes them.

>> THE INSTRUCTION SIGNATURE, 80cc minus sdcc, and it is the SAME in every case:
       ptrbench    ld +70  pop +29  jp +27  push +24  sbc +9
       crcbench    pop +31  push +29  rr +24  jp +11  add +10  xor +9  srl +8
       queenbench  pop +16  push +12    <- the ONLY classes differing by >=8
   By register: 80cc stacks HL/BC/DE far more (ptrbench HL +58 BC +28;
   crcbench DE +30 HL +26; queenbench BC +23 HL +17) while sdcc's higher `push af`
   count is FRAME ALLOCATION, not saving. Checked and NOT the cause: the call
   convention is the same (both push args, same byte cost), and
   --opt-disable=bc-pack / word-resident moves ptrbench only -45 B and the others 0.

>> ►► THE NAMED DISEASE, from crcbench's 32-bit shift — the clearest instance:
       sdcc:  ld e,(ix-4) / ld d,(ix-3) / srl d / rr e / rr b
       80cc:  push de / push hl / srl d / rr e / rr h
       80cc also does:  ld hl,3 / add hl,sp / srl (hl)   <- shifting MEMORY through
                                                            a computed stack address
   **80cc PARKS the operand to get registers; sdcc keeps it in registers and shifts
   in place.** Same story as the push/pop deltas everywhere else, and the same
   story as _fcall (s3 entry): 80cc's answer to pressure is the stack or the frame.

>> WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE WORK LIST. The gap is not a missing peephole and not a
   missing pass — it is the register allocator's behaviour under pressure on (a)
   WIDE values and (b) values live across calls. That is §5.2's pressure term,
   and it is now supported by three independent measurements: the s3 _fcall
   arithmetic (117 calls vs 54 reads), the Arm-A picker lift (+22 B: clean
   candidates that still do not pay), and this census.

RAW DATA: /tmp/cmp3.txt format `bench 80cc-sp 80cc-fp sdcc xcc-Os xcc-Of sccz80`.

11/9/2026 (s3) — THE REPEATED FRAME READS: the route is REAL and MEASURED
            (clisp -198 B, _fcall's 54 `ld hl,(ix+4)` -> ZERO) but it MISCOMPILES.
            FOUR exclusions stack, and the last one is LOAD-BEARING. The work is a
            LOWERING capability. Prototype: src/80cc/IDXBASE_PROTO.patch.txt
================================================================================
THE TARGET, priced exactly. clisp `_fcall` is 2704 asm lines, 131 frame word reads
(6 B each on z80 = 786 B), of which **54 are ONE pointer param at (ix+4)** = 324 B.
It makes **117 calls** and already carries 368 push/pop bc.

>> WHY A BC HOME CAN NEVER PAY HERE, ARITHMETIC NOT OPINION:
     saves  54 reads x (6 B - 2 B `ld l,c; ld h,b`) =  216 B
     costs 117 calls x  2 B (push bc / pop bc)      =  234 B
     NET +18 B. There are MORE CALLS THAN READS. This is why callsplit, bc-pack
     and every BC-shaped lever have failed on this function for a year. Stop
     aiming BC at it.

>> THE ONLY REGISTER THAT PAYS IS AN INDEX REGISTER, because IY is callee-saved —
   no per-call cost at all — and because a pointer in an index register need never
   be LOADED: `ld a,(iy+d)` (3 B) replaces `ld hl,(ix+4)` + `ld a,(hl)` (7 B).

>> FOUR EXCLUSIONS STACK BETWEEN _fcall's PARAM AND AN IY HOME. Each one looks
   correct in isolation; they were found by lifting them one at a time and getting
   NO CHANGE each time, which is why this has stayed hidden:
    1. the BC veto (ir_alloc.c:4674) — collect_home_candidates is never CALLED for
       a vetoed function, so RC_IDX2 is never even proposed. The picker lift is a
       prerequisite for the index path, not just the BC path.
    2. `is_base[v]` in idx2_home_realizable (ir_alloc.c:534) — deref bases are
       excluded from INDEX homes. For BC that is right (a base is read straight
       out of BC); for an index register it is backwards.
    3. the fp rule in idx2_home_available (ir_alloc.c:~1281) — idx2-across-calls is
       sp-mode only, argued as "fp: idx2=IY, cheap (ix+d) slots, lose/lose". TRUE
       FOR A VALUE, FALSE FOR A DEREF BASE — and (2) had already removed every
       deref base from the population, so the leftover population really does not
       pay and the rule reads as correct. **(2) and (3) INTERLOCK: lift them
       together or neither.**
    4. MY OWN Arm-A filter (BCVETOLIFT) applied the BC cleanliness test to EVERY
       class — `BCLIFT fcall pool=2 -> 0`. Wrong: the veto is a BC veto, only a
       class that OWNS BC must answer it; IY has its own narrower gate
       (iy_region_ok, already true here). Applying the BC test to IY rejects every
       candidate in a function with a CALL — exactly the population that matters.

>> WITH ALL FOUR LIFTED (IR_BCVETOLIFT=1 IR_IDXBASE=1), fp:
       clisp code_compiler 14680 -> **14482 = -198 B**
       _fcall `ld hl,(ix+4)`: **54 -> 0**  (param homed in IY, `push hl; pop iy`)
   The realised win is the LESSER one: each read became `push iy; pop hl` (4 B vs
   6 B = 2 B/read), NOT `(iy+d)` addressing (4 B/read). Zero `(iy+d)` in the output.

>> ►► BUT IT MISCOMPILES. clisp: `] (+ 1 2)` -> `ERROR. FUNCTION UNDEFINED`.
   Baseline prints 3. **The is_base exclusion is LOAD-BEARING** — the index-home
   path does not correctly serve a deref base. So the task is NOT the allocator
   gates; it is the LOWERING: make a deref read its base from an index home (and
   ideally address through it as `(iy+d)`, which is where the other half of the
   win is). The gates are then a 4-line follow-on, already prototyped.

SCOPE, before anyone sizes this corpus-wide: emu.c has NO deref-base callsplit
case at all (its candidates fail span<3 / uses<2 / not-spill). The measured prize
is clisp's 81 reads (fcall 54, symb_make 16, eval_args 11), ~200-300 B in ONE FILE.
Worth doing because it is the whole `_fcall` class, not because it is corpus-wide.

PROTOTYPE: src/80cc/IDXBASE_PROTO.patch.txt (188 lines, all four lifts + the
IR_IDXWHY/IDXWHY2 diagnostics). MISCOMPILES — it is a measurement, not a candidate.
Reverted; tree clean; clisp verified back to printing 3.

11/9/2026 (s2) — §1, THE BC VETO: the veto is NOT the binding constraint. Lifting
            it is MEASURED and does not pay (+22 B corpus, +48 B emu.c). The real
            blocker for the repeated frame reads is the CALLSPLIT DEREF-BASE

THE GOAL: drop repeated frame reads. 509 `ld hl,(ix+d)` word reloads across the
four real files ~= 3054 B, 6 B each on z80 against 2 for `ld hl,bc`. clisp _fcall
reloads ONE pointer param 54 times. §1 was believed to be the stepping stone.

>> FIRST, THE 8/9 SIZING IS THE WRONG LINE. Its table ("97 of 194 REAL_emu ::
   ms_rungame", "28 of 36 REAL_clisp :: symb_make") is the BCVETO line, which is
   the UPPER BOUND the probe comment itself says to discount. The BCVETOC line,
   which applies the real proposer predicates, says ms_rungame is 20 of 31 — not
   97 of 194. Honest totals, real predicates, fp:
       emu.c   96 proposed / 51 clean, over 10 functions
       clisp   62 proposed / 12 clean, over  5 functions
   With one BC home per function that is 106 + 17 = 123 reads, NOT 614 vregs.

>> SECOND, HALF OF §1 HAS ALREADY SHIPPED AND THE HANDOVER DOES NOT SAY SO.
   `IR_BCPERCAND` is DEFAULT-ON (ir_alloc.c:3071) and already runs ir_bc_pack
   inside vetoed functions, filtering by vreg_bc_clean. `ir_stack_spill` is no
   longer gated by the veto either — it is gated by `bc_region_ok || !fp_ix_frame`
   (ir_alloc.c:5553), so it ALREADY runs in long-containing functions in sp mode
   and on 808x/gbz80. What the veto still blocks is (a) the GENERAL PICKER
   (ir_alloc.c:5405) and (b) CALLSPLIT (ir_alloc.c:5830).

>> BUILT AND MEASURED, BOTH ARMS, opt-in IR_BCVETOLIFT (gate-off byte-identical,
   clisp 9683 + emu.c 13126 lines both modes):

   ARM A, the general picker — narrow each candidate to the classes whose register
   is clean across its OWN range (the IR_BCPERCAND treatment, one level up):
       corpus z80/z80n/z180/gbz80 x sp/fp = 240 cells: 2 smaller (-16 B),
       7 larger (+38 B), 231 UNCHANGED, NET +22 B, 0 aborts
       clisp -11 B, emu.c +48 B (code_compiler) -> NET LOSS
       emu.c frame word reloads went UP 262 -> 268, push/pop bc +8, 2998 asm
       lines churned. A whole-range BC home in a long-heavy function pays for
       itself in call save/restore and displaced allocations.
   VERDICT: refuted as written. This is §5.2's missing PRESSURE term again,
   reached from a new direction — the candidates are clean, taking them is not free.

   ARM B, callsplit (the RANGED path, and the one that matters) — lift the gate and
   require the SPAN it homes to be BC-clean instead of the whole range. Sound: the
   span is already call-free by construction, so only in-span BC staging is left.
       Result: ZERO splits committed. clisp gets 2 span-bc-dirty rejects.

>> ►► THE FINDING, AND IT IS THE USEFUL ONE. With the veto lifted, _fcall IS
   REACHED — and the log says:

       cs-skip fcall     v1 param=1 uses=54 deref-base
       cs-skip symb_make v0 param=1 uses=16 deref-base
       cs-skip eval_args v2 param=1 uses=11 deref-base

   **THE BLOCKER IS THE DEREF-BASE EXCLUSION, NOT THE VETO.** 3 candidates
   carrying 81 repeated frame reads in clisp alone. The 8/9 handover's "_fcall is
   not rejected by a callsplit predicate, it is never reached" is only half right:
   it is not reached, AND when you make it reachable a predicate rejects it.

   The exclusion (ir_alloc.c ~5843) is Phase-1 and honest: "a pointer used as a
   deref base is read straight out of BC (`ld a,(bc)`) with no load_to_* reload,
   so an opportunistic BC cache can't serve it". So the work is a LOWERING
   capability — teach the deref path to read its base from a BC home — not an
   allocator gate. THAT is the stepping stone to the repeated frame reads.

   emu.c has NO deref-base case: its callsplit candidates fail on span<3, uses<2
   and not-spill. The ranged opportunity in the real files is clisp's 81 reads
   (~4 B saved per read, so ~300 B in one file), not a corpus-wide 3 KB.

PATCH: src/80cc/BCVETOLIFT.patch.txt (122 lines, `git apply` verified). Both arms,
opt-in, gate-off byte-identical. Re-apply ARM B after the deref-base work; ARM A is
refuted and should be dropped unless a pressure term lands first.

11/9/2026 — §0 (widen the long stack-park pass, use_count==1) is REFUTED. Lifting
            the gate reaches ZERO sites, not the ~325 the 8/9 sizing claimed. NOT
            WORTH DIGGING INTO. Next item is §1, the BC veto.

THE ITEM AS WRITTEN: "lift `use_count[dst] != 1` in ir_opt_insert_long_pushes.
Rejected on it alone: 197 in md5, 128 elsewhere ~= 325 sites." That number is an
artifact of how it was counted.

THE 8/9 CENSUS IS AN if/else CHAIN AND TESTS `usecount>1` FIRST, so that bucket
absorbs every candidate that ALSO fails another gate. Re-testing those 311
rejects against the gates a widened pass actually needs (corpus + clisp + emu.c,
fp):

    195  W-multi-def         70  W-use-other-bb      33  W-use-before-def
     10  W-consumer-kind      3  W-producer-kind      0  W-ELIGIBLE

    by function: 193 multi-def in md5 Transform; the use-other-bb/use-before-def
    tail is clisp (special 31, fcall 24, apply 13, l_eval 7) and crcbench crc32 10.

>> THE 195 ARE AN ILLUSION. md5's "197 rejects" are FOUR distinct vregs — Transform's
   MD5 state a/b/c/d — each redefined ~48 times across the 64 unrolled rounds and
   reported once per def.

>> THE REAL FINDING, AND THE REASON THIS CANNOT BE WIDENED CHEAPLY: the IR is NOT
   SSA. `use_count` is function-wide and pools the uses of EVERY def of a vreg;
   `bb_use_idx` is the FIRST use in the BB, which for a redefined vreg can sit
   BEFORE the def under consideration. So `use_count[dst] == 1` is NOT a use-count
   heuristic — it is doing double duty as a DEF-UNIQUENESS gate, and it is what
   makes def/use pairing sound without reaching definitions. Lifting it removes
   the thing keeping the pass correct. A widened pass needs real liveness FIRST,
   and the only shape it then reaches is md5 Transform — the one bench 80cc
   already wins 0.64x. The ~19 % deficit is elsewhere; this is upside in the
   bench that is already winning.

TRAPS HIT, each of which gave a WRONG ANSWER before being caught:
 1. THE PASS IS fp-ONLY BY DEFAULT. `want_pushes = fp_active(f)` (ir_lower.c:5908);
    OFF in sp, `IR_LONG_PUSHES=0/1` forces. The first run logged NOTHING because it
    was built sp. "An empty log is not no-candidates" — the 8/9 handover's own trap,
    hit within a day.
 2. ADJACENCY DOES NOT EXCUSE A MULTI-USE VALUE. A re-census first scored 194 md5
    sites as "also adjacent, therefore not a loss". WRONG: the cur_dehl_dst_dead_safe
    block is guarded by L.la.cur_dst_dead (ir_lower.c:7751), so for a still-live
    vreg it never fires and the value IS spilled. Adjacency excuses only the FIRST
    use; uses 2..N reload from the slot.
 3. A CAP READ AS A MEASUREMENT. All 193 "eligible" sites reported n=64 — the
    probe's own array cap — and spans ran NEGATIVE. A census that reports a
    CONSTANT is reporting its own limit, not the code.

The measuring probe was REVERTED, not committed: the answer is recorded here and
the shape is a dead end. The committed inert IR_LONGPUSH_PROBE still reproduces the
FIRST census (md5 fp: 315 adjacent / 197 usecount>1 / 69 ELIGIBLE / 1 consumer-kind
= 582); just do not read its usecount>1 bucket as opportunity.

8/9/2026 — §5 item 3 (the ez80 fp cost row) is CLOSED, but as a REFUTATION: the
            row is not mis-measured, the hardware genuinely ties, and the missing
            information is not in the byte table either. Byte tie-break shipped
            OPT-IN: -106 B / 0 cells larger, but ticks 9 faster / 3 SLOWER.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE ITEM AS WRITTEN: "the ez80 fp cost row of g0_word_cost cannot separate a
register from a slot (both 2 cycles), so every ez80 fp allocation is settled by
tie-break order rather than cost. Bounded; the same treatment the gbz80 row got."

►► THE FRAMING IS WRONG AND THAT IS THE RESULT. The gbz80 treatment was MEASURING
   real, distinct cycle numbers where the old row guessed. There is nothing
   equivalent to measure here: on ez80 fp a slot read genuinely IS a native
   `ld hl,(ix+d)` at 2 cycles, which is exactly what `ld l,c; ld h,b` costs. THE
   ROW IS RIGHT. Confirmed by reading interval_benefit_x: on ez80 fp only the
   STEP column differs (4 vs 2), so every read/write/deref contributes ZERO and
   only stepped values score at all — which is why the IVWHY census showed
   ez80 fp rivals at ben=0 and accumulators at 4-12.

WHAT WAS BUILT: `IR_BYTETIE` — rank a candidate pool LEXICOGRAPHICALLY, cycles
first and STATIC BYTES to break the tie (g0_byte_benefit, bc_byte_benefit
generalised to any class, incl. the push/pop charge per spanned call). Kept as a
SEPARATE Cand field, never summed — the units differ, and adding them would let a
3-byte candidate outrank a 2-cycle one.

SIZE: **-106 B, 13 cells smaller, ZERO larger**, exactly where the item predicted:
  ez80 -85 B over 8 cells, ALL fp (lexbench -35, hashbench -15, vecbench -11,
  searchbench -5, maskbench -5, shiftbench -5, queenbench -4, bitfieldbench -5)
  plus bitfieldbench on r2ka/r4k/r6k/kc160 — the other cheap-slot targets.

TICKS: 12 cells changed, **9 faster / 3 SLOWER**, aggregate -0.04 %.
  queenbench ez80 fp -2.81 %  ...  hashbench ez80 fp +1.76 %
  Those two numbers are VERBATIM the trade IR_BCCALLCOST already measured and
  refused on this row ("it wins queenbench 2.81 % and loses hashbench 1.76 % on
  the same CPU, mode and shape"). Reproducing them from a different direction is
  the strongest evidence yet that the row carries no signal either way.

  A MINIMUM BYTE GAP DOES NOT SEPARATE THEM. Swept IR_BYTETIE=1/2/4/8/16: at 1-4
  all four benches move; at 8+ only lexbench does, and lexbench is itself a tick
  loser (+0.68 %). No threshold keeps the wins and drops the losses.

VERDICT: OPT-IN, default OFF (`IR_BYTETIE=1` enables, `=<N>` sets the gap), because
the bar for default-on is NO CELL SLOWER, not "faster on average". Default is
byte-identical to the pre-change compiler on all 660 cells. long_ir 693/693 sp AND
fp with the gate BOTH off and ON; enigma RXSEC and emu.c 2 hits in both states.

►► CARRY FORWARD: do NOT "fix the ez80 fp row" — there is nothing wrong with it,
   and bytes are not the missing term either. What is missing is second-order:
   HL pressure and spill placement. That needs a real term in the model, which is
   §5.2 territory, not a row edit. This item should be struck from the open list
   and replaced by "the ez80 fp tie needs a pressure term".

ALSO COMMITTED: `IR_ADDRRES_PROBE` (inert), with its measurement in the comment —
118 multi-deref address bases but 91 have only TWO accesses and just 8 have five
or more, which REFUTES address residency as a general lever. Its useful output was
one row: clisp `_fcall` does 54 loads through a SPILLED pointer param, emitted as
54 x `ld hl,(ix+4)` = 6 B each on z80 (there is no real `ld hl,(ix+d)`) against 2
for `ld hl,bc`. 509 such reloads across the real files ≈ 3 KB. That is stage 3,
and it wants a CALL-BOUNDED ranged home — `_fcall` is call-heavy (368 `pop bc`).

7/9/2026 (s4) — the localbench census named the disease, and chasing it turned up
            THREE PRE-EXISTING SILENT MISCOMPILES plus the biggest density win
            of the session: corpus -3408 B / 0 cells larger AND 144/144 tick
            cells FASTER / 0 slower / -1.29 %.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE CENSUS. localbench is the worst SIZE outlier (1.41x sdcc, see the 7/9 s3
basis correction below). It uses only 1.17x sdcc's INSTRUCTIONS (512 vs 436) but
1.41x its bytes — 2.11 bytes/instr against 1.75. The instructions are FATTER,
not more numerous. By class, on z80 fp:

    ld rr,nn   3B    sdcc 105   80cc 264   +159   <- half the whole gap
    jp/call    3B         36         84    +48
    add hl,rr  1B         55         79    +24
    indexed (ix/iy+d)    246        192    -54    <- 80cc uses FEWER

►► TARGET FOUND: the signed-compare sign tail. `i < 16` on a loop counter
   rendered as `and a; sbc hl,de` plus SEVEN bytes of pure sign correction
   (`ld a,h; jp po,L; xor 0x80; L: rla`), because the carry out of `sbc` is the
   UNSIGNED answer and the signed one is S^V. Where both operands are provably
   non-negative the two coincide.

   Sized FIRST with an inert probe (IR_CMPSIGN_PROBE, kept): 153 signed 16-bit
   compares, 50 provable = 350 B in fp. The probe corrected two guesses:
     - v_fits_byte carries only 10 of the 50. The other 40 are `i = i + 1`
       induction variables, which it rejects. A new prover was needed.
     - "init>=0 and += positive" is NOT a proof — a rising value can pass 32767.
       It is a proof only when the compare STOPS the growth. That condition
       rejected 6 of 56 otherwise-passing sites, 2 of them in adv_a.

   SHIPPED `IR_CMPUNSIGN` (default-on, --opt-disable=cmp-unsign):
   corpus **-3408 B, 196 cells smaller, ZERO larger**; ticks **144 cells
   changed, 144 FASTER, ZERO slower, -1.29 % aggregate** (localbench ez80 fp
   -7.96 %, kc160 -6.78 %, 8080 -5.46 %, gbz80 -5.25 %). adv_a -18 B.
   The realised lowering beats the estimate: 9 instructions become 4, because
   the unsigned path also skips materialising HL and DE —
   `ld hl,bc / ld de,16 / and a / sbc hl,de / ld a,h / jp po / xor / rla`
   becomes `ld a,c / sub 16 / ld a,b / sbc a,0`.

►► THREE PRE-EXISTING MISCOMPILES, ALL THE SAME ROOT CAUSE, all found by writing
   the regression tests for the above. ALL predate this session (verified by
   building the compiler at the session-start commit fcff9c2037).

   ROOT CAUSE: **A PARAMETER'S INCOMING VALUE IS A DEF THAT NO DEF-COUNTER SEES.**
   Passes count the defs in THIS function, so a parameter assigned once under a
   condition looks single-def and is not.

     1. remat (ir_lower.c). `int floor0(int v) { if (v<0) v=0; return v+1; }`
        took `LD_IMM 0` as v's defining value; every read became `ld hl,0` and
        the parameter was NEVER LOADED. floor0(5) returned 1, every CPU, both
        modes. Correct on the path where the assignment RUNS, wrong where it
        does not — which is why it hid.
     2. sym_deref_fold (ir_opt.c). `int pick(int *p,int f){ if(f) p=tbl;
        return p[1]; }` folded every `p[i]` to the absolute `tbl+i`, so the
        caller's array was never read.
     3. sym_addr_fold (ir_opt.c) — same table-building hole, found by audit
        rather than by a failure. Guarded before it could bite.

   Fix in all three: add IR_VREG_PARAM beside the existing ADDR_TAKEN/VOLATILE
   exclusion. **Corpus cost: ZERO bytes over 660 cells** — the shapes do not
   occur in any bench, which is exactly why they survived. ir_lower.c:5698
   already had this guard WITH a comment explaining it, so the hazard was known
   and simply not applied everywhere.

   AUDIT: every `ndef[...] == 1` site in ir_opt.c / ir_lower.c now carries the
   guard. Regression long_ir/parremat.c covers the constant and symbol-address
   kinds, the inverted condition, the local-copy control and the two-clamp
   `sat` shape.

7/9/2026 (s3) — ⚠ MEASUREMENT CORRECTION. The whole-binary size tables in
            BENCH_MATRIX.md are INVALID for codegen claims: sdcc carries
            +563..+765 B of extra printf runtime, which inverts the sign. On the
            honest basis 80cc is +23.4 % LARGER on the outlier benches, not
            smaller. Subtraction factors + corrected table: BENCH_MATRIX.md, top.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
CAUSE: sdcc's driver does not restrict the printf formatter set; 80cc's (and
sccz80's) does. Map files: sdcc links `CLIB_OPT_PRINTF = $FFFFFFFF801BF7BF`
(every formatter incl. the 64-bit tables), 80cc emits `CRT_printf_format =
$0201` derived from the format strings it saw. A DRIVER asymmetry, not codegen.
`-pragma-define:CRT_printf_format=0x0201` does NOT equalise it.

SUBTRACTION FACTORS (null bench = same framework/main, no bench code):
    cpu    sdcc  80cc   sdcc penalty
    z80    3957  3394   +563
    z80n   3957  3394   +563
    z180   3932  3365   +567
    r2ka   3774  3009   +765
    gbz80  3973  3977     -4
VALIDATED: (whole - null) reconciles with the module's code_compiler section and
the residual (bench rodata + bench-specific library) is the SAME for both
compilers to within 2 B on z80 — widthbench 356/354, queenbench 121/119,
localbench 104/102, strbench 2172/2170 — so it cancels in a difference.

USE ONE OF THESE, never the whole binary:
  - the module's `code_compiler` section (what corpus_sizescan.sh reads) — BOTH
    compilers emit into it, so it is directly comparable and runtime-free;
  - or whole-binary MINUS the null figure above.

CORRECTED OUTLIER SIZES (code_compiler, best-of-sp/fp / sdcc, >1 = 80cc larger):
  localbench 1.41  widthbench 1.37  structbench 1.34  strbench 1.30
  interpbench 1.27  vecbench 1.25  searchbench 1.23  queenbench 1.22
  hashbench 1.17  shiftbench 1.12 (0.92-0.95 on the z80 family — 80cc WINS)
  predbench 1.09      SUM over 55 cells: sdcc 30822 vs 80cc 38049 = 1.234x

  Consistent with the bases that were already sound (§3 "+4.6 % converter-
  adjusted", sccz80 "+6-8 %"); the outlier set is wider because these benches
  were picked for being bad.

►► THE SIZE AND TICK OUTLIERS ARE DIFFERENT SETS. localbench is the WORST size
   outlier (1.41x) and has never been on the tick list; queenbench is the worst
   TICK outlier (1.64x r2ka) but only 1.22x on size. Stop treating "the
   outliers" as one group — they want different work.

    from test/suites reports BUILD for every sdcc cell needing m4. (Same family

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
The earlier gate demanded BC be UNCONTENDED, which refused widthbench's
mix_char. That was too blunt: an accumulator almost always overlaps something.
The right question is not "is it contended" but "does it WIN the contention".

IR_RANKDUMP on mix_char shows why the accumulator deserves to win: its three
rivals are write-once candidates with TWO uses each, ben=111 (sp) / 90 (fp),
against the accumulator's 8 accesses at ben=332 / 318. A 3:1 gap.

MEASURED ben:rival over every candidate in the gap, against the per-cell size
and tick outcome of admitting it — this is what sets the margin at 3x:

    mix_char  3.0 sp / 3.5 fp   ADMIT   widthbench ticks faster on EVERY cell
    sat       no rival          ADMIT   predbench -462 B, 16/16 faster
    reg_get   2.7 / 2.6         refuse  bitfieldbench +7 B z80 fp for -0.15 %
    kmul      2.3 / 2.7         refuse  divbench +37 B and +4.5 % ticks
    kshift    2.3 / 2.3         refuse  shiftbench +23 B and +2.1 % ticks
    sdiv iir fxdot matrix_compute lex_compute  0.6-0.9  refuse (the RIVAL is
                                               worth more than the accumulator)

The cut sits between 2.7 (a byte-for-tick trade) and 3.0 (a two-axis win). Note
mix_char lands at 2.99 in sp and is REFUSED there — and sp is exactly the mode
where the home cost +3 B for only -0.34 % ticks. The margin picked that apart on
its own; it was not tuned to. `IR_IVACCK=<N>` re-sweeps it.

►► THE ez80 fp TRAP, and the fix that matters more than the margin. On the first
   attempt divbench ez80 fp took a home worth -1 B and **+3.365 % TICKS**. Cause:
   on ez80 fp `g0_word_cost` cannot separate a register from a slot (a slot read
   is a native `ld hl,(ix+d)`, 2 cycles, same as `ld l,c; ld h,b`), so
   interval_benefit prices EVERY rival at 0 — and a rival-max of 0 read as "BC is
   free", admitting everything on a target where the model is BLIND.
   Fix: report a rival COUNT as well as a maximum, and distinguish
     nrivals == 0            -> BC genuinely free      -> admit
     nrivals > 0, max == 0   -> the model cannot see    -> REFUSE
   This is the same reasoning as the `seen` condition in IR_BCCALLCOST (§5.1):
   ask for a real gap before displacing anything. It removed the only tick
   regression while KEEPING predbench ez80 fp (-2.01 %), where sat has no rival
   for real. That distinction is the whole difference between 29-faster-0-slower
   and 29-faster-2-slower.
   NB this is item 3 of §5's open list biting again — the ez80 fp cost row is
   still the prerequisite for taking any ez80 fp case on merit.

RESULT (`IR_IVACC` default-on; `IR_IVACC=0` / `--opt-disable=iv-acc` opts out):
  - corpus **-608 B, 43 cells smaller, 3 larger**, 0 aborts. The three are
    shiftbench r2ka sp +3, bitfieldbench ez80 sp +6, widthbench ez80 sp +3 —
    +12 B total, and the two measurable ones are PAID FOR on the same cell
    (bitfieldbench ez80 sp -0.90 %, widthbench ez80 sp -0.53 %).
  - ticks **29 changed cells, 29 FASTER, 0 SLOWER, -0.70 % aggregate**.
    widthbench fp -2.74 z80 / -2.75 z80n / -2.35 z180; predbench -4.80 gbz80,
    -4.32 8085, -3.85 kc160 sp; bitfieldbench kc160 -3.09/-3.00.
  - emu.c **-11 B both modes**; adv_a and clisp byte-identical.
  - `IR_IVACC=0` byte-identical to the pre-change compiler on all 660 cells.

WIDTHBENCH, finally, against the §4 table in the 5/9 handover: fp was +38.1 %

7/9/2026 — §5.4 stage 2: the accumulator gap is CLOSED, but NOT where the plan
            said. The handover's proposed fix (swap the >=8 constant for

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE GAP, confirmed. Two BC gates leave a hole: bc_home_realizable demands
write_count == 1 (write-once), iv_home_realizable demands use_count >= 8 (hot).
A value written many times and read once per write clears NEITHER and lands in a
slot, paying a round trip per term. Two source shapes:

    acc = acc + t; acc = acc + u; ...          an accumulator   (widthbench mix_char)
    if (v > 255) v = 255; if (v < 0) v = 0;    a clamp chain    (predbench sat)

Census (IR_IVWHY, now committed as an inert probe): the hole is NARROW — 4-ish
candidates over the whole corpus, w in [2,7], u in [1,7].

►► REFUTATION 1 — interval_benefit CANNOT decide this, so stage 2 as written is
   a dead end. It is a CYCLE model and the outcome here is byte- AND mode-driven.
   It rates shiftbench's `kshift` at 590, the HIGHEST of any candidate, on both
   z80 (admitting it costs +23 B and +2.1 % ticks) and gbz80 (-36 B, -4.3 %).
   Same number, opposite sign. Lowering the constant wholesale (IR_IVHOT=4, and
   =2 is identical) is corpus +229 B, 49 smaller / 44 larger, ticks 33 faster /
   24 slower for an aggregate of -0.021 % — a wash bought with bytes.
   This is the same lesson as §5.1: a cycle model alone cannot arbitrate a
   register home. There it was fixed by ADDING a byte table (g0_word_bytes).

►► REFUTATION 2 — call-freeness alone does not decide it either. It correctly
   rejects fixedbench's `iir`/`fxdot` (they call qmul), but `kmul`, `udiv` and
   `kshift` are call-FREE: `v * 25`, `v / 2u`, `v << 4` all lower INLINE. Their
   loss is register PRESSURE, not call saves. Gate = call-free only: -192 B but
   still 43 cells larger and +2..+5 % ticks on divbench/shiftbench.

►► WHAT DOES DECIDE IT: whether BC is actually FREE over the value's window.
   Every loser has a hot operand — the parameter `v`, re-read by every term —
   competing for BC, so the home is taken FROM something better. The winner has
   none. Gate = call-free AND uncontended (`iv_acc_bc_uncontended`, using the
   arbiter's own `iv_overlap` on candidate windows, NOT `ir_live_ranges_overlap`
   which is inclusive over whole ranges and calls every accumulator contended).

RESULT (`IR_IVACC`, default-on; `IR_IVACC=0` / `--opt-disable=iv-acc` opts out):
  - corpus **-462 B, 22 cells smaller, ZERO larger** — every CPU, both modes.
    Only predbench changes. 0 aborts.
  - predbench ticks **16/16 cells FASTER, none slower, -3.55 % aggregate**
    (gbz80 -4.80 %, 8085 -4.32 %, kc160 -3.85 %, z180 sp -3.56 %). Bytes and
    cycles move TOGETHER, so there is no byte-for-tick trade to arbitrate.
  - emu.c -11 B (23244 -> 23233). adv_a / clisp / enigma byte-identical.
  - `IR_IVACC=0` byte-identical to the pre-change compiler on all 660 cells.

►► WIDTHBENCH IS NOT FIXED, and this is the honest finding: `mix_char`'s
   accumulator IS contended, so it is refused. Its -15 B fp / -2.7 % ticks needs
   the ARBITER to rank two competing BC candidates properly — that is §5.2, the
   standing shipping blocker, and the same item as §5's "ranker's ordering of two
   competing BC candidates". A wider gate here cannot get it without dragging in
   divbench/shiftbench/fixedbench. Do not re-try the gate; go at the arbiter.

METHOD NOTE, and an invariant nearly broken: splitting the hotness test out of
`iv_home_realizable` de-synced `home_realizable` from pool membership, which
IR_HR_CHECK asserts as EXACT equality — it would have started false-alarming for
every admitted candidate. Fixed properly rather than documented away: the
contention test now SKIPS the IV arm's own CF_SPECULATIVE candidates, which makes
it independent of pool order (the arm runs last, so generation only ever sees a
prefix) and lets the query reproduce it from the full pool. IR_HR_CHECK verified
0 mismatches over 12 benches x both modes. The split itself was proven
codegen-neutral (660/660 identical) BEFORE the behaviour change went in.

asm differs with IR_IVACC=0 (a frame-slot round trip disappears); it also pins
the REJECT paths (`mix`, `pick`) so a future widening cannot silently break them.
