5/9/2026 (s3b) — the deleted fold RECOVERED soundly as `gwiden`, in ir_lower
            where A-liveness is a fact. emu.c -37 B both modes (a THIRD of what
            the deletion cost); corpus unchanged; the rest is genuinely unsafe.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
`gw_fold_byte_global_widens` in ir_lower.c does what the copt rule did —
`ld a,(_g); ld l,a; ld h,0` -> `ld hl,(_g); ld h,0` — but only where A is
provably dead after. It runs as a pre-pass inside `filter_dead_bc_parks`, the
post-render backward sweep that already computes per-line B/C/D/E/F liveness,
because that is the ONLY place in the pipeline with real liveness over the
emitted text.

DELIBERATELY INVALIDATE-BY-DEFAULT, the OPPOSITE polarity to the A-carry tracker
in the same file. There an unrecognised line costs BYTES; here it would cost
CORRECTNESS. So `gw_a_dead_after` concludes "dead" only by REACHING a proven
killer (`ld a,<x>`, `pop af`, `xor a`) with every intervening line on a proven
no-read list. Any branch, any call, any unknown mnemonic answers LIVE.

WHAT IT RECOVERS, and why not more:
  emu.c 23281 -> 23244 sp, 22794 -> 22757 fp = -37 B each, of the -111/-105 the
  deletion cost. 62 of the 80 sites stay unfolded and SHOULD: the blocker is
  `call` (13x `push hl; call _set_arg2`, 7x `call _set_info`, ...). A call is NOT
  safe to treat as killing A, even though no z88dk convention passes a general
  argument there — because the lowerer's A-carry can ELIDE a byte-arg `ld a,l`
  when it believes A already holds the value, leaving A live into the call with
  NO visible write. That is the exact shape of the bug just fixed. `xline_c_call`
  reasons this way for BC and is sound there; the same argument does not
  transfer to A.

  Also note the fold now runs BEFORE copt, so copt rules that CREATE the shape
  later (e.g. #285p) are out of reach. That is part of the residual too.

MEASURED: corpus 660/660 cells UNCHANGED and 0 aborts — the shape does not occur
in any bench, which is why the deleted rule cost nothing there and why a tick
matrix would be all-zero. Real files: only emu.c fires it (adv_a, clisp, enigma,
main.c are 0). No byte-for-tick trade — `ld hl,(nn); ld h,0` is 23 T against
`ld a,(nn); ld l,a; ld h,0` at 24 T, so bytes and cycles move together.

gbz80 EXCLUDED: it has no `ld hl,(nn)`, and the z80asm synthetic is longer AND
goes through A — the very register the fold is spending.

GATES: long_ir 681/681 sp AND fp (clean rebuild each); enigma RXSEC both modes;
emu.c 2 hits both modes; `IR_GWIDEN=0` and `--opt-disable=gwiden` BOTH reproduce
the no-fold sizes exactly (23281/22794).

long_ir/copta.c now gates BOTH directions, each proven load-bearing:
  - must NOT fire where A is live — make `gw_a_dead_after` return 1 and copta
    fails at copta.c:73 (run, confirmed).
  - must STILL fire where A is dead — array_elem() folds `ld a,(_A2+2); ld l,a`
    to `ld hl,(_A2+2)`, so gate-on vs gate-off asm genuinely differs.

5/9/2026 (s3) — the stale-A miscompile is FIXED. It was never in narrow-byte:
            a COPT RULE deleted a LIVE definition of A. Rule removed, 0 corpus
            bytes, +111B emu.c. Regression long_ir/copta.c.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE PREVIOUS SECTION BLAMED THE WRONG PASS. `ir_opt_narrow_byte` is INNOCENT and
was never patched. 80cc's own output for the repro is CORRECT:

    ld a,(_W)            ; A := 0xEF
    ld l,a  ; ld h,0     ; a = 239
    pop de  ; push hl
    ld l,a  ; ld h,0     ; b = 239   <- A still live and still right

The wrong answer is introduced AFTER the compiler, by `lib/80cc_rules.1`:

    ld a,(_%1) / ld l,a / ld h,0   ==>   ld hl,(_%1) / ld h,0

Its comment claimed "A is left untouched". THE OPPOSITE IS TRUE: the fold deletes
the only instruction that PUT the byte in A, so the SECOND widen reads whatever A
held before. narrow-byte's only role is to produce the byte-load shape the rule
matches, which is why `--opt-disable=narrow-byte` masked it and sent the last
session into ir_opt.c.

  METHOD NOTE, and the reason a session was spent in the wrong file: DIFF THE
  COMPILER'S OWN OUTPUT (`z88dk-80cc -m<cpu> -o x.asm`) AGAINST THE LINKED ASM
  (`zcc -a`) BEFORE OPENING ANY PASS. copt sits between them and is invisible to
  every IR dump. `IR_DUMP_ALLOC` was clean here and told us nothing.

FIX = the rule is DELETED. There is no sound guard: copt has no liveness, and a 4-line window cannot prove A dead. The
80 fire sites in emu.c are followed by `push hl` (36, proves nothing), `call`
(21, and A can be a byte-arg register), `and n` / `ld a,l` (6, which READ A).

PRICE, measured both ways:
  - bench corpus 30 x 11 CPUs x sp/fp = 660 cells: **BYTE-IDENTICAL**, and the
    rule fires ZERO times anywhere in it.
  - emu.c: +111 B sp / +105 B fp (23170->23281, 22689->22794). The only real
    file that fires it: adv_a, clisp, enigma, main.c are all 0.
  So the fold IS worth ~0.5% on one real file. RECOVERING IT belongs in
  ir_lower's post-render backward sweep (`filter_dead_bc_parks`), which already
  computes real per-line B/C/D/E/F liveness — add an A track and do the fold
  there, where "is A dead after this line" is a fact rather than a guess.

TREE STATE CHANGE: `src/80cc/ir_alloc.c` is now CLEAN at HEAD. The maintainer's
uncommitted `IR_FPIDX_PROBE` (which earlier handovers said to leave alone) was
lifted out to `src/80cc/FPIDX_PROBE.patch.txt` and reverted from the working
file, on request. The patch is verified to re-apply (`git apply --check`), and
the probe was INERT (env-gated, gate untouched) so nothing it did is lost. The
compiler was rebuilt + installed from the reverted source and re-validated:
corpus 660/660 byte-identical to the pre-revert compiler, long_ir 681/681 sp AND
fp, enigma RXSEC both modes, emu.c 2 hits both modes at unchanged sizes
(30425 sp / 29942 fp). Re-apply with `git apply src/80cc/FPIDX_PROBE.patch.txt`.

AUDIT of the other 24 A-touching rules in the file: no second instance. Several
folds DO change A (#G1 #S1 #S2 #285s #285t #285u #Z2 #RMW1), but every one only
drops an INCIDENTAL clobber — A is a scratch temp inside a word-load or
byte-swap idiom, so the lowerer already treats it as dead. The deleted rule was
the only one deleting a LIVE definition. That asymmetry is the thing to check
when reviewing any new rule: dropping a clobber is safe, dropping a def is not.

GATES, all green with the fix:
  - long_ir 681/681 sp AND fp, from a CLEAN `rm -f *.bin` build in each mode.
    The only Error 1 is the pre-existing longshl_vm1 (KR580VM1 has no assembler).

    restore the rule and it fails at copta.c:73. Its `single_widen` control
    passes with the bug present, so it pins the ordinary case separately.

5/9/2026 (audit) — nodes_equivalent audited (CLEAN), but the differential sweep
            found a SECOND silent miscompile: `narrow-byte` leaves a STALE A
            CLAIM, so `(unsigned char)global` can come back 0. NOT YET FIXED.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE AUDIT ITSELF CAME BACK CLEAN. After the OP_CAST fix (`cc7c5d6dc0`), 24 shapes
where one operand appears under two different TYPE contexts were built three ways
— default, `--opt-disable=cse`, `--opt-disable=cse-synth` — and all three agree
on every shape: different cast widths, same width different signedness, equal
literal values of different types, UNION members at one address, BITFIELDS
sharing a unit, one index into arrays of different element size, an impure call
twice (must not fold), a volatile read twice (must not fold), address vs value,
nested casts in both orders, one pointer deref'd through two pointee types, two
struct members of different width, address-of two members, pointer difference.
**No further type-blindness found in nodes_equivalent.**

►► BUT THE SWEEP FOUND THIS, which is not a CSE bug at all:

  unsigned int W = 0xBEEFu;                        /* a GLOBAL */
  unsigned int a = (unsigned char)(unsigned int)W;   /* 239  correct */
  unsigned int b = (unsigned char)W;                 /* 0    WRONG   */

`--opt-disable=narrow-byte` fixes it; `--opt-disable=cse` does NOT. sdcc gets
both right (239/239). **NB sccz80 miscompiles the OTHER one** on the same source
(a = 48879, ignoring the inner truncation) — a separate, pre-existing sccz80 bug.

MECHANISM, from the asm diff — a STALE A CLAIM:

  narrow-byte OFF (correct)        narrow-byte ON (wrong)
    ld hl,(_W)                       ld hl,(_W)
    ld bc,hl                         ld h,0        ; a = 239, uses L directly
    ld a,l      ; A := 0xEF          ...
    ld h,0      ; a = 239            ld l,a        ; <-- A WAS NEVER SET
    ...                              ld h,0        ; b = garbage
    ld hl,bc
    ld a,l      ; A := 0xEF
    ld h,0      ; b = 239

Narrowing lets the FIRST conversion use L directly, so the `ld a,l` that used to
establish A is never emitted — but the SECOND conversion still reads A. The byte
cache claims A for a vreg without loading it. Same family as the IR_A_CARRY
"invalidate-by-default A tracker" work.

REACH (measured): **globals and ARRAY ELEMENTS are hit; locals and PARAMETERS are
not**, and the result must be widened back to int (`unsigned char` destinations
are fine). It needs TWO narrowing conversions of the same value that are
STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT — identical ones are safe only because CSE folds them to a
single computation, which is why two plain `(unsigned char)W` reads look fine.

NOT FIXED. The pass (`ir_opt_narrow_byte`, ir_opt.c) is large and heavily guarded;
this needs its own session. `--opt-disable=narrow-byte` is the workaround.
No long_ir case pins it yet.

►► METHOD NOTE, twice-burned: an EMPTY comparison reads as a PASS. Two of the
sweep runs "matched" only because the binaries had not built (a float case needed
a maths library) or because piping `z88dk-ticks` into `grep` LOST buffered lines —
the same trap AGENTS.md documents for emu.c. ALWAYS capture ticks output to a file
first and PRINT THE LINE COUNT before trusting a diff.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
5/9/2026 (§5.4 stage 1) — narrow a truncated long shift: -102 B, 0 cells larger,
            widthbench -3.5% ticks. AND A SILENT MISCOMPILE FOUND AND FIXED:
            ast_cse treated two casts of one expression as the same expression
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
►► THE MISCOMPILE IS THE IMPORTANT PART. Found by writing a DIFFERENTIAL test
while validating something else — not by any existing gate.

  unsigned char a3 = (unsigned char)(v>>3);   /* 207   correct */
  unsigned int  s3 = (unsigned int)(v>>3);    /* 35535 expected, GOT 207 */

Either cast ALONE is correct; sharing the subexpression breaks it.
`--opt-disable=cse` fixes it, a bogus flag name does not, sccz80 and sdcc are
both right, and it reproduces with `IR_BCCALLCOST=0` — so it is old, not new.

CAUSE, in `nodes_equivalent` (ast_opt.c): OP_CAST sat in the operand-only group

    case OP_NEG: case OP_COMP: case OP_LNEG:
    case OP_CAST:                              <-- compares a->operand only
    case OP_ADDR:  case AST_ADDR:

so `(unsigned char)X` and `(unsigned int)X` were the SAME expression and ast_cse
substituted the byte for the int. **This is precisely the bfcse.c bitfield bug
one node type along** — the OP_DEREF case immediately above already documents
"a 1-bit flag read back as its 12-bit neighbour". Fixed by comparing the target
type's kind, size and isunsigned. Commit `cc7c5d6dc0`.

►► COST: **ZERO. All 660 corpus cells byte-identical.** The bad CSE fires nowhere
in the corpus — which is also why nothing caught it. long_ir 671/671 sp AND fp,
enigma/clisp/adv_a/sorter clean.

►► THE GATE GAP THIS EXPOSES: long_ir, the corpus and the behavioural gates ALL
missed a silent wrong-answer bug. New regression `castcse.bin`/`castcse_fp.bin`
(sibling of bfcse), PROVEN to catch it: reverting the fix fails it at
castcse.c:72, restoring it passes. Covers narrow-then-wide, wide-then-narrow,
signedness-only-at-equal-width, and a long beside an int, plus a single-cast
control that passes either way.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STAGE 1 ITSELF — [IR_SHRNARROW=1], opt-in. A width-4 CONSTANT shift whose SOLE
use is a following CONV_TRUNC needs only the bytes the truncation keeps: result
byte i is source bits [8i+K, 8i+K+8), so a W-byte result needs only source bytes
[K/8, (K+8W-1)/8]. The lowering already trimmed the LOW bytes (byte_shift); this
is the symmetric HIGH trim, with the shift body re-indexed by an active-byte
count so the untrimmed path is unchanged.

SAFETY: the high result bytes are left ZERO, i.e. WRONG. The guard is therefore a
WHOLE-FUNCTION single-use test, NOT a dead-store or in-BB test —
`cur_dehl_dst_dead_safe` only means no SLOT read is needed, and a second reader
can be served from the DEHL cache. Valid for logical AND arithmetic shifts: the
surviving low bytes depend only on source bits [K, K+8W).

RESULT (660 cells; only widthbench moves — the only bench with this shape):

  size   -102 B    16 cells smaller, ZERO larger
         z80 -17  z80n -17  z180 -17  gbz80 -18  ez80 -11  kc160 -7  rabbit -5 ea.
  ticks  widthbench z80 sp -2.97%, fp -3.50%

►► TWO SIZE REGRESSIONS FOUND AND FIXED EN ROUTE, both the same lesson — a
hand-rolled loader must not replace a target's NATIVE addressing:
  (1) rabbit/kc160 read a word off sp in ONE 2-byte op (`ld hl,(sp+n)`); the
      generic add-hl-sp walk cost +13 B a cell on rabbit, +9 on kc160.
  (2) fp: `ld hl,(ix+d)` is native/short on ez80/rabbit/kc160 and synthesised to
      the same two byte loads on z80 — hand-rolling the halves cost bytes.
  (3) A 3-BYTE window has no native form, so on a target that reads a word off sp
      in one op the staging walk costs more than trimming the 4th byte saves.
      DECLINED there. After all three: every cell smaller or equal.

GATES: long_ir 671/671 sp AND fp with the gate on; widthbench checksum passes on
every CPU measured; gate-off unchanged.

►► FINISHED AND FLIPPED DEFAULT-ON (`IR_SHRNARROW=0` opts out). Both items that
were left on the table are now in, and together they DOUBLED the win:

  (a) TWO-ENDED WINDOW. The shift's low trim and the truncation's high trim now
      combine, so `v >> 11` (byte_shift 1 AND a high trim) is covered.
  (b) DIRECTION FLIP, which is what sdcc does. Past K%8 == 4, shifting the
      2-byte window LEFT by 8-K and keeping byte 1 beats shifting right:
      `add hl,hl` is ONE byte against the two-op `srl h; rr l`. K=5 goes from
      5x(srl h; rr l) to 3x`add hl,hl` plus `ld l,h`. Single-byte results only —
      a wider one needs two bytes off the top, which `ld l,h` cannot deliver.

FINAL: size **-257 B over 660 cells, 18 smaller, ZERO larger**, every CPU better
(gbz80 -38, z80/z80n/z180 -32, kc160 -30, ez80 -29, r2ka -24, r4k/r6k -20).
Ticks on widthbench: z80 -6.35/-7.14 %, ez80 -7.40/-11.21 %, kc160 -10.24/-11.13 %,
gbz80 -7.42 %, r2ka -5.63/-5.30 %.

GATES: long_ir **673/673 sp AND fp**; enigma RXSEC both modes tick-identical;
clisp 6/42; adv_a; sorter; fib; **emu.c "On The Path" x2 in BOTH modes**;
`IR_SHRNARROW=0` byte-identical to the pre-change compiler and the default
reproduces the measured gate-on scan exactly (both verified by full re-scan).
Plus an exhaustive differential: every shift count 0..31 x 8 values x both result
widths = 256 outputs, matching a reference on 6 CPUs x 2 frame modes.

►► A TEST THAT WAS DECORATION, CAUGHT BY THE GAUNTLET'S OWN TRAP #4. The first
`shrnarrow.c` was byte-identical with the gate on and off: it loaded the long
from a GLOBAL straight into DEHL, and the narrowing only fires on a SLOT-homed
source (`!dehl_has`). Rewritten to take the long as a PARAMETER it moves 127 asm
lines. **Always diff gate-on against gate-off asm before believing a new test.**

►► THE emu.c GATE IS ~8 s, NOT ~6 min — USE `-w 1`. The game finishes its work in
well under 400M cycles; the rest is ticks spinning on the blocked quit-confirm
until the budget runs out, and wall time scales LINEARLY with -w (3 s at -w 1,
16 s at -w 5, ~3 min at -w 60). Two false-pass traps found while running it, both
now in AGENTS.md: the game data `pawn.mag` is read from the CWD (elsewhere it
exits in under a second with 0 hits, looking like a crash), and a FAILED `zcc -o`
leaves a previous session's binary in place for the gate to measure and pass.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
5/9/2026 (later) — §5.4 OPENED on widthbench: the gap is a SPILLED ACCUMULATOR
            because HL is not allocatable; and the corpus scan scripts were
            BLIND to this benchmark
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
►► FIRST, A COVERAGE DEFECT. `corpus_sizescan.sh` / `corpus_tickscan.sh` list 29
benchmarks; BENCH_MATRIX measures 30. The missing one is **widthbench** — the
single bench the 5/9 handover names as the best §5.4 target. Every corpus scan in
this and previous sessions was blind to it. Added to both scripts. Anything
touching byte residency would have measured as "no corpus change" and been
believed. (The other unscanned dirs — imath, math, regex, spectralnorm, long_ir —
are separate suites, not corpus benches.)

THE GAP, re-measured (80cc vs sdcc -SO2, whole binary, ticks):

  z80  sp +61.3%   z80n sp +68.7%   z180 sp +73.6%
  z80  fp +48.8%   z80n fp +55.6%   z180 fp +46.1%

WORSE than the 3/9 table recorded (+49/+55/+46) and the largest gap in the corpus.

THE DIFFERENCE, named from `mix_char` asm (39 lines sdcc vs 79 lines 80cc):
**sdcc loads the two chars ONCE into b and c and never touches memory again.**
80cc stores each to a frame slot at the point of load and RELOADS it at every
use — in sp mode each byte reload is `ld hl,N; add hl,sp; ld a,(hl)`, four
instructions to reach a byte. Same disease as the operand-residency frontier,
in its BYTE form.

►► REFUTED BY EXPERIMENT: the `use_count >= 8` gate in byte_home_realizable is
NOT the binding constraint. Thresholds 8/4/2 are byte-identical; at 1 it fires and
widthbench gets SLOWER (+0.09%). The gate is RIGHT — those byte vregs have one use
each, and a one-use value in a register saves nothing. Do not retry this.

►► THE ACTUAL DIAGNOSIS, from the POST-OPT IR (`IR_DUMP_ALLOC`), which corrects a
first reading taken from HOMEMAP alone. CSE has ALREADY done the byte-residency
job: `s` is ONE vreg (v2) with exactly ONE use, because the second read of `s` was
rewritten to reuse the widened value (`MOV v14 <- v9[BC]`). v2/v11/v14 sharing
slot 2 is ordinary slot COALESCING of three DISJOINT unrelated temps — NOT one
variable split across vregs. There is no byte-residency defect here.

THE GAP IS REGISTER PRESSURE, AND ONE FACT NAMES IT: **the accumulator is
spilled.** mix_char has 17 vregs; BC carries v1 then v9, DE takes the short
conversions, and `acc` (v8, live [8,19], FIVE references) lands in a FRAME SLOT.
Every `acc +=` is therefore a slot RMW reached by `ld hl,N; add hl,sp` — 8 such
address formations in 80cc's mix_char against ZERO in sdcc's (its two `add sp`
hits are the ix prologue).

sdcc fits the identical computation entirely in registers: `acc` lives in HL for
the whole function, the two source bytes live in B and C, and DE takes each
widened form transiently. **80cc cannot do that because HL is not allocatable** —
it is the transient staging bus, so any value live across statements must reach
BC, DE or a slot. That is the difference, and it is architectural.

►► SO THIS IS THE HL-RESIDENCY / SINGLE-HOME problem (memory
`operand-residency-frontier`), reached from a new direction, NOT a byte-home
problem. The pair-allocator "no opportunity" verdict
(`pair-allocator-no-opportunity`) is NOT overturned by widthbench: mix_char's byte
vregs are one-use and genuinely not worth homing. Two byte homes would only help
once HL residency freed BC/DE — the cap is downstream of the real blocker.

►► BUT THE ACCUMULATOR IS NOT THE MAIN GAP — MEASURED. The accumulator falls in a
GAP between two predicates: `bc_home_realizable` demands `write_count == 1` (an
accumulator has 4), and `iv_home_realizable` demands `use_count >= 8` (it has 4).
Instrumented: `IVWHY mix_char v8 w=4 u=4 REJECT cold`. Closing the gap is a REAL
but SMALL win — widthbench fp 52.07M -> 50.74M (-2.5%), size 909 -> 894; sp
-0.3% / +3 B. Worth doing, nowhere near the 48-74% gap.

►► THE DOMINANT LEVER, from the mix_store asm: **sdcc NARROWS BEFORE SHIFTING;
80cc shifts the full width then truncates.**

  sbuf[k] = (signed char)(v >> 5);      /* v is unsigned long */

  sdcc   loads only the LOW 16 BITS of v (`ld l,(ix+6); ld h,(ix+7)`) and does
         `xor a,a; add hl,hl; rla` x3, taking `h` — only 8 bits survive the cast,
         so it shifts the OTHER WAY by 8-5=3 on a 16-bit value.
  80cc   `ld b,5; srl d; rr e; rr h; rr l; djnz` — all 32 bits, 5 iterations,
         20 shift ops plus loop overhead, THEN truncates.

  Likewise `(unsigned char)(v >> 11)`: sdcc loads a 3-BYTE WINDOW (ix+7,8,9) and
  shifts 3; 80cc shifts 32 bits by 11.

The rule: for `(narrow_t)(wide >> K)` with K constant, only the byte window
[K/8, K/8 + sizeof(narrow_t)] is needed and the residual shift is K%8. Pure
lowering/IR work, not allocation.

NOT on WIDTH_HANDOVER.md's "Do NOT re-open" list — that covers PUSH_ARG
narrowing, DEBC long homes, the BC=low stash, PUSH_DEHL_LONG, argument order,
global-value caching and frame residency. Shift-feeding-truncation is fresh.

►► DECOMPOSITION — **CORRECTED 5/9 (later), the first one was WRONG.** It used
HARDCODED asm line ranges and captured 91 lines of a 364-line width_compute
against 100 of sdcc's 187, producing the false claim "the driving loop is already
BETTER than sdcc (0.91x), the entire gap is in the three helpers". Counted
properly, from label to label with identical rules on both files, AFTER stage 1:

  mix_char       72 / 35  = 2.06x      mix_store     107 /  62 = 1.73x
  mix_long       93 / 50  = 1.86x      width_compute 358 / 183 = 1.96x
  TOTAL         630 / 330 = 1.91x

**The gap is UNIFORM at ~1.9x across ALL FOUR functions — it is not localized to
the conversion helpers.** width_compute is the single biggest ABSOLUTE
contributor (+175 lines, more than the three helpers combined at +125) and
carries 34 `add hl,sp`, the sp-mode frame tax. LESSON: never decompose by
hardcoded line ranges; find the label boundaries.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
5/9/2026 — §5.1 CLOSED: the ez80/rabbit IR_PREPUSH_NARROW regression is a MISSING
            COST, not a missing recovery. IR_BCCALLCOST DEFAULT-ON, -92 B and
            12 cells faster / 0 slower. New: g0_word_bytes, a SIZE companion to
            g0_word_cost — and ez80 fp cannot tell a register from a slot
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE DIAGNOSIS. The 5/9 handover's §5.1 said the IR_BCSAVE_LIVE recovery "does not
fire" on ez80/rabbit. It fires correctly. The saves it leaves are REQUIRED: in
shiftbench's `shift_compute` the accumulator `chk` is genuinely live across all
seven calls in the inner loop, so every `push bc` / `pop bc` is real. The home
should never have been taken.

The defect is one level up. The arbiter's RC_BC arm has NO benefit gate at all —
unlike the index arm's grounded `idx_ben <= 0` reject — and interval_benefit
prices the accesses a register home saves while charging NOTHING for the call
saves the home forces. IR_RANKDUMP on shift_compute:

  z80  fp   ben 11068   slot is dear, BC wins anyway; chk gets a call-free RANGED home
  ez80 sp   ben  1804   earns its saves
  ez80 fp   ben   256   seven pairs x weight 16 — a clear loss

►► THAT IS WHY ALL NINE ez80 CELLS WERE fp, the clue the handover flagged. The
ez80 fp slot is a native `ld hl,(ix+d)` (2 cyc) against sp's 8, so the SAME home
is worth a quarter as much in fp while the save cost is unchanged.

THE FIX. [IR_BCCALLCOST=<margin>] charges a whole-function BC home the
depth-weighted push/pop pair for every call inside its live range, and declines
the home when the charge sinks it. Because IR_BCSAVE_LIVE emits a pair on exactly
the calls a tenant is live across, "calls in the live range" IS the emitted code,
not an estimate. Declining does not spill the value — ir_bc_pack and the
call-bounded split still place it over a call-free range, which is the home z80
already gives it.

►► THE BYTE TERM IS WHAT MADE IT SHIPPABLE. Charging cycles alone is a
byte-for-tick trade, and a bad one:

  cycles only, margin 1    ticks 74 faster / 21 slower    size  +701 B
  cycles only, margin 2    ticks 28 faster /  1 slower    size  +332 B
  + byte term, margin 2    ticks 14 faster /  1 slower    size  -119 B

g0_word_bytes is a new SIZE companion to g0_word_cost — same [reg][kind] shape,
same fp/sp adjustment — with every number MEASURED by assembling the idiom the
lowerer emits (`z88dk-z80asm -m<cpu> -b`, byte count of the binary):

  BC read/write `ld l,c; ld h,b`     2 everywhere      push bc / pop bc   1 + 1
  BC deref      `ld a,(bc)`          1 (gbz80: 3, no such op)
  slot fp       `ld hl,(ix-2)`       z80 6   ez80 3   RABBIT 2   kc160 3
  slot sp       `ld hl,n; add hl,sp` 8;  rabbit `ld hl,(sp+n)` 2;  gbz80 5

►► THE RABBIT ROW IS WHY THE TABLE HAS TO EXIST. Its `ld hl,(ix+d)` and
`ld hl,(sp+n)` are BOTH two bytes — the same as the `ld l,c; ld h,b` a BC home
costs — so on rabbit a call-spanning BC home saves ZERO bytes an access and still
pays two at every call. It is byte-NEGATIVE. On ez80 the same home is
byte-POSITIVE (+1 an access, 3 vs 2). The cycle model cannot see the difference
and rates them alike, which is exactly why charging cycles alone made rabbit
smaller and ez80 +424 B larger. Bytes are STATIC and are summed with NO loop
weighting — a body inside a loop is not bigger.

The rule: decline only when the home loses on BOTH axes. A home that loses cycles
but SAVES bytes is a trade the allocator has no mandate to make on its own.

FINAL, `IR_BCCALLCOST=2` (638 size cells, 224 tick cells on ez80+3 rabbits):

  size   -119 B   16 cells smaller, 8 larger, worst +4 B (md5 r4k/r6k sp)
         r2ka -48   r4k -20   r6k -20   ez80 -27   kc160 -4
         z80 / z80n / z180 / 8080 / 8085 / gbz80 BYTE-IDENTICAL
  ticks  14 faster, 1 slower
         r2ka -0.243%   r4k -0.208%   r6k -0.214%   ez80 -0.025%
         best  queenbench ez80 fp -2.81, divbench r2ka sp -2.79,
               bitfieldbench r2ka sp -2.73, divbench r6k sp -2.75

Smaller AND faster on every CPU that moves. Margin 2 is load-bearing: margin 1
fires too widely (21 slower cells) and margin 3 stops the rabbits moving at all.

GATES: long_ir 671/671 sp AND 671/671 fp with the gate on (only the pre-existing
`longshl_vm1.bin`, no VM1 assembler); enigma RXSEC both modes, tick-identical;
clisp 6 and 42; adv_a intro; clisp/adv_a code_compiler unchanged. GATE-OFF IS
BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-change compiler on all 638 cells — proved by stripping
the hunks, rebuilding and re-scanning, not by inspection.

►► THE OUTLIER THAT BLOCKED DEFAULT-ON, AND THE REAL DEFECT UNDER IT.
hashbench ez80 fp read +1.76%. IR_RANKDUMP on `ht_lookup` explains it: all four
BC candidates rate ben=0. On ez80 fp `g0_word_cost` prices an fp slot read
(native `ld hl,(ix+d)`) at 2 cycles and a BC read at 2 cycles — IDENTICAL — so
interval_benefit rates EVERY candidate 0 and the arbiter's stable sort breaks the
tie by POOL ORDER, not merit. Acting on a benefit the model cannot compute is a
coin flip: it wins queenbench ez80 fp 2.81% and loses hashbench 1.76% on the same
CPU, mode and shape.

REFUTED en route: excluding PARAMs. It fixes hashbench (+1.76 -> 0.00) but kills
most of the wins (queenbench ez80 -2.81 -> 0, divbench r2ka -2.79 -> 0,
queenbench r4k -1.54 -> 0) because the winners are the SAME shape. Also refuted:
declining only when BC would go unused (the pool is sorted by benefit descending,
so an inheritor always ranks BELOW the declined candidate) — that substitution is
BENEFICIAL in bitfieldbench (-2.7%) and HARMFUL in hashbench and vecbench, and
forbidding it costs nearly every win.

THE FIX, AND IT IS ONE LINE: only act where the cycle model can SEE a difference,
`g0_word_cost(GR_SLOT,GK_READ) > g0_word_cost(GR_BC,GK_READ)`. Principled, not a
CPU special-case. ez80 fp goes inert (slot 2 == BC 2); rabbit (11/9 vs 4) and
kc160 (4 vs 2) keep everything. Costs ez80's whole contribution, which was -27 B
and -0.025% ticks — noise. NB the byte term had ALREADY conceded shiftbench ez80
fp, the original §5.1 exhibit: that home is byte-POSITIVE, so declining it is a
byte-for-tick trade we decline to make.

►► FLIPPED DEFAULT-ON at margin 2 (`IR_BCCALLCOST=0` opts out):

  size   -92 B    12 cells smaller, 8 larger, worst +4 B (md5 r4k/r6k sp)
         r2ka -48   r4k -20   r6k -20   kc160 -4
         ez80 AND the other seven CPUs BYTE-IDENTICAL
  ticks  12 faster, ZERO slower
         r2ka -1.000%   r4k -0.928%   r6k -0.964%   ez80 0.000%   kc160 0.000%

Footprint is four benches (bitfieldbench, divbench, md5, queenbench) on four CPUs.
md5 was NOT in the first tick subset though it moves on size — measured
separately, faster on all 8 cells. GATES on the shipped rule: long_ir 671/671 sp
AND fp; enigma RXSEC both modes tick-identical; clisp 6/42; adv_a intro; sorter
ordered; `IR_BCCALLCOST=0` byte-identical to the pre-change compiler on all 638
cells, and the default reproduces the measured gate-on scan exactly.

►► THE FOLLOW-ON THIS EXPOSED, and it is bigger than the lever: the ez80 fp row
of g0_word_cost CANNOT SEPARATE A REGISTER FROM A SLOT (both 2). Every ez80 fp
register-allocation decision is therefore settled by tie-break order rather than
cost. Giving that row real discrimination — a slot consumes a frame slot, needs
the frame pointer, and cannot serve `ld a,(bc)` — is the same treatment the gbz80
row already got, and it is the prerequisite for ever taking the ez80 fp cases.
Belongs with §5.2, not here.

3/9/2026 — both 80cc columns re-measured after the call-clobber density arc; every
            one of the 600 cells is smaller than it was on 31/8; the sweep found
            a 10% z80 regression, fixed here, and a stale rabbit tick baseline
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MEASURED FRESH: 80cc-fp and 80cc-sp, 30 benchmarks x 12 CPUs = 360 rows / 600
numeric cells, built and run with `gen_bench_matrix_vm1.py`. Every cell builds,
runs and passes its checksum — no BUILD, HANG, WRONG or RUN in the whole sweep.
ALSO MEASURED FRESH: sccz80 + sdcc for r2ka/r4k/r6k (180 cells, the rabbit ticks
predate a ticks fix), and sdcc + sdcc-max for z80/z80n/z180/gbz80 (120 cells,
their ticks had drifted in sdcc's favour). CARRIED FORWARD: sccz80 outside rabbit
— deliberately, it drifted a constant +122 B with ticks unchanged — plus xcc -Os
and xcc -Of everywhere.

  ticks   301 cells faster by >0.5%, 37 slower by >0.5%, 262 level within +-0.5%
  size    net -69191 B; 0 cells bigger, 600 smaller

The tick counts are NOT a straight diff against the table below: the rabbit rows
are re-baselined, for the reason under READ THE RABBIT ROWS WITH CARE.

►► THE SIZE COLUMN IS COMPARABLE WITH THE PREVIOUS TABLE'S, and this time the
whole of it is the compiler. The 31/8 table had to warn that its +17.5 KB was the
div32/16 fastpath entering the link rather than anything the commits did, so the
same question was asked first here: the 31/8-era compiler (`cdaea84a31`) was
rebuilt and re-run on TODAY's tree, and it reproduces the previous table cell for
cell — charbench z80 5097/5108, z180 5073/5092, 8080 5708, 8085 5317, sieve z80
11837, divbench 8080 5019. Nothing in the tree, the libraries or the link moved.

►► THE SWEEP EARNED ITS KEEP: structbench z80/z80n sp WAS +10.5%, AND IS FIXED.
The first sweep showed the only large regression outside the rabbit/ez80 group:

  structbench z80  sp   3.61M -> 3.99M  +10.53%     structbench z80n sp  +9.72%

`walk()` IS that benchmark — one loop over an array of 3-int structs. Bisecting
the 31 commits put it on the FIRST one after the previous table, `36da801581`
("a byte-walk compare needs a slot, not just a spill"), a correctness fix that
stops a NO_SLOT rematerialisable constant reaching a byte-walk compare as
`ld hl,-1; add hl,sp`. It guarded on `vreg_spill_slot[v] < 0` — but a PARAMETER
is homed in the CALLER's frame, so it has no spill slot (-1) while `slot_off`
returns a perfectly good offset. `i < n` therefore lost its byte-walk compare,
the bound went to DE for `sbc hl,de`, and that evicted the running sum `s` from
its DE home to a stack-transient one: three `pop hl / add hl,de / push hl` pairs
per iteration where the old code did `add hl,de / ex de,hl`.

The guard now asks `slot_off(f, v) < 0` — the thing the caller actually emits
from, and what the two sibling shape tests already used. It touches exactly TWO
of 638 corpus cells, which are the two that regressed:

  structbench z80  sp   5220B / 3.61M  (31/8)   5103B / 3.99M  (before the fix)
                        5119B / 3.62M  (now: -101 B on 31/8, and the ticks back)

ptrbench — the benchmark whose miscompile `36da801581` was written for — passes
on all 9 CPUs in both modes with the narrower guard, as it must: `slot_off` is a
strictly more direct test of the condition that commit describes.

►► EVERY CELL IS SMALLER, INCLUDING ALL 37 THAT ARE SLOWER, and the 37 have ONE
cause. Median size change is -120 B on the faster cells and -95 B on the slower
ones, so these are byte-for-tick trades. After the structbench fix they are all
ez80 or rabbit:

  slower cells   r2ka 10   ez80 9   r4k 9   r6k 9   (z80 family: none)
                 37 cells, ALL smaller, -3513 B between them
  worst          shiftbench ez80 fp +4.57%, divbench ez80 fp +3.05%,
                 bitfieldbench r2ka sp +2.86%

The cause is NOT the rabbit `jr` relaxation, which is what an earlier draft of
this note guessed from the commit subjects. Bisected, on both families it is
`c8e1a7b61f` ("the pre-pushed veto narrowing and the live bc save are default, as
a pair"), and `IR_PREPUSH_NARROW=0` restores every affected cell to its 31/8
value EXACTLY — shiftbench ez80 fp 14.42 -> 13.79M, predbench r2ka sp 22.19 ->
21.66M against a 21.68M baseline, and so on for all 37.

That commit knew about these benches. Its note records that the narrowing ALONE
regresses divbench, shiftbench, bitfieldbench, strbench and structbench, and that
pairing it with IR_BCSAVE_LIVE takes them to "EXACTLY zero". It does — on z80.
On ez80 and the rabbits the recovery does not fire, so the regressions the commit
measured and dismissed survive there. **All nine ez80 cells are fp**, which is
the sharpest clue available for fixing it.

►► BUT THE GATE IS STILL RIGHT, AND THAT WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Turning
IR_PREPUSH_NARROW off across the four affected CPUs is a NET LOSS on both axes:

  rabbit   ticks +0.41 %, size +1462 B      ez80   ticks +1.12 %, size +1505 B
  worst losses from disabling it: predbench ez80 sp +14.09 %, hashbench r6k fp
  +5.82 %, strbench ez80 sp +7.14 %, callbench ez80 sp +6.46 %

So the 37 cells are a real trade the gate wins several times over on the same
CPUs, not a CPU-gating mistake. The opportunity is narrower than "turn it off":
make IR_BCSAVE_LIVE's recovery fire on ez80/rabbit fp the way it does on z80.

►► THE RABBIT ROWS ARE FULLY RE-MEASURED — 80cc, sccz80 AND sdcc.
`e1f5b719d0` ("a rabbit relative branch is its cheapest encoding, not its
dearest") landed on 2/9, AFTER the 31/8 table, so every rabbit tick in it was on
the old timing model and none of them were comparable with a fresh 80cc sweep:

  listbench r4k sp   31/8 compiler, OLD emu 16.30M (the number in the 31/8 table)
                     31/8 compiler, NEW emu 16.96M
                     today,         NEW emu 16.73M   <- a 1.4% GAIN, not a loss

Naively that cell read +2.64% SLOWER. Five of the apparent worst rabbit
regressions — listbench, structbench, recordbench and interpbench on r4k/r6k —
were entirely this artefact. So the r2ka/r4k/r6k sccz80 and sdcc columns were
re-run on today's tree and today's emulator, and the 37 slower cells above use a
rabbit baseline re-measured the same way. **The rabbit rows are now internally
consistent; no other CPU is affected** (ez80 and z80 reproduce the 31/8 table
exactly).

►► WHERE 80cc STANDS ON RABBIT, everything on one tree and one emulator:

  bytes, summed over the benches where all three build
    r2ka (28)  sccz80 153574   sdcc 173659   80cc-fp 155880   80cc-sp 154132
    r4k  (20)  sccz80 109000   sdcc 122191   80cc-fp 107948   80cc-sp 106729
    r6k  (20)  sccz80 108646   sdcc 121573   80cc-fp 107567   80cc-sp 106431

  80cc-fp vs sdcc   -10.2 % r2ka, -11.7 % r4k, -11.5 % r6k
  80cc-fp vs sccz80  +1.5 % r2ka,  -1.0 % r4k,  -1.0 % r6k
  ticks, median per cell: 80cc-sp is -45.9 % against sccz80 and +4.0 % against sdcc

That is the healthiest position 80cc has held here: SMALLER than sdcc by about a
ninth, level with sccz80 on size, and within 4 % of sdcc on speed while being
roughly twice sccz80's.

►► sdcc IS NOT A RABBIT PORT, AND THE OLD TABLE HID IT. 22 of the 90 rabbit sdcc
cells do not produce a trustworthy number: BUILD failures (sortbench r6k,
hashbench r4k/r6k, histbench ALL THREE, md5 r4k/r6k), HANGs (searchbench,
vecbench, widthbench, maskbench on r4k/r6k) and — worst — WRONG checksums
(crcbench r4k/r6k, divbench r4k/r6k, and bitfieldbench on ALL THREE including
r2ka, which IS a supported port). `gen_bench_matrix3.py` says as much in a
comment: "r4k/r6k are not sdcc ports at all". The sdcc rabbit column should be
read as indicative only, and the 68 cells that do run are what the comparison
above uses. sccz80 built and ran all 90 cleanly.

►► THE sdcc AND sdcc-max COLUMNS ARE RE-MEASURED TOO, on z80, z80n, z180 and
gbz80 (120 cells). They were re-run because the carried-forward values do not
reproduce on today's tree, and unlike the sccz80 drift they move the TICK axis —
the axis 80cc is judged on:

  sdcc      106 comparable cells   size median  +65 B   ticks median -0.14 %
  sdcc-max  100 comparable cells   size median  +47 B   ticks median -0.92 %

The medians understate it because the drift is CONCENTRATED, not uniform: **37 of
206 cells move by more than 3 %**, and almost all of them are sdcc getting
faster — interpbench gbz80 -27.6 %, listbench gbz80 -18.3 %, charbench z80
-13.3 %, rle -10.3 %, searchbench -8.1 %, intbench -6.5 %. The stale column was
therefore flattering 80cc on those cells, which is the one direction worth paying
to remove.

The exception is loud and goes the other way: **switchbench under sdcc-max is now
38 % SLOWER on z80 and z80n (37.83M -> 52.22M) and 35 % slower on z180.** Plain
sdcc barely moves on the same benchmark, so this is something in the
--max-allocs-per-node path.

►► sdcc HAS ALSO LOST GROUND ON CORRECTNESS. Three cells that carried a number
now fail their checksum, all under sdcc-max:

  maskbench z80n   5323B / 24.78M  ->  WRONG
  localbench z80   4720B / 234.74M ->  WRONG
  localbench z180  4697B / 201.06M ->  WRONG

These are not truncation: `-w 30` is 30 x 400M = 12 BILLION cycles, far beyond
any bench here. They ran to completion and returned the wrong answer. Together
with the WRONG cells the table already carried (bitfieldbench on all four CPUs,
callbench/lexbench/vecbench on z80n, queenbench/sieve/sortbench on gbz80) sdcc
now miscompiles 12 of 120 plain cells and 15 of 120 sdcc-max cells on CPUs it
genuinely supports.

**ez80 is left reading `no port`**, which the re-run confirms rather than
contradicts: all 30 benches fail to build under both sdcc profiles. **md5's three
sdcc-max cells keep their previous values** — that build takes over four minutes
and the sweep's 120 s cap recorded BUILD for it, which would have been recording
a harness limit as a compiler failure.

►► sccz80 IS DELIBERATELY NOT RE-MEASURED. It drifted too, but differently: a
CONSTANT +122 B on every bench measured (charbench, sieve, intbench, crcbench)
with ticks unchanged to five significant figures — a tick-neutral module entering
the link, never executed. Re-running 360 cells to rediscover the same +122
everywhere buys nothing; treat the sccz80 SIZE column as 122 B light and its tick
column as sound.

**Neither drift is explained.** For sdcc, every input was checked and is older
than the table: the `z88dk-zsdcc` binary (5 June), the sdcc peephole and opt rule
files (15 Aug), the libraries (30 Aug), the benchmark and framework sources, and
zcc (old and rebuilt binaries produce identical output). No flag combination
(`-SO2`, `-SO3`, `--opt-code-speed`, `--max-allocs` variants) reproduces the old
numbers. What IS established is that today's measurement is exactly reproducible
— three independent builds give byte-identical binaries and identical tick counts
— so the fresh column is trustworthy and the old one simply cannot be
regenerated. The likeliest reading is that the reference columns are older than
their heading suggests, carried forward while the tree moved under them.

►► WHERE 80cc STANDS AGAINST sdcc, now that both columns are current. Two
corrections have to be applied before this table says anything true, and both
have bitten someone in this file already.

FIRST, sdcc's binaries carry converters they never needed. sdcc does no
format-string scanning, so its map defines no `CRT_printf_format` at all and the
crt falls through to every converter there is — 197 printf symbols linked, against
80cc's scanned `$0201`. The 31/8 entry measured that inflation at **~790 B per
binary** and warned that any size comparison against sdcc is that much too
generous to 80cc. It is still true today, verified by map inspection. Every
number below has 790 B subtracted from each sdcc cell.

SECOND, **DO NOT SUM BYTES ACROSS BENCHMARKS.** md5 is three cells and 7.5 % of
the summed bytes, but 80cc beats sdcc by 38.8 % on it (17473 B against 28569 B on
z80 — an 11 KB swing per cell, where the average binary is 5.5 KB). Summing lets
those two cells cancel a steady few-percent deficit spread over the other 171 and
reports 80cc as 3.1 % larger when the truth is nearer 5 %. Weight each benchmark
equally.

  80cc-fp vs sdcc (converter-adjusted), one vote per benchmark, cells where BOTH
  pass their checksum AND sdcc actually finished:

    cpu      n   size median   size mean   ticks median   worst size bench
    r6k     17        +2.0 %      +1.9 %         +4.9 %   ptrbench    +6 %
    r4k     18        +2.2 %      +1.7 %         +0.9 %   ptrbench    +6 %
    r2ka    28        +3.4 %      +3.3 %        +10.3 %   localbench  +8 %
    z180    29        +4.6 %      +3.7 %         -7.5 %   localbench +12 %
    z80n    24        +5.2 %      +5.4 %        -10.9 %   localbench +13 %
    z80     29        +5.4 %      +4.2 %         -5.0 %   localbench +13 %
    gbz80   24       +19.7 %     +19.5 %         -1.7 %   shiftbench +29 %
    ALL    169        +4.6 %      +5.7 %         -2.0 %

**80cc is about 5 % LARGER than sdcc on size and, on ticks, level-to-slightly-
ahead** — faster on 92 of 169 cells, slower on 77. The summed-byte reading of
"-9.7 %, 80cc smaller" is what you get with both corrections skipped; excluding
md5 the summed figure moves to +5.8 %, which brackets the +4.6 % median.

►► THE TICK MEDIAN IS NEARLY MEANINGLESS ON ITS OWN — THE SPREAD IS ENORMOUS.
A median of -2 % suggests two compilers neck and neck. They are not; they are
wildly different per benchmark:

    < -20 %  ######################################## 40 cells
   -20..-5   ####################################     36
    -5..+5   ################################         32
    +5..+20  ##########################               26
    > +20 %  ###################################      35

A QUARTER of cells have 80cc more than 20 % faster and a FIFTH have it more than
20 % slower (min -60.9 %, max +80.0 %). Quote the distribution, not the median.
The worst losses cluster: widthbench (+55 % z80n, +49 % z80, +46 % z180),
queenbench r2ka +80 %, hashbench r2ka +45 %, predbench r2ka +44 %, searchbench
z180 +40 %.

►► FIVE sdcc CELLS WERE FAKE, AND THE GENERATOR LET THEM THROUGH. switchbench
r4k/r6k, maskbench r6k and localbench r4k/r6k all reported sdcc at exactly
`12000.00M` — which is not a measurement, it is the `-w 30` watchdog cap
(30 x 400M cycles). Those runs print

    ticks: stopped at counter limit (12000000002); raise -counter
    Ticks: 12000000002 (counter limit)

and NO `N run, N passed, N failed` line at all. The generator matched `Ticks:`,
found no "failed" text, and recorded a valid number — turning five sdcc hangs
into 99 %-faster wins for 80cc. They are marked HANG above. **The cell function
now rejects any run containing "counter limit" or lacking a result line.** Their
removal moved the tick MEAN from -5.2 % to -2.4 % and flipped r4k from -2.2 % to
+0.9 % and r6k from +2.1 % to +4.9 % — so all three rabbits are now at or behind
sdcc on speed, not two of them.

Checked across every sweep in this entry: the flaw touched ONLY those five sdcc
rabbit cells. All 600 80cc cells and the z80/z80n/z180/gbz80 sdcc cells are free
of it.

Two footnotes. The md5 result deserves its own look: sdcc emitting 29 KB against
80cc's 17.5 KB on one source suggests heavy unrolling rather than a like-for-like
comparison. And this is WHOLE-BINARY size on small benchmarks, so several KB of
shared runtime dilutes both sides; `emu.c`'s +21.8 % on `code_compiler` is the
undiluted measure on a real file and the one the density work is steered by. The
two are not in conflict.

►► HOW THE 80cc COLUMNS WERE PRODUCED. 31 commits landed on `src/80cc` between
the two tables — the density arc that reads what a call to C code destroys
(`1d5e3433f6` BC, `57609c8523` the flags, `b1f6df43e9`/`2bc516cdbc` following a
branch to answer it), the byte and long residency work (`8706257eaa`,
`1b3278af66`, `0515d61297`), `4e9fdadf5e` xor a, the rabbit/gbz80 cost fixes, and
two silent wrong-code fixes (`274817a030` a struct member array read past its end,
`39eace1681` block-scoped statics). TWO further changes are UNCOMMITTED in the
tree these numbers were taken from: `IR_DEFLOW`, DE liveness through the branch
fixpoint (-40 B, 8085 only), and the `slot_off` guard above.

►► A MEASUREMENT NOTE FOR ANYONE RE-RUNNING THIS. The generator names its sources
by ABSOLUTE path, and `/workspaces/z88dk/test/suites/` is 30 characters that reach
the binary through `__FILE__` in the framework's assert strings. A hand-run
command using relative paths therefore reads exactly 30 B smaller per cell and is
NOT comparable with this table — it cost an hour here, chasing a uniform -30 B
that looked like a library change and was nothing of the kind. Run the generator.
Separately, `bin/zcc` was three days behind `src/zcc` when this sweep started and
has been rebuilt; the missing commit is `911d2bb86d`, which is inside the xcc arm
of `configure_compiler` and moves no 80cc number (the sweep reproduces cell for
cell either way).

being right: the old weight counted any edge to a lower-numbered block as a
back-edge, so vm_run's switch arms read as nested loops and a 48-iteration init
loop outranked the 48024-iteration dispatch body 256:1.

  interpbench sp   ez80 -28.2%   vm1 -27.3%   z80/z80n -26.0%   z180 -25.9%
                   8080 -25.3%   8085 -20.5%   z80 fp -19.2%

►► THE +17.5 KB IS NOT THESE COMMITS, IT IS THE DIV32/16 FASTPATH.
`94fd9c55ce crt0 - rework long/int divides for DIV16_FASTMATH` puts
`l_small_divu_32_32x16` in the link, and the test framework reaches the divide
path in every benchmark, so the module lands in all 600 binaries whether the
benchmark divides or not — a near-uniform ~+30 B per cell, which is the shape
measured. `divbench 8080 sp` pins the split: 4983 B in the previous table,
5022 B with the PRE-commit compiler on today's tree, 5019 B with the new one.
The three commits take 3 B OFF that cell; the rest arrived with the fastpath.
The size column is therefore not comparable with the previous table's; the tick
column is (the fastpath is a code-size cost for a division speed win, and no
benchmark here divides in its hot loop).

►► THE FIVE SLOWER CELLS.

  queenbench ez80  sp  +3.39%    lexbench   vm1  sp  +1.43%
  queenbench r4k   fp  +1.12%    queenbench r6k  fp  +1.12%
  queenbench vm1   sp  +0.62%

Only the first was known before this sweep. The 7-CPU tick matrix these commits
were validated on covers z80, z180, 8080, 8085, ez80, gbz80 and kc160; r4k, r6k
and vm1 were outside it, so their three cells are new information — small, but
they were not in the 41-faster/1-slower figure the commits shipped against.

The ez80 cell is understood: `safe()`'s `d` sits behind `if (d < 0) d = -d;`, a
genuine ~50/50 branch that the new weight correctly discounts, and discounting it
flips a 110-vs-128 near-tie the hardware disagrees with. A cost model built from
static estimates has no better answer — a tie broken wrongly, not a defect.

lexbench is the bench these commits were written for and it lands level with the
old default on every CPU but vm1. That is the intended outcome: the corrected
loop-depth weight ALONE made lexbench 12-15% slower, and the yield plus the
conditional weight are what pay that back. `IR_MWBC=0 IR_MWBC_PRESSURE=0`
reproduces the previous codegen byte-for-byte.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
31/8/2026 (2) — the xcc columns were carrying ~800 B/binary of printf converters
                 nobody asked for; fixed, re-measured, and the same is true of
                 the sdcc columns
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MEASURED FRESH: xcc -Os and xcc -Of on z80, z80n and ez80 — 90 cells, rebuilt and
re-run after the fix below. CARRIED FORWARD: everything else from 31/8.

►► THE BUG. z88dk picks its printf/scanf converter set from a bitmask the
compiler derives by scanning the format strings; the crt reads it at
`crt_runtime_selection.inc:167` as `IF DEFINED_CRT_printf_format`. sccz80 and
80cc write that `defc` into the shared `zcc_opt.def` — a temp file handed over as
`-zcc-opt=<file>` and included globally at link time.

**xcc was scanning correctly and throwing the answer away.** For
`printf("%d %u\n", 1, 2u)` it emitted `defc CRT_printf_format = 0x00000003` —
bit-identical to sccz80's `$0003` — but into its own `.asm` module, where the
symbol is module-local and the crt never sees it. The link therefore fell through
to the default `0x801BF7BF`, which is every converter there is.

xcc already accepts `-zcc-opt=<file>` ("Append inferred z88dk link capabilities to
file"). zcc simply was not passing it. One line in `configure_compiler`.

  pf.c = printf("%d %u\n", 1, 2u)      before        after
    xcc                                2863 B        2007 B      mask $0003
    sccz80 / 80cc, for reference       2011 / 2012 B

►► THE EFFECT ON THE TABLE. Over the 30 benchmarks on z80, xcc -Of drops
193273 B → 170980 B (**−22293 B, −11.5%**), and -Os 182397 B → 160104 B (−12.2%).
The saving is a near-constant −796 B on 27 of the 30, −788 on two, and −21 on
md5 — which is exactly right, because md5 formats a hex digest and genuinely
needs most of the converter set. Ticks moved −0.01%: this is dead weight being
dropped from the link, not a codegen change.

►► THE sdcc COLUMNS HAVE THE SAME INFLATION, and it is not fixed. sdcc does no
format scanning at all, so it takes the same everything-default. Forcing each
benchmark's converter set to the one 80cc derives for it:

  sdcc -SO2, 30 benchmarks:   202862 B → 179408 B   (−23454 B, −11.6%)

That is the like-for-like size sdcc would report if it scanned. **The sdcc and
sdcc-max cells below are left as measured — they are what sdcc really produces —
but any size comparison against them is roughly 790 B per binary too generous to
80cc and sccz80.** The same applied to every xcc cell in every table before this
entry.

►► WHERE THAT LEAVES THE SIZE STANDINGS on z80, 30 benchmarks, whole binary:

  xcc -Os        160104 B        sccz80          168620 B
  xcc -Of        170980 B        sdcc (corrected) 179408 B
  80cc-fp        180080 B        80cc-sp         184297 B

80cc is now the largest of the four, not the smallest. The earlier reading — that
80cc led on size and traded bytes for speed — was an artefact of comparing its
scanned converter set against everyone else's unscanned one. This is the first
apples-to-apples size comparison in this file.

A zpragma-based scanner would give sdcc (and any future compiler) the same
treatment; zpragma already runs on every C path and already owns zcc_opt.def. The
governing rule has to be that any format it cannot read forces the full mask —
under-detection prints garbage with no diagnostic. xcc gets this right: given a
runtime format string it falls back to `0xC01BF7BF` rather than trusting the one
literal it could see.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
31/8/2026 — the xcc columns extended to z80n and ez80; z180 and kc160 cannot be
             done, and the reason is xcc's use of the undocumented IY halves
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MEASURED FRESH: xcc -Os and xcc -Of on z80n and ez80, 30 benchmarks each, both
profiles — 120 cells, built and run. Every one builds; the only non-result is
shiftbench, which fails its assertions on these CPUs exactly as it already does
on z80 (a pre-existing xcc bug, not a porting problem).

CARRIED FORWARD: everything else, verbatim from the 30/8 (3) table below.

►► WHAT AN xcc CELL ON ANOTHER CPU MEANS. xcc has no CPU selector — `-mz80` is
listed in its help as "Accepted for SDCC compatibility" and there is nothing
else. Its output is **byte-identical** on z80, z80n, z180, ez80 and kc160; only
the library and the CPU running it change, and no CPU-specific copt rule file is
applied on the xcc path (checked both ways: none appears on the command line, and
the generated asm does not differ). Compare 80cc, which really does retarget —
its ez80 output differs from its z80 output by 79 lines.

So read these two columns as *xcc's z80 code, on that CPU, against that CPU's
library*. They are not the like-for-like retargeting the sccz80 and 80cc columns
report. On ez80 that is still worth having: charbench 26.95M on z80 against
6.59M on ez80 is the CPU, not the compiler.

►► z180 AND kc160 STAY EMPTY, AND NOT FOR WANT OF A LIBRARY. xcc emits the
undocumented IY half-register instructions — `cp iyl`, `cp iyh`, `ld d,iyh`,
`ld e,iyl` — which z80asm rejects on both:

  searchbench.c:68: error: illegal identifier   ^---- cp iyl
  interpbench.c:86: error: illegal identifier   ^---- ld d, iyh

Six of thirty benchmarks fail on each CPU at -Of (interpbench, lexbench,
maskbench, md5, predbench, searchbench) and two at -Os, which is only to say -Os
reaches for the index halves less often. A partial column would be a column whose
gaps mean "xcc used IY halves here", which is not a useful thing for a matrix to
say, so both are left as —. ez80 accepts the halves, which is why it is fine.

►► z80n NEEDED A ONE-LINE LIBRARY FIX. Nine benchmarks failed with
`undefined symbol: __mul16` and friends: `libsrc/l/l_z80n.lst` did not include
`@${NEWLIB_ROOT}l/xcc.lst`, so none of xcc's runtime helpers reached
`z80n_crt0.lib` — the only CPU library missing them. The others get them by three
different routes: crt0_z80.lst and crt0_ez80.lst include `l_z80.lst` directly,
while crt0_z180.lst and crt0_kc160.lst end with `@crt0_z80.lst` and inherit it.
z80n uses `l_z80n.lst`, which had the z80n-specific sccz80 and util lists but not
the xcc one. Adding the line and rebuilding `z80n_crt0.lib` fixed all nine.

The helpers are plain z80 assembly with no CPU-specific encodings, so a z80n
build linking them is sound.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
30/8/2026 (3) — 80cc-fp and 80cc-sp regenerated on master, all twelve CPUs,
                 after the toolchain and library rebuild
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MEASURED FRESH: every 80cc cell in the table — 30 benchmarks × 12 CPUs × fp/sp,
360 cells, each built and run. All 360 pass; no BUILD, no WRONG, no missing
ticks.

CARRIED FORWARD: sccz80, xcc -Os, xcc -Of, sdcc and sdcc-max, verbatim from the
30/8 (2) table below.

►► WHY NOW. master has merged 80cc-vm1 (#3075) and xcc-runtime-fixes (#3091),
and the installed binaries were stale — `bin/z88dk-z80asm` still rejected
`-mvm1` although `cpu.def` had carried it since the merge. The root Makefile's
`bin/%` rules depend only on `src/config.h`, so with a binary already present
`make` skips them and reports success without doing anything; the tools have to
be rebuilt through their own sub-makes. z80asm, sccz80, 80cc, zcc, ticks, copt,
ucpp and zpragma were rebuilt, then the whole library tree (364 libs, 0 errors).

►► THE HEADLINE IS THAT NOTHING MOVED. Against the previous 80cc numbers:

  ticks    −0.03% to −0.10% on every CPU and both modes, no cell slower
  bytes    +43..53 B per binary on z80, near-uniform

A near-constant per-binary byte delta with flat ticks is the signature of a
library change, not a codegen change. **80cc's code generation is unchanged since
19/8** — this regeneration re-baselines the columns against today's libraries and
confirms the older numbers rather than correcting them.

►► THE LIBRARY CHANGE, IDENTIFIED. Of the 167 library .asm files that changed
since 19/8, exactly three are linked into a benchmark binary, and all three are
32-bit unsigned divide routines:

  math/integer/l_divu_32_32x16.asm              48 → 35 lines
  math/integer/small/l_small_divu_32_32x16.asm   0 → 104 lines  (new file)
  math/integer/small/l_small_divu_32_32x32.asm 123 → 136 lines

They come from `94fd9c55ce crt0 - rework long/int divides for DIV16_FASTMATH`,
with `3e6318377d kc160 - fix div 32_32x16 linkage` on top. They land in *every*
binary — `l_small_divu_32_32x16` is in sieve's map, and sieve does no long
arithmetic at all; printf's number formatting pulls the divide in unconditionally.
That is why the delta is a constant per binary rather than proportional to
anything the benchmark does.

The same commit explains the whole spread of per-binary deltas, because it also
added CPU-specific long-divide code:

  gbz80  +122 B   new l_long_div_0.asm (123 lines)
  ez80    +78 B
  8080    +76 B   new l_long_div_0.asm (129 lines)
  r2ka    +59 B     r4k / r6k  +56 B
  z80     +47 B     z80n / z180 the same
  kc160   +35 B   the linkage fix
  8085    −29 B   its l_long_div_0.asm was REWORKED and came out smaller
  vm1      +0 B   both vm1 measurements already used the new library

8080 and gbz80 grew most because they gained a dedicated divide path they did not
have; 8085 is the only CPU that shrank, and it is the only one whose existing
path was rewritten rather than added to. The −0.03..−0.10% tick movement is the
same rework being marginally faster, which is what DIV16_FASTMATH is for.

Per-CPU totals over the 30 benchmarks, sp mode:

  cpu     bytes  old → new        ticks old → new
  z80    182885 → 184297  +1412        1418 → 1417 M
  z80n   182370 → 183782  +1412        1355 → 1354 M

8085 is the one that shrank. vm1 reproduces the 30/8 (2) measurement to the byte
and to the tick on all 30 benchmarks — an independent re-run an hour apart, which
is the cross-check that the harness is deterministic.

►► MECHANICS, for whoever regenerates this next. Per-CPU `-clib` and emulator
flags:

  z80    (default)          -b msx          z80n   -clib=z80n      -mz80n
  z180   -clib=z180         -mz180          ez80   -clib=ez80_z80  -mez80_z80
  r2ka   -clib=rabbit       -mr2ka          r4k    -clib=rabbit4k  -mr4k
  r6k    -clib=rabbit6k     -mr6k           kc160  -clib=kc160     -mkc160
  8080   -clib=8080         -m8080          8085   -clib=8085      -m8085
  gbz80  -clib=gbz80        -mgbz80         vm1    -clib=vm1       -mvm1

fp mode is `-fframe-pointer`. The older `-Cc-frameix` spelling no longer reaches
80cc — `-Cc` now feeds sccz80 only, since the multi-compiler options moved off
`-compiler` (#3089) — and a run using it silently produces no binary. 8080, 8085,
gbz80 and vm1 have no index register, so fp == sp and only sp is measured.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
30/8/2026 (2) — the VM1 column, measured for real: z80asm assembles it, there is
                 a VM1 library, and sccz80 targets it
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MEASURED FRESH: every vm1 cell — sccz80 (30 benchmarks, a column that did not
exist before) and 80cc-sp (30 benchmarks, re-measured natively). All 60 built and
run, all 60 pass.

CARRIED FORWARD: every non-vm1 cell, verbatim from the 30/8 table below.

►► WHAT CHANGED IN THE TOOLCHAIN. The 19/8 entry had to say "z80asm does not know
this CPU yet" and compiled VM1 while assembling as 8080, rewriting the ten VM1
instructions to `defb` through src/80cc/vm1_shim.py, linking the 8080 library
because there was no VM1 one. All three of those are now gone: z80asm has vm1 and
vm1_strict (`cpu.def` 37/38) and assembles `ld hl,(de)` / `cp hl,de` / `sub hl,de`
to ED / DD / 18 directly, libsrc builds vm1_crt0.lib, vm1_clib.lib and
testvm1_clib.lib, and `zcc -clib=vm1` works for sccz80 as well as 80cc.

►► THE SHIM WAS HONEST. Comparing 80cc's native vm1 numbers against 19/8's
shim-and-8080-library numbers, over all 30 benchmarks:

  ticks   +0.02%          — 22 of 30 within ±0.3%, worst +1.61% (switchbench)
  bytes   +78B per binary, near-constant (74..97B across every benchmark)

The +78B is the real VM1 library against the 8080 library it used to borrow, not
codegen. The 19/8 numbers can be read as valid; this entry supersedes them only
because it no longer needs a caveat.

►► sccz80 ON VM1, FOR THE FIRST TIME. All 30 benchmarks build, run and pass.
Totals against 80cc on the same CPU:

  sccz80   190186 B    3257 M
  80cc     204367 B    1670 M      +7.5% bytes, −48.7% ticks

That is a wider tick gap than 80cc holds on any other 808x CPU, and the same
direction as everywhere else: 80cc trades size for speed against sccz80.

►► VM1 AGAINST ITS NEIGHBOURS, 80cc, whole binary, 30 benchmarks:

  8080   203425 B   1725 M
  8085   189869 B   1359 M
  vm1    204367 B   1670 M      +0.46% bytes, −3.19% ticks vs 8080

The tick figure matches 19/8's −3.21% exactly. The byte figure moved from −0.69%
to +0.46% purely because of the +78B/binary library difference described above —
VM1 codegen is the same size as 8080's, its library is slightly larger.

Read the VM1 column against 8080, not 8085: the 8085 column links the 8085
library, which is tuned for it, so its whole-binary lead is mostly library rather
than codegen.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
30/8/2026 — xcc 2.5.0 re-measured with the classic runtime actually enabled;
             −13.2% ticks, four cells repaired, an option-word bug fixed in copt
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MEASURED FRESH: the xcc -Os and xcc -Of columns, 30 benchmarks on z80 — the only
CPU those columns have ever carried — every cell built and run.

CARRIED FORWARD, NOT re-run: sccz80, sdcc, sdcc-max, 80cc-fp and 80cc-sp are
copied verbatim from the 19/8 table below, all of their cells, every CPU. They
are that entry's numbers carrying that entry's caveats; nothing measured here
touches those compilers.

►► TWO FIXES MADE THESE NUMBERS POSSIBLE, both outside xcc itself.

zcc handed xcc `-runtime=z88dk-classic` with one dash. xcc takes `--runtime`, so
it rejected the flag as an unknown option, warned, and compiled every benchmark
against its own default runtime instead of z88dk's. Fixed in src/zcc/zcc.c.

xcc then writes the z88dk printf/scanf option words as bare hex —
`defc CRT_printf_format = C01BF7BF`, `defc CLIB_OPT_PRINTF_2 = 0000005F` — and
z80asm needs `0x`. Two rules in lib/xcc_rules.1 now add the prefix, in both the
plain and the `| value` accumulate form. Note what the missing prefix did: a
value containing a-f is a hard syntax error, which is what killed md5, but a
value of digits alone assembles SILENTLY AS DECIMAL — `00002205` became 2205 —
selecting the wrong printf converter set with no diagnostic at all. Only md5
moved when the rules went in; every other cell in this table is byte-identical
with and without them, so md5 was the only benchmark reaching either path.

►► THE COLUMN MOVED −13.2% over the 26 cells measurable both then and now
(1311.5M → 1138.8M ticks, -Of). It is concentrated, not uniform: hashbench
−39.2%, strbench −32.1%, predbench −31.3%, charbench −31.2%, intbench −30.0%,
sieve −28.2%, md5 −27.2%, listbench −21.9%, rle −20.6%. Six cells moved less
than 3%, and crcbench and divbench did not move at all.

►► xcc -Of IS NOW THE FASTEST COLUMN on 23 of the 29 z80 benchmarks it compiles,
judged against the carried sccz80/sdcc/sdcc-max/80cc-fp/80cc-sp cells — so
against 19/8's toolchain, not today's. Where it loses it mostly loses to
sdcc-max (widthbench 60.7M vs 32.0M, callbench 73.8M vs 52.5M, localbench 274.6M
vs 234.7M, predbench 43.2M vs 39.0M, histbench 28.5M vs 28.2M). The exception is
divbench, where 80cc-fp is 66.1M against xcc's 220.4M.

►► SIZE IS WHERE IT PAYS FOR THAT. Over the 28 benchmarks comparable on size,
xcc -Of totals 173583B against sdcc's 168155B (+3.2%) and 80cc-fp's 156807B
(+10.7%). -Os buys some back and costs a lot of speed: crcbench 86.1M → 107.4M,
intbench 33.0M → 40.3M, switchbench 31.2M → 41.1M, matrixbench 28.4M → 44.3M.

►► FOUR CELLS REPAIRED, NONE LOST.

  fixedbench     WRONG → 20.77M   (-Of; -Os likewise WRONG → 43.34M)
  bitfieldbench  WRONG → 27.03M   (-Of; -Os likewise WRONG → 30.42M)
  callbench      BUILD → 73.77M   (-Of; -Os BUILD → 81.19M)
  md5            30.29M → 22.06M  (-Of, −27.2%; -Os 34.54M → 27.68M, −19.9%)

shiftbench is the one cell still bad, and unchanged in status: -Of builds and
runs but fails its assertions, -Os does not build (`undefined symbol: __shl16`,
a different failure from the one it had on 19/8). spectralnorm is not in the
matrix and does not build either — xcc emits SDCC-style float helpers (__fsadd,
__fssub, __fsmul, __fsdiv, ___fscmp, ___sint2fs) and none of them exist in the
classic libraries. Both want the same treatment the integer helpers already get:
a rename rule in xcc_rules.1 onto a z88dk wrapper.

Two mechanical notes. zcc hardcodes -Of for xcc and its -Cc pass-through only
feeds sccz80/80cc, so there is no way to ask for -Os through zcc; the -Os column
was measured through a wrapper on PATH that rewrites -Of to -Os on xcc's command
line. And sizes here are whole-binary bytes, as everywhere in this file, so they
move with the library as well as the compiler.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
19/8/2026 — the KR580VM1 joins the matrix; 80cc re-measured, references
             carried; a VM1 miscompile found by md5 and fixed
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MEASURED FRESH on branch 80cc-vm1: the 80cc-fp and 80cc-sp columns, 30
benchmarks x 12 CPUs, every cell built and run.

CARRIED FORWARD, NOT re-run: sccz80, xcc -Os, xcc -Of, sdcc and sdcc-max are
copied verbatim from the 18/8 table below, all 330 of their cells. Nothing in
this branch touches those compilers, so they are a valid reference — but they
are last week's toolchain against today's 80cc, and any caveat the 18/8 entry
puts on them (its md5 row's xcc and sdcc cells are older still, carried from
12/8) travels with them. The VM1 rows have no reference cells at all: no other
compiler targets this CPU.

►► THE NEW CPU. The KR580VM1 is a Soviet 8080 with ten more instructions, two
prefixes and a second pointer pair. 80cc uses six of them: `cp hl,de`,
`sub hl,de`, `ld hl,(de)`, `ld (de),hl`, `sbc hl,de`, and h'l' as an index home.
Like the other CPUs with no index register it takes fp == sp.

►► READ THE VM1 COLUMN AGAINST 8080, NOT AGAINST 8085, and know two things
about how it was built.

z80asm does not know this CPU yet. The VM1 cells are compiled as VM1 and
assembled as 8080, with the ten instructions rewritten to defb by
src/80cc/vm1_shim.py (a z88dk-z80asm wrapper does it on the way into the real
assembler). The encodings are the real ones and z88dk-ticks -mvm1 runs the real
CPU model, so the numbers are honest — but nothing here has been through a VM1
assembler, and the encodings are asserted from the wiki page, not validated.

The VM1 links the 8080 LIBRARY, because it runs 8080 code unchanged and there is
no VM1 library. The 8085 column links the 8085 library, which is tuned for it.
So the whole-binary gap to 8085 (+22% ticks) is much wider than the gap in
compiler output alone (+8.1%, measured separately as the code_compiler section);
most of that difference is library, not codegen.

Totals over the 30 benchmarks, sp mode, whole binary:

  8080   203425 B   1725.46 M
  8085   189869 B   1358.78 M
  vm1    202024 B   1670.12 M      −0.69% bytes, −3.21% ticks against 8080

The wins are concentrated where the VM1's instructions actually bite — pointer
work, 16-bit compares, and the extra register home:

  queenbench   −16.35% ticks     structbench  −15.73%     lexbench   −8.79%
  recordbench   −7.86%           sieve         −6.14%     predbench  −5.92%

and are flat elsewhere: md5 and listbench move by less than 0.02%, which is what
a corpus dominated by library time and 32-bit arithmetic looks like.

►► THE 8080, 8085 AND gbz80 COLUMNS MOVED TOO, and not because of the VM1.
80cc used to emit `sbc hl,de` on those CPUs, where z80asm substitutes a call to
__z80asm__sbc_hl_de — 86T on the 8080, 82T on the 8085, 80T on the gbz80, plus
19 bytes of linked helper. Half that time is the helper preserving A and BC that
neither call site needs preserved. It now subtracts inline: same size, and on a
negate-heavy loop 8080 −13.0% ticks, 8085 −14.1%, gbz80 −2.5%. The helper is
gone from the corpus entirely — 12 sites to 0.

►► md5 EARNED ITS PLACE IN THE MATRIX. It was the one cell that would not run,
and it was a real VM1 miscompile, not a harness fault this time.

PSW bit 3 on the VM1 is MF, the data-bank select. So `pop af` used to DISCARD a
stack word switches the bank, and every data access afterwards reads the other
64K. 80cc used AF as its discard register in the fused long bitop
(ir_lower_ops.inc.c), which md5's Transform hits 64 times: it read the wrong
bank from the first one on. The discard now goes through HL, which the byte
chain above it has finished with — the same two bytes and the same 20T.

That site arrived with the 80cc-further merge (7f22e23d8a), AFTER the two
earlier `pop af` discards had been found and fixed. A one-off audit does not
hold, so there is now a standing check: src/80cc/vm1_legal.py refuses any
`pop af` with no `push af` outstanding, counted per function. Compiler output
reports zero; the only hits are 13 in the zx suite's hand-written #asm, which
really would switch the bank and will never be built for a VM1.

Reproduce with test/suites/gen_bench_matrix_vm1.py (MX_CPUS=vm1 re-measures one
column). It runs md5 with the md5 directory as the working directory, because
md5sum.c md5sums a file and a run from anywhere else reports WRONG for every
compiler on every CPU — the trap that has twice lost this row.


────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
THE 8080 FAMILY ON ITS OWN
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
The same measurements filtered to the three CPUs that share this lineage, which
is the comparison the VM1 work is actually about, and turned on its side: the
CPUs are the columns and the compiler is a row, so a bench reads across. What is
gone: xcc and sdcc do not target any of these three, sccz80 does not target the
VM1 (hence the dashes in that column), and the fp column goes because none of
the three has an index register, so all of them take fp == sp.

Totals over the 30 benchmarks:

  8080   203425 B   1725.46 M
  8085   189869 B   1358.78 M
  vm1    202024 B   1670.12 M    against 8080: −0.69% bytes, −3.21% ticks

The VM1 sits nearer the 8080 than the 8085, and the reason is which instructions
each CPU adds. The 8085's LDSI and LDHI make FRAME-relative access cheap, and
frames are everywhere; the VM1 has no way to form a slot address in DE without
going through HL, so none of the 8085's lhlx/shlx slot folds are open to it. What
it has instead — `sub hl,de` with no staging, a 16-bit compare that keeps HL, and
a second pointer pair — pays on pointer and compare shapes, which is why the wins
concentrate in queenbench (−16.35% ticks), structbench (−15.73%) and lexbench
(−8.79%) and vanish on md5 and listbench.

Read the whole-binary numbers knowing the VM1 links the 8080 LIBRARY while the
8085 links its own. Comparing compiler output alone (the code_compiler section,
8 benchmarks) the gap is much narrower: 8080 23557 B, 8085 21463 B, VM1 23206 B —
VM1 −1.5% against the 8080 and +8.1% against the 8085, where the whole-binary
tick gap to the 8085 is +22%. Most of that difference is library, not codegen.
