════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
18/8/2026 — 80cc re-measured on 80cc-further; 8085 −2.9% ticks; md5 restored; an
             fp abort found and fixed
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MEASURED FRESH at 1f1773f9f5 (branch 80cc-further): the 80cc-fp and 80cc-sp
columns only, 570 cells — 30 benchmarks x 11 CPUs in sp, x 8 in fp (the three
CPUs with no index register take fp == sp). Every cell built and run. Compiler
frozen for the whole run at md5 4aac8e27f4; it was rebuilt afterwards from the
same tree and reproduced that md5 exactly, and the 8085 corpus asm is
byte-identical across the two builds, so the table is one compiler throughout.

TWO ROWS WERE MEASURED AFTERWARDS, both stated where they appear below: md5 (which
this matrix had lost — see below) and localbench (whose fp cells were the abort,
re-measured once it was fixed). The fix that lies between the two compilers
(4aac8e27f4 -> e6c66e324e) changes exactly ONE cell in the whole corpus — verified
by measuring compiled-code size for every benchmark on z80-sp, z80-fp and 8085-sp
before and after: byte-identical everywhere except the function that used to
abort. So the table is consistent even though it was not all taken in one pass.

►► md5 IS BACK. It has been absent since the 14/8 regeneration, and there are two
reasons a bench list drops it. Its source is md5sum.c, so any harness that globs
<dir>/<dir>.c misses it (the same trap that makes codesize.sh's md5 cell a no-op).
And md5 READS A FILE — it md5sums md5test.bin — so z88dk-ticks has to run with the
md5 directory as its working directory or the test fails at runtime. The first
attempt at this row reported WRONG for every compiler on every CPU for exactly
that reason, sccz80 included, which is the tell: a whole column of failures is a
harness fault, not eleven compiler faults. Its xcc and sdcc cells are CARRIED FROM THE
12/8/2026 entry, the last table that still had an md5 row: z80 has all four
reference columns there, z180 and kc160 have sdcc and sdcc-max, z80n's sdcc ticks
were already unknown then and its `?M` marks are kept as they stand, and r6k has
no cell at all because it postdates that table. Those cells are an older toolchain
against today's freshly measured sccz80 and 80cc — a reference point, not a
like-for-like reading.

CARRIED FORWARD, NOT re-run: sccz80, xcc -Os, xcc -Of, sdcc and sdcc-max are
copied verbatim from the 14/8/2026 table. That table's 80cc columns were measured
at 8d15e17b9b, which IS a direct ancestor of this branch with nothing exclusive to
it, so the 80cc before/after below is a clean walk along this branch's history —
not a comparison across divergent branches.

►► READ THE TICKS, NOT THE BYTES, when comparing against the 14/8 columns.

Whole-binary bytes rose on the z80 family and the Rabbits and fell on ez80,
kc160 and gbz80, which looks like a codegen regression and is not one. Measured
separately, COMPILED CODE (the `code_compiler` section, compiler output with the
library excluded) went DOWN across the same 29 benchmarks:

  z80    23270 -> 23115 B   (−155 B, 4 benches smaller, 0 larger)
  8085   20633 -> 20229 B   (−404 B, −1.96%, 28 smaller, 0 larger)

(Those two figures are the 29 benchmarks the 14/8 list carried, so they are a
like-for-like walk; md5 is excluded from them because 14/8 has nothing to compare
it against.)

The whole-binary movement is therefore link and library side: the classic
libraries installed in lib/clibs today are not the ones the 14/8 table linked, so
the byte columns are not a like-for-like before/after. Ticks and the compiled-code
figures above are.

One library change IS deliberate and does move bytes, for BOTH compilers equally:
the 8085 32-bit divide by a 16-bit divisor now runs in registers (DIV16_FASTPATH,
on), which adds 86 B to every 8085 binary that links the long divide and pays only
when the divisor really fits in 16 bits at runtime. Across this corpus that is
+86 B for nothing measurable — sccz80 8085 divbench 4273 -> 4359 B with ticks
151.83M -> 151.80M (−0.02%), fixedbench 4387 -> 4473 B and 33.84M -> 33.81M
(−0.09%). pi.c is where it pays: 7,375,640,847 -> 2,744,570,287 ticks, 2.69x. The
carried sccz80 8085 byte cells therefore read 86 B low against the fresh 80cc
ones; the tick cells are unaffected.

80cc ticks against the 14/8 measurement, sp mode, per CPU (cells / total tick
change / benches faster / benches slower):

  8085    29   −2.89%   29 faster   0 slower      <- the branch's 8085 work
  gbz80   29   −1.56%   29 faster   0 slower
  8080    29   −1.13%   10 faster   2 slower
  z80     29   −0.36%    5 faster   0 slower
  z80n    29   −0.38%    5 faster   0 slower
  z180    29   −0.36%    5 faster   4 slower
  ez80    29   −0.36%    4 faster   0 slower
  r2ka    29   −0.25%    3 faster   2 slower
  r4k     29   −0.27%    2 faster   3 slower
  r6k     29   −0.28%    3 faster   1 slower
  kc160   29   −0.22%    2 faster   1 slower

fp mode is flat everywhere (every CPU within ±0.01%, at most 2 benches moving).
That is expected: the 8085 levers this branch added — dsub, the lhlx/shlx slot and
deref paths, the immediate word compare, the dead DE park — are sp-slot shapes,
and the three CPUs that gained most have no fp mode at all.

80cc-sp against sccz80 over the 313 cells where sccz80 has a number: bytes
1.051x, ticks 0.541x, 80cc faster in 307 of 313 and smaller in 22. The tick lead
is the story and it is unchanged; the byte gap is the standing density work.

►► THE fp ABORT: FOUND HERE, ROOT-CAUSED, FIXED.

The first pass of this matrix produced three non-clean cells — localbench 80cc-fp
on z80, z80n and z180 — all the same hard abort:

  localbench.c:63: error: ir_lower: value read with no live register and no stack
  slot (v11, phys 20, width 2)

phys 20 is IR_PR_STACK, a value parked with push/pop instead of a frame slot. The
cells held numbers on 14/8, so it was new, and it was a shipped configuration: z80
family, fp mode, where word slots are dear enough that ir_stack_spill parks.

Bisected to a45fbacc39 ("a lea escapes remat when it is parked on the stack, not
when the cpu is 8080") — its parent compiles cleanly. But that commit only removed
the mask; the defect was older and lived somewhere else entirely, which the gates
said plainly: --opt-disable=stack-spill compiled, while --opt-disable=remat still
ABORTED even though it skips the whole block a45fbacc39 touched, and origin/master
aborted the same way under that flag.

THE DEFECT: gen_lea emits nothing when lea_all_uses_indexed() says every use of
the address became a frame-indexed access, and that predicate disagreed with the
lowering. gen_st_mem's frame-indexed store path is guarded on `src[0] >= 0`, so a
store whose VALUE is a folded immediate (`r.d = 0`) skips it and materialises the
base with load_to_hl(mem.base) instead. The predicate never looked at src[0]. So
the address was elided and then read. Remat hid it: the LEA was a frame-slot
address, recomputed on demand, so the read got the right value anyway. Parking the
address makes remat correctly decline — and then the def emitted no push and the
use had no slot.

A SILENT WRONG ANSWER WAS NEVER REACHABLE, and the reason is worth recording: the
predicate returns 0 the moment the function contains any call, and remat-LEA is
gated to call-free functions, so the only functions that can elide a LEA are
exactly the ones where remat covers the read. Every path to the bug ends at the
guard, which is why it aborted instead of miscompiling. Confirmed by running the
with-call shape through the pre-fix compiler: correct output.

THE FIX makes the predicate mirror the lowering's own guard — a store with
src[0] < 0 needs the address. Cost, measured as compiled code across all 29
benchmarks: ZERO on z80-sp, zero on 8085-sp, zero on z80-fp except the one
function that used to abort. In whole-binary terms localbench z80-fp is 4609B
against 14/8's 4580B, +29 B, with ticks identical at 322.68M — the address is now
emitted where it was previously (wrongly) elided.

Regression test: test/suites/long_ir/leaimm.c, four targets (z80, z80-fp, 8085,
8080). It ABORTS the pre-fix compiler in fp mode and passes with the fix, so it
pins the bug rather than merely exercising the area; sp mode passes either way,
which is why the fp target is the one that matters.

Everything else on the branch is gated and reverts byte for byte:
`--opt-disable=de-park` restores every 8085 DE park, `DIV16_FASTPATH = 0` drops the
register divide, `IR_DEPARK_SWEEP=1` cross-checks the park sweep against an
independent forward walk (541/541 sites agree corpus-wide, 0 violations).

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
14/8/2026 — sccz80 + 80cc(fp/sp) re-measured; Rabbit 6000 joins the matrix
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MEASURED FRESH at 8d15e17b9b (branch 80cc-bit-test), 870 cells, every one built
and run: sccz80, 80cc-fp and 80cc-sp across 29 benchmarks x 11 CPUs.

CARRIED FORWARD, NOT re-run: the xcc -Os / xcc -Of / sdcc / sdcc-max columns
are copied verbatim from the 14/8/2026 table so the comparison stays whole.
They were measured with a different compiler build; treat them as a reference
point, not as a like-for-like reading against today's 80cc numbers. r6k has no
carried cells at all — it is new to the matrix, and xcc is z80-only.

EXCEPT the r2ka, r4k and r6k sdcc columns, which ARE freshly measured — the
first sdcc numbers this matrix has ever carried for any Rabbit. They read BUILD
or blank in every prior table because sdcc's Rabbit output would not assemble:
`ioi`/`ioe` were emitted on their own line (they are prefixes, not opcodes), the
`.area _XABS` sections had no mapping, and the offset-before-paren index forms
(`ld hl, 0(hl)`, and on r6k the whole `alu hl, N (sp)` family) were unconverted.
r4k and r6k additionally needed the zcc CPU map corrected — it was handing sdcc
`-mr4ka`, which is not an sdcc port. NOTE the assembler rules in
lib/sdcc/sdcc_opt.1 are UNCOMMITTED, so these three columns are not reproducible
from a clean checkout until they land.

The kc160 sdcc column is freshly measured too. It needed no new rules — zcc
maps kc160 to sdcc's z80 port (`-mz80`) and assembles the result for kc160 —
it had simply never been run.

80cc-sp is SMALLER than sdcc on every one of these benchmarks that sdcc
completes, 91 cells for 91:
  r2ka   27/29 clean   0.891x bytes (27/27 smaller)   1.009x ticks
  r4k    19/29 clean   0.893x bytes (19/19 smaller)   0.970x ticks
  r6k    18/29 clean   0.896x bytes (18/18 smaller)   0.999x ticks
  kc160  27/29 clean   0.892x bytes (27/27 smaller)   0.809x ticks

kc160 is the strongest showing: 80cc is ~11% smaller AND ~19% faster, winning
on ticks in 21 of 27. Its two failures are WRONG, never BUILD or HANG:
bitfieldbench (sdcc's own bitfield defect — it is WRONG on z80/z80n/z180 too)
fixedbench was ALSO failing here, and that one turned out to be OURS, not
sdcc's: the kc160 `pop bc / push hl` -> `ld (sp+0),hl` fold drops the BC
clobber, which is only sound where BC is dead. sccz80 and 80cc are; sdcc is
not. Fixed by gating the rule with the new %notcompiler directive (copt now
takes -compiler=<name> from zcc), so sccz80 and 80cc keep the fold with
byte-identical output. kc160 sdcc is now 28/29.

Reliability splits sharply by core. r2ka is sound. r4k and r6k share an
identical failure set, none of which occurs on r2ka and all of which sccz80 and
80cc run correctly (29/29 each), so these are sdcc faults on the newer cores:
  WRONG  crcbench, divbench, bitfieldbench   (bitfieldbench also fails on z80)
  HANG   searchbench, switchbench, vecbench, maskbench, localbench, widthbench
  BUILD  histbench — sdcc emits `inc (sp+d)`, not a Rabbit opcode
  BUILD  sortbench — r6k ONLY: a `jr` out of range in l_ins_sort
         (`integer range: -$86`), r6k code being larger than r4k's
The hangs are real, not a watchdog artefact: searchbench was given 160 billion
cycles and 300s of wall clock without terminating, where r2ka runs the same
source in 12.06M ticks.

Cell = `bytes / ticks(millions)` for the whole -create-app binary, so every
cell carries the same fixed runtime overhead. `= sp (no IX)` marks the IX-less
CPUs, where fp mode is identical to sp by construction. BUILD / HANG / WRONG
are recorded rather than dropped, so a gap cannot be mistaken for missing data.

Both compilers were frozen for the whole run (md5s in test/suites/matrix/frozen.md5):
rebuilding mid-run silently mixes two compilers into one table.

Non-clean fresh cells (6):
  localbench     r2ka   sccz80-sp  BUILD
  localbench     r4k    sccz80-sp  BUILD
  localbench     r6k    sccz80-sp  BUILD
  shiftbench     r2ka   sccz80-sp  BUILD
  shiftbench     r4k    sccz80-sp  BUILD
  shiftbench     r6k    sccz80-sp  BUILD

14/8/2026 — full regeneration: all 29 benchmarks, every column measured
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Complete re-measure at bbdca875e5 (branch 80cc-bit-test). Not a column refresh —
every cell is a fresh build and run — so the seven benchmarks added in August
(bitfieldbench, widthbench, predbench, shiftbench, localbench, divbench,
callbench) have rows for the first time.

COLUMN COVERAGE. Each compiler is measured on every target it actually supports,
rather than being restricted to z80:

  sccz80      all 10 CPUs                            286/290 cells
  xcc -Os/-Of z80 only (xcc has no other backend)     25/290
  sdcc        z80, z80n, z180, gbz80                 104/290
  sdcc-max    same, -Cs--max-allocs-per-node -Cs100000  103/290
  80cc-fp     all 10 (`= sp (no IX)` on gbz80/8080/8085)
  80cc-sp     all 10                                 290/290

sdcc does NOT cover the six targets expected. Two are hard limits of this build,
recorded rather than papered over:
  ez80  `error 131: cannot generate code for target 'ez80_z80'` — no port at all,
        so those cells read `no port`.
  r2ka  compiles the C but the framework fails to assemble: test.c:444
        `SECTION XABS (ABS)` syntax error. Every one of its 58 cells is BUILD.

sdcc-max: nothing in the tree records how the historical sdcc-max column was
produced, so these figures use --max-allocs-per-node 100000 (maintainer's
answer). They are NOT necessarily comparable with sdcc-max in the older tables.

A cell that would not build or ran wrong is BUILD / HANG / WRONG rather than
dropped, so a gap cannot be mistaken for missing data.

z80, 80cc-sp against each reference:
  vs sccz80    faster on 29, slower on 0   best charbench 0.16x
  vs sdcc      faster on 14, slower on 14  best switchbench 0.53x, worst widthbench 1.75x
  vs sdcc-max  faster on 12, slower on 16  best divbench 0.60x,    worst widthbench 1.91x
  vs xcc -Of   faster on 13, slower on 12  best divbench 0.31x,    worst queenbench 1.49x

divbench went from 1.79x SLOWER than sdcc to 0.58x on the back of this run's
signed-divide work. The known remaining losses are widthbench (1.75x, not yet
root-caused) and localbench (1.47x — address-taken locals spill to a frame slot
where sdcc parks them on the stack; open task).

OTHER COMPILERS' OWN FAILURES, recorded as their results:
  sdcc   wrong checksum on bitfieldbench (z80) and 22 other cells across z80n /
         z180 / gbz80. 80cc and sccz80 both match the gcc-derived reference.
  xcc    callbench will not build at either profile; shiftbench will not build at
         -Os and is wrong at -Of; fixedbench and bitfieldbench are wrong.
CI runs 80cc and sccz80 only, so none of these gate anything.

Thirty commits since master. The ones that move these numbers:

  4334d55cf1  signed divide and remainder by a power of two -> bias and shift
  34eeda19f7  a full-width arithmetic shift right is a sign mask
  3e4666cefe  frame address at a constant displacement via the frame register
  1d956e6048  frame access uses each target's own addressing form
  ebb7ba830a  address CSE matches remat frame bases by the slot they name
  39b1602635  gbz80 has the CB shift set, so an arithmetic >> inlines
  9f4dcd6a0b  a constant-count byte right shift stays in the accumulator
  a4d9a1e451  a value that fits a byte still fits after a copy
  4d341ccf9f  gbz80 takes a nibble shift with swap
  cd265f8606  z80n takes a nibble shift with swapnib
  bbdca875e5  a mask already sets Z, so the truth-test needs no or a

Correctness fixes found alongside them:

  7437c9d060  a frame-address remat must not clobber the operand held in HL
  46dd644168  type the callee expression of a call so its subtree is optimised
  e33b231a8e  an l_asr result must reach a DE-homed destination (8080)
  0016aa0903  ticks: swap actually swaps, and rabbit6k swap r mirrors
  1cab9c2c12  ticks: rabbit swap assigns across banks, it does not exchange

XCC RE-MEASURED (12/8, later the same day). The xcc -Os / xcc -Of columns are
NOT carried over from 10/8 — xcc was rebuilt and both profiles moved a lot.
44 of its 46 cells changed, -8835 B in total, 34 faster and 6 slower.
The gain is overwhelmingly in -Os, which was leaving a great deal on the table:
      structbench   -Os   -57.9%
      queenbench    -Of   -53.7%
      queenbench    -Os   -51.6%
      listbench     -Os   -50.3%
      searchbench   -Os   -50.2%

  -Os is now close to -Of on several benches rather than 1.5-2x behind it.

  Two -Of cells go the OTHER way and are the only real tick regressions:
      rle           -Of   +61.2%
      intbench      -Of   +26.0%

  Both still shrink in bytes, so this reads as an -Of inlining/scheduling trade
  rather than lost work. Worth a look on the xcc side.

  fixedbench remains a pre-existing FAIL in both profiles (it now reports a
  size and tick count alongside the FAIL rather than bare 'FAIL').

THE TWO DENSITY LEVERS are one idea: sp-mode reaches a frame slot through
`ld hl,off; add hl,sp` (4 bytes), and the lowerer already tracked which slot HL
points at — it just threw the belief away. byte_alu_operand hand-rolled the
address and then called hl_about_to_change(-1), which CLEARS it, so three
accesses to one slot emitted three copies. Routing it through
emit_byte_slot_addr recovers the in-block case; bb_hl_addr_out (the address
analogue of bb_hl_out) recovers it across block edges. An address belief needs
no live_in test, unlike a value: a slot's absolute address is fixed for the
function's lifetime, so only a physical clobber can invalidate it. Both are
pure wins — bytes and ticks together, no byte-for-tick trade.

THE BYTE-RESIDENCY LEVER is what actually closes the fp/sp gap. byte-remat was
restricted to AND/OR/XOR uses, so a byte compared against a global had the
global loaded into A, evicting the compared value; widening it to byte EQ/NE
lets the value STAY in A, the A-carry hands it to the next block, its slot
loses every reader, dead-store elision drops it and the frame goes with it.
The motivating shape (mini2.c: `unsigned char a = src+1; if (a != b) b = a;`)
went 31 B sp / 36 B fp -> 14 B in BOTH modes, against sdcc's 19.

THE 8085 COLUMN IS A DELIBERATE TRADE, not a regression to chase. #ADDR folds
`ex de,hl / ld hl,_sym / add hl,de` into `ld de,_sym / add hl,de` on the claim
that DE is dead after. On 8085 that is false — LDSI+LHLX leaves the index in DE
and a later `ex de,hl` reclaims it — and sieve/z88dk-classic HANGS on it. The
rule is now notcpu-8085 and the 8085 column pays for it: measured directly,
switchbench 8085 is 4782 B with the rule and 4805 B without, exactly the +23 B
in the table above. Every 8085 cell that grew or slowed traces to this.

ez80 (-311 B) is the biggest mover, and rle/charbench/lexbench carry most of it
across all CPUs. Real files: emu.c sp -195 B, enigma -4 B sp / -2 B fp,
adv_a unchanged.

REGRESSION STATE at 879d2e6d08: long_ir 157/157 sp AND fp; full test/suites
533 clean runs, the only failure being the dai32 pow tolerance (fixed here —
that tolerance had never actually been in force, TINY_POS_AM9511 mis-encoded as
~9.2e18 sent every comparison down the near-zero branch, making approx_equal
vacuously true); emu.c behavioural "On The Path" sp+fp; enigma RXSEC sp+fp;
adv_a inventory sp+fp; 172-source corpus with zero backend aborts.
IR_HLADDR_BB=0 reverts the cross-BB carry byte-identically.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
10/8/2026 (4) — DCE + byte-wise const compare + add hl,bc
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
80cc-fp/sp re-measured at commit abed5aac48; other columns verbatim from 7/8.

Three commits since the 10/8 (3) block, all from chasing two z88dk-classic
benchmarks rather than the suite corpus:

  da0df6dcf6  mark-sweep DCE for self-referential dead values
  51e3bc48ad  byte-wise width-2 compare against a constant (frees HL and DE)
  abed5aac48  add hl,bc when ONE operand is BC-resident

  391 cells vs the previous block:

      cpu     bytes  larger  faster  SLOWER
      z80      -154       1      19       1
      z80n     -154       1      19       1
      z180     -154       1      19       1
      ez80     -109       0      17       1
      kc160    -109       0      24       1
      r4k      -102       0      16       1
      r2ka      -90       1      18       1
      8080      -74       0      10       0
      gbz80     -74       0      10       0
      8085      -55       0       8       2
              -1075       4     160       9

  The 9 "slower" cells are 6 at +0.00% (rounding) and 3 x listbench fp at
  +0.04%, which is the one file that also grows (+8 B, from add hl,bc). Not
  understood: restricting the add-hl,bc path to operands cheap to reach made it
  WORSE (lost sieve entirely, listbench unchanged), so the guard was reverted
  and the +8 taken against -835 B. Worth a look.

WHERE THIS CAME FROM. support/benchmarks/sieve/z88dk-classic was 2.07x slower
than sdcc; it is now AHEAD:

    6,561,785 -> 4,064,982 -> 3,863,787 -> 3,154,170     sdcc 3,162,918
                    DCE        cmp-K       add hl,bc

  - The 2x was DEAD CODE, not codegen. Without -DPRINTF that bench's `count` is
    written every iteration and never read; sdcc deletes the chain. 80cc's DCE
    was a use COUNT, so a self-referential accumulator (`count -= x`) could never
    die -- its own def kept the count non-zero. Corpus opportunity for the new
    mark-sweep pass is ~zero (sortbench 2 ops; emu/clisp/adv_a/enigma 0), but
    dead computation is easy to create while developing: comment out a printf
    and you have it.
  - The other two are the same idea twice: STOP CONSUMING DE WHERE THE ISA DOES
    NOT REQUIRE IT. `ld de,K; and a; sbc hl,de` becomes `ld a,lo; sub K_lo;
    ld a,hi; sbc a,K_hi` (same bytes, HL and DE both free). `sym + index` with
    the index in BC becomes `ld hl,sym; add hl,bc` instead of copying BC->DE
    first. sieve's inner loop went 22 instructions -> 13 with DE gone from it.

pi.c (support/benchmarks/pi) is 3.7% behind and it is NOT the division: measured,
the 32-bit div helper is within 1.7% of sdcc's, the multiply helper +8.5%. The
loss is 80cc's own 32-bit scalar code -- load to DEHL, `ex de,hl` shuffles, store
back, where sdcc walks the value in memory byte-wise. pi is ~4.2 BILLION ticks a
run; measure it sparingly.

NOTE FOR THE DE-HOME ARC (Phase 1c). Both wins came from the LOWERER giving DE
back, not the allocator. The `de_dirty` model in IR_SPILLAUDIT still lists every
compare and every ADD as DE-dirtying, so it is now pessimistic on both counts.
Re-run the buckets before building the DE-home substrate -- values currently in
the `pressure` bucket (where the allocator provably cannot help) move into
`A_loop*` (where it can) every time an op stops dirtying DE.

Regression green at abed5aac48: long_ir 491/491 sp and fp; sccz80 588, stdlib
2107, string 308, ctype 7168, math 384, stdio 79, 0 failed; emu.c, enigma and
adv_a behavioural in both frame modes; listbench and sortbench (the two files
that change) both pass.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
10/8/2026 (3) — every gp-pair copy spelled `ld rr,rr'`: smaller on ALL ten CPUs
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
80cc-fp/sp re-measured at commit a86e546e46; every other column still verbatim
from the 7/8 table. Columns are the shipped default (IR_DS_SHARE now default-ON).

The 10/8 (2) block respelled ONE direction, HL->DE, because Rabbit 4000/6000
put the 8-bit register moves on a prefixed page (2 bytes each, so a pair costs
4) while `ld de,hl` is a native ONE byte. This block finishes the job:
`ld hl,de`, `ld bc,hl`, `ld hl,bc` as well.

  391 cells (23 benches x 10 cpus x sp/fp) vs the previous block:

      cpu     cells changed   bytes   larger   slower
      z80              17      -41        0        0
      z80n             17      -41        0        0
      z180             17      -41        0        0
      ez80             17      -41        0        0
      kc160            18      -42        0        0
      r2ka             17      -40        0        0
      r4k              20      -35        0        0
      8080              2       -8        0        0
      8085              2       -8        0        0
      gbz80             2      -11        0        0
                                -308

EVERY CPU SMALLER. 0 cells larger, 0 cells slower, anywhere. That is the part
worth reading twice, because the first attempt at this REGRESSED gbz80 by 229 B
and looked like a Rabbit-only micro-optimisation not worth the rule churn.

The rule churn was not the problem. INCOMPLETE rule churn was. That text has
THREE consumers and they have to move together:

  1. the emitters in the backend      -- 30 sites, now all via 4 helpers
  2. lib/80cc_rules.1                 -- #G4, #IR-const/sym-to-DE, #DE7,
                                         #GB1..#GB6, #285e
  3. filter_dead_reg_copies           -- 80cc's OWN post-render peephole, which
                                         matched `ld h,d`/`ld l,e` as LITERAL
                                         TEXT and silently stopped firing

(3) is the whole 229 B, and it is the one that is easy to miss because it lives
in ir_lower.c, not in the rules file. It drops a dead one-way copy whose
destination is fully reloaded, and it sees ACROSS A LIVE LABEL, which copt's
fixed three-line window cannot -- so the copies it removes are ones no rule can
reach. Its comment now names itself as the third consumer.

Where the z80-family bytes come from: filter_dead_bc_parks, the sibling filter,
already matched `ld bc,hl` and could never see a park spelled `ld c,l; ld b,h`.
Respelling those made a filter that already existed start working. Two of the
#GB rules (#GB1, #GB2) now fire zero times in this corpus because #285b/#285c/
#285d already match the pseudo-op forms and take over -- they are kept for the
non-immediate reload shapes those do not cover.

Regression green at a86e546e46: long_ir 491/491 sp and fp; sccz80 588 (the
multi-CPU gate) + math 384 / string 308 / stdlib 2107 / ctype 7168 / stdio 79,
0 failed; emu.c, enigma and adv_a behavioural in both frame modes.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
10/8/2026 (2) — the r4k blemish, diagnosed and fixed: `ld de,hl`
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Supersedes the r4k paragraph in the block below. 80cc-fp/sp re-measured at
commit 8f5d9a215f; every other column still copied verbatim from the 7/8 table.

The IR_DS_SHARE matrix in the previous block had exactly one blemish: all 26
growing cells were r4k, and none of them was explained. The cause was not the
elision.

  Rabbit 4000/6000 put the 8-bit ALU and register moves on a PREFIXED PAGE.
  `ld d,h` and `ld e,l` are 2 bytes EACH there, while `ld (sp+n),hl` is a
  native 2-byte store and `ld de,hl` a native ONE-byte move. So eliding a
  word store and letting the value ride to its reader traded a 2-byte store
  for a 4-byte copy. Everywhere else the pair is 2 bytes and the store is
  4-6, which is why only r4k grew.

  Measured, one instruction at a time:

                        r4k   r2ka   z80   gbz80
      ld (sp+6),hl        2      -      -       -
      ld d,h / ld e,l     4      2      2       2
      ld de,hl            1      2      2       2

z80asm accepts `ld de,hl` on every target and assembles it to exactly what the
pair produces everywhere except r4k/r6k, so the backend now spells the copy that
way at all 7 HL->DE staging sites (8f5d9a215f). Three copt rules matched the
pair as text and were updated with it.

  the spelling alone   r4k -291B over 46 cells, 46 faster / 0 slower;
                       every other CPU BYTE-IDENTICAL, ticks unchanged
  with IR_DS_SHARE=1   r4k -39B with ZERO cells larger. No CPU has a growing
                       cell any more. Net -1200B (was -1088B).

  So the IR_DS_SHARE matrix now reads: 0 cells slower on any CPU, 0 cells
  larger on any CPU. A pure win on both axes.

The other three gp-pair directions are NOT worth doing, checked rather than
assumed: the backend already emits `ld bc,hl` / `ld hl,bc`, so what is left in
r4k output is 2 adjacent pairs across the 21-bench corpus (6 B) and ZERO in
emu.c — against 16 `ld h,d` emit sites in the compiler source. Count what is
addressable, not what is written. `ld bc,de` / `ld de,bc` assemble to 4 bytes on
r4k, so there is nothing to win there either.

Regression green at 8f5d9a215f: long_ir 491/491 sp and fp with IR_DS_SHARE both
off and on; sccz80 588 (the gate that actually covers r4k) + math 384 / string
308 / stdlib 2107 / ctype 7168 / stdio 79, 0 failed; emu.c, enigma and adv_a
behavioural in both frame modes; and the 391-cell matrix ran every r4k binary in
both configurations with no failures.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
10/8/2026 — 80cc-fp/sp re-measured; IR_DS_SHARE ticks matrix
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
80cc-fp/sp columns re-measured at commit a403b39d0e, branch
80cc-f32-implicit-int-conv. Every other column (sccz80 / xcc -Os / xcc -Of /
sdcc / sdcc-max) is copied verbatim from the 7/8 table below — none of those
toolchains changed. The columns below are the SHIPPED DEFAULT, i.e. IR_DS_SHARE
OFF.

THE MEASUREMENT. Every cell was built and run TWICE on this one compiler, with
the gate off and on: 391 cells (23 benches x 10 cpus x sp/fp, minus the no-IX
combinations). 0 cells failed their run in either configuration, which doubles
as the full-corpus no-abort check.

  IR_DS_SHARE=1  (dead-store elision stops vetoing on every coalesced reader,
                  0c0eb0e006 — vetoes only a reader that reads a slot it never
                  wrote)

    ticks   77 cells faster, 0 SLOWER anywhere — including the CPUs whose
            tick counts are not trustworthy under -b msx. Restricted to the
            valid-tick CPUs it is 47 faster / 0 slower. No byte-for-tick trade
            to weigh: eliding a store removes memory traffic, so bytes and
            cycles move together.
    bytes   201 cells change, net -1088 B.  166 smaller, 26 larger.

  Per cpu (bytes; 'faster' counts tick-improving cells):

      cpu     changed    bytes   smaller   LARGER   faster   ticks
      8080         23     -197        23        0        7   valid
      8085         23      -32        23        0        7   valid
      ez80         25     -233        25        0        8   valid
      gbz80         1       -9         1        0        1   valid
      kc160        23      -36        23        0        8   valid
      z180         23     -217        23        0        8   valid
      z80          23     -217        23        0        8   valid
      z80n         23     -217        23        0        8   unreliable
      r2ka         11       -2         2        0       11   unreliable
      r4k          26      +72         0       26       11   unreliable

  THE ONE BLEMISH IS r4k, AND IT IS EVERY r4k CELL. All 26 growing cells are
  Rabbit 4000, +1..+8 B each, +72 B total; not one r4k cell shrinks, while every
  other CPU is smaller or unchanged. That is systematic, not noise, and it is
  unexplained — r4k ticks still improve on all 11 of those cells, so it reads
  like a Rabbit-specific reload being fatter than the store it replaced rather
  than anything wrong. Worth one look before the elision is widened further;
  the rest of the table says the change is a pure win.

  The biggest movers are the memory-traffic-heavy benches: rle z80 -21 B and
  -2.76% ticks, recordbench z80 -12 B / -2.70%, md5 z180 -24 B / -1.38%,
  fixedbench z180 -25 B / -1.49%. Roughly half the corpus does not move at all.

  Real files (not in this table), IR_DS_SHARE=1 vs off:
      emu.c  fp 23981 -> 23627 (-354)     sp 25420 -> 25373 (-47)
      adv_a, clisp, enigma unchanged; nothing grows.

  Regression green at a403b39d0e with the gate ON: long_ir 491/491 sp and fp;
  sccz80 588 / math 384 / string 308 / stdlib 2107 / ctype 7168 / stdio 79, 0
  failed; emu.c behavioural sp+fp; enigma sp+fp; adv_a interactive sp+fp (get
  flint, then i — the inventory lists the flint, which exercises the parser and
  SH_INVE/SH_GET, the functions this branch's narrowing also touched). Gate off
  is byte-identical to the pre-change compiler across the corpus and all four
  real files.

  STILL OPT-IN. The matrix above is what a default-on flip needed and it came
  back clean, so the flip is now a two-line change to ds_share_on(); it is left
  for the maintainer because an unsound first cut of this same predicate
  miscompiled emu.c earlier the same day (see src/80cc/WIDTH_HANDOVER.md).

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
7/8/2026 — 80cc-fp/sp re-measured: three algebraic rewrites + branchless rotate
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
80cc-fp/sp columns re-measured at commit 3c47d37e91. Every other column
(sccz80 / xcc -Os / xcc -Of / sdcc / sdcc-max) is copied verbatim from the 6/8
table below — none of those toolchains changed.

Two commits since the 6/8 table. Both are pure wins on bytes AND ticks.

  BRANCHLESS SINGLE-BIT RIGHT ROTATE (7e961a7dc4) — gen_rotl lowers a fused
      32-bit ROTATE_LEFT as a byte permutation plus single-bit rotates. The
      right-hand step shifted the wrap bit OUT of L and branched to put it
      back (`srl d / rr e / rr h / rr l / jr nc,+2 / set 7,d`, 12 B). But that
      bit is bit0 of L and is known BEFORE the shift, so seed the carry with
      it and let `rr d` shift it in (`ld a,l / rrca / rr d / ...`, 10 B and
      branchless). In the common rotl8+rotr1 shape the permute ends `ld l,a`,
      so A already holds L and the seed is elided — 3 B at those sites.
      Rabbit needed the missing companion copt fold (`rr d; rr e` -> `rr de`),
      which also drops the `and a` the old form needed: 9 B -> 5 B there.
      8080/8085 are excluded from the fusion (no CB shifts) and unchanged.

  THREE ALGEBRAIC REWRITES IN ir_match (3c47d37e91) — all three turn a TREE of
      bitwise ops into a CHAIN. That is the point, not the operator count: in
      a tree two width-4 intermediates are live at the combining op, they do
      not fit, and the lowerer parks one with push/pop and merges the two back
      through an SP-derived pointer. In a chain one is ever live and the
      register cache carries it. Because that is about how many values are
      LIVE rather than how locals are addressed, they pay in BOTH modes and on
      EVERY CPU including 8080/8085.

        mux       (x & y) | (~x & z)  ==  z ^ (x & (y ^ z))
                  md5's F and G are both this (32 of 64 rounds); so are SHA-1
                  and SHA-256 Ch() and the masked blit (dst & ~m) | (src & m).
                  --opt-disable=pattern:mux
        demorgan  (~x)&(~y) == ~(x|y), (~x)|(~y) == ~(x&y). Same shape one step
                  smaller, and a NOT goes — 12 instructions at width 4.
                  --opt-disable=pattern:demorgan
        pack16    16-bit byte pack, BOTH endiannesses. Endianness is one test:
                  little-endian holds `offset - shift/8` constant across lanes,
                  big-endian holds `offset + shift/8`. Big-endian needs a byte
                  reversal, and at width 2 that IS a rotate by 8, so it reuses
                  IR_ROTL — no new IR op. Width-4 big-endian is still rejected
                  (a 4-byte reverse is not any rotation). --opt-disable=pack16

  WHAT MOVES IN THIS TABLE: md5 (both commits) and intbench (mux only). Every
  other bench is BYTE-IDENTICAL on every CPU, as are adv_a / clisp / enigma /
  emu.c. demorgan and pack16 fire NOWHERE in this corpus — they are out-of-tree
  levers (bitset predicates; big-endian file and network formats) and cost
  nothing when they do not fire.

  md5 is the headline: -970 B fp / -616 B sp on z80 from mux alone, and
  -12849 B summed across all 9 CPUs x sp/fp. The mux output is byte-identical
  to hand-rewriting md5sum.c's F and G macros, i.e. the pattern reaches the
  full source-level ceiling.

  Regression green at 3c47d37e91: long_ir 129 runs at DEFAULTS (exit code
  checked) incl. new rotl32.c / mux.c / demorgan.c / pack16.c; md5 passes on
  all 9 CPUs x sp/fp; run-matrix 42 OK / 4 FAIL — the same pre-existing
  `file not found: rc2014.lib` link failures as baseline, not codegen; every
  opt-out restores the pre-change output byte-for-byte.

  MEASURED EFFECT ON THIS TABLE, against the 6/8 table below. Exactly two
  benchmarks move, on 35 of the 230 cells, and EVERY changed cell improves on
  BOTH axes — no byte-for-tick anywhere:

    md5       -1102 B fp / -828 B sp on z80 (= -132 rotate, -970 mux), and
              -3.3 to -5.2 % ticks on every CPU. Best cells r4k -1209 fp,
              r2ka -1026 fp. 8080/8085 get -616 (mux only — they are excluded
              from the rotate fusion, having no CB shifts).
    intbench  -14 B fp / -21 B sp on z80, -0.5 to -1.4 % ticks. mux only.
    TOTAL     -15749 B summed over all changed cells; 0 regressed cells.

  The other 21 benchmarks are byte-identical on all 9 CPUs in both modes, as
  are adv_a / clisp / enigma / emu.c — demorgan and pack16 fire nowhere in
  this corpus at all.

  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Z80-ONLY SUMMARY — the only slice where all seven columns are populated
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  xcc is z80-only, so on every other CPU row two of the eight columns are
  em-dashes and a like-for-like ranking is impossible. This is the 23 z80 rows
  of the table below, one line per benchmark: each cell is `bytes/ticks`,
  ticks in millions, and a `*` sits immediately before whichever of the two
  leads that row — so `*4990/29.9` is smallest, `5032/*28.2` is fastest, and a
  cell can hold both. Totals cover the 22 rows every column except sdcc-max
  measured (fixedbench is excluded — xcc fails it); sdcc-max ran on 6 rows and
  gets its own sub-total.

  Reading it: sccz80 is smallest on most rows and fastest on NONE — it
  call-threads nearly every operation into a library helper, so bytes move out
  of the function and into the cycle count (2.3x 80cc-fp in total). Against the
  three compilers that inline the same work (xcc, sdcc, 80cc), 80cc-fp is both
  smallest and fastest overall. md5 dominates the size column; strip it and the
  four converge. These are whole-binary sizes with a common CRT base in every
  cell — codesize.sh's `code_compiler` is the metric for judging codegen, and
  this table exists because no shared metric spans four toolchains.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
6/8/2026 — xcc (z80) AND all 80cc fp/sp cells re-measured
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
xcc columns re-measured with the updated xcc (profiles passed through zcc as
-Cx-Os / -Cx-Of; xcc is z80-only, so every other CPU row keeps its em-dash).
80cc-fp/sp re-measured on every CPU at commit 409381b568. sccz80 / sdcc /
sdcc-max columns are copied verbatim from the 5/8 table.

  XCC CHANGES vs the 27/7 measurement (the last time these columns were run):
   - sieve and md5 now BUILD AND RUN. Both previously failed to link
     (undefined `__memset` / duplicate symbol), so their cells read FAIL.
     sieve 12350B/6.53M -Os, 12307B/5.27M -Of; md5 15257B/42.01M, 22328B/32.41M.
   - fixedbench is a NEW FAILURE: it built and passed on 27/7 (5752B/52.5M) and
     now FAILS its own checksum under BOTH profiles, while the same source
     passes under 80cc and sccz80. Its cells read FAIL rather than carrying a
     number, because a failing run's size/ticks mean nothing. For the record it
     built and ran: -Os 5122B/50.77M, -Of 5050B/42.70M, both wrong-answer.
   - -Os and -Of now differ where they previously did not on several rows
     (charbench 5622B/59.73M vs 5513B/38.93M), i.e. the size/speed profiles
     are actually diverging.

Six 80cc changes since the 5/8 table. Four are wins, one is a correctness fix
that costs bytes, one is an inert probe:

  jp -> jr BRANCH RELAXATION (default on, IR_JR=0 opts out) — 80cc emitted a
      3-byte `jp` for every CFG branch and nothing downstream recovered it:
      copt has no addresses and z80asm only ever WIDENS (`jr`->`jp` under
      -opt-speed). The rendered function is now re-scanned and an in-range
      branch rewritten to `jr`, sized by an UPPER-BOUND table that is one
      max-over-CPUs entry per shape — being wrong only costs a conversion, and
      an out-of-range `jr` is a loud assembler error. Unconditional jumps
      INSIDE loops are excluded: taken every iteration, `jr` is a flat +2T
      there, whereas a conditional still wins (7T vs 10T when it falls
      through). 8080/8085 have no `jr` and are byte-identical.

  DEAD WORD-SPILL ELISION (default on, IR_DSWORD=0 opts out) — store_hl and
      store_a_byte mark their slot accesses as WRITES; store_hl_keep_hl did
      not, and it is the helper that commits a CALL RESULT, so every
      call-result spill read as "never written" to the dead-store analysis.
      Fixing the attribution and widening the elision from width-1 to width-2
      removes 46 dead word stores in the corpus and 15 in emu.c. Excludes
      IR_ST_MEM bases (eliding CREATES the reader) and gbz80 (no `ex de,hl`).

  PER-BB DEAD DEFS (--opt-disable=dead-def) — ir_opt_dce counts uses PER VREG,
      so with one-local-one-vreg it cannot see a REDUNDANT def. `int r = 0;
      r += f();` has const-fold rewrite the add into a direct define by the
      CALL and strand the `LD_IMM r <- 0`. A def whose vreg is redefined later
      in the same BB with no read between is now removed — stopping at any
      control transfer, because a BB here can hold a mid-block conditional
      branch.

  RANGED BC HOME FOR A REASSIGNED PARAM — a param multiplied by a multi-bit
      constant is read 7-8 times by the strength-reduced Horner chain, and was
      reloaded from its caller slot for EVERY partial product. Params were
      excluded from both the call-split candidate filter and IR_SPILLAUDIT, so
      the shape was invisible to every census. One eligibility rule now admits
      them: a >=3-read span with no call, plus (for a param) no write, and no
      requirement to cross a call.

  FRAMELESS NARROWED (correctness, +8 B fp) — frameless_ok accepted any param
      homed in BC or DE. DE is the `ex de,hl` scratch, so a DE-homed param is
      reloaded from the CALLER's slot at (ix+d) — through an IX a frameless
      function never sets up. Only a whole-function BC home is accepted now.

  IR_PARAMRELOAD (inert probe) — reports the reloads actually EMITTED per
      spilled param, not raw refs.

  TOTALS (code_compiler, codesize.sh z80, the honest density metric):
    corpus  16984 -> 16305 B   vs sdcc 14153: +20% -> +15%
    emu.c   24696 -> 24410 B (fp)      adv_a 3250 -> 3173
    histbench ticks 44.14M -> 32.07M (-27%), and -23..-33% on every dear-slot
    CPU; ez80/kc160/rabbit unchanged there (the dear-slot cost gate suppresses
    the split). `main` went 25 B -> 7 B in every program.

  Regression green at 409381b568: long_ir 47/47 fp+sp (+ new jrelax.c,
  dsword.c, deaddef.c, csparam.c), run-matrix 56 OK, 420-cell all-CPU compile
  sweep, sccz80 588 tests, emu.c "On The Path" fp+sp, enigma RXSEC fp+sp.

  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Z80-ONLY SUMMARY — the only slice where all seven columns are populated
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  xcc has no backend other than z80, so on every other CPU row two of the eight
  columns are em-dashes and a like-for-like ranking is impossible. This is the
  23 z80 rows of the table below, condensed to one line per benchmark: each
  cell is `bytes/ticks`, ticks in millions, and a `*` sits immediately before
  whichever of the two is the leader for that row — so `*4990/29.9` is the
  smallest on its row, `5032/*28.2` the fastest, and a cell can hold both.
  Totals cover the 22 rows that every column (except sdcc-max) measured —
  fixedbench is excluded because xcc fails it. sdcc-max only ran on 6 rows, so
  it gets a separate 6-row sub-total instead.

  READING IT

  sccz80 is smallest on 21 of 23 rows and fastest on NONE — it is 2.3x the
  ticks of 80cc-fp in total. That is the expected shape, not a density result:
  sccz80 call-threads nearly every operation into a library helper, so its
  ".c-attributable" bytes are low and its cycle count is dominated by call
  overhead. The meaningful size peers are xcc, sdcc and 80cc, all of which
  inline the same work. Against those three, 80cc-fp is SMALLEST overall
  (145210 B vs xcc -Os 154713, xcc -Of 161401, sdcc 163367) and fastest overall
  (645.0M vs xcc -Of 707.4M and sdcc 783.0M), and it leads on 11 of 23 rows for
  speed against sdcc's 6 and xcc -Of's 4.

  Caveats on the totals:
   - md5 dominates the size column (14948..29274 B). Excluding it, the four
     inlining compilers are much closer and 80cc-fp's size lead narrows.
   - The size total is whole-binary, so it carries a fixed CRT/library base in
     every cell. codesize.sh's `code_compiler` (the density metric quoted in
     the header) isolates the compiler-attributable bytes and is the number to
     use for judging codegen; this table is for cross-compiler comparison,
     where a common metric across four different toolchains does not exist.
   - fp vs sp: fp is both smaller (-2.0%) and faster (-7.2%) in total. sp wins
     individual rows (charbench, matrixbench, hashbench) but the IX-relative
     frame is still the better default on z80.

  THE TWO OUTLIERS

  crcbench — xcc -Of 86.1M vs 80cc-fp 117.8M, the largest single deficit in
  the table (80cc still beats sdcc's 141.8M here). Read the crc32 asm: per
  loop iteration 80cc emits 335 instructions to xcc's 172, and 64 of those are
  push/pop. 80cc parks the 32-bit `crc` on the STACK and peeks it with
  `pop hl; pop de; push de; push hl` for each of the 8 unrolled steps; xcc
  keeps the long in DEHL with fixed (ix+-d) slots. That shuffling alone is
  ~44M ticks over 64512 iterations — more than the whole 31.6M gap. Second,
  xcc fuses the `crc & 1` test into the shift: `srl d; rr e; rr h; rr l`
  leaves bit 0 in carry, so `jr nc` IS the test, and the eight explicit
  `ld a,(ix-10); and 1` sequences disappear. Both `srl d` counts are 8, so the
  shift is NOT duplicated across the ternary arms. This is the sharpest
  instance of the known long/DEHL stack-park behaviour (LONG_DEBC_RESIDENCY_
  PLAN territory), not a crcbench-specific quirk.

  md5 — 80cc 20099 B against sccz80's 14948 and xcc -Os's 15257, but 22328 for
  xcc -Of and 29274 for plain sdcc. The spread is unrolling policy, not
  density: the size-oriented profiles keep the round loops rolled.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
5/8/2026 — 80cc-fp/sp re-measured (HEAD 79fda1f2): remat-LEA + loop-const cleanups
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
80cc-fp/sp columns re-measured at commit 79fda1f2 with the current compiler.
Movement since the 3/8 table (below, at f37bf27315): binary code drops
Σ fp -980 B and sp -1964 B over 230 rows, with 0 new FAIL cells.

Per CPU (binary bytes, fp / sp):
  z80 / z80n / z180    -215 / -296     the dear-slot z80 family, the largest move
  ez80                  -67 / -290     sp gains most, from remat-LEA's sp path
  kc160                -127 / -123
  r2ka  -73 / -73       r4k  -68 / -68
  8080 / 8085 / gbz80   fp == sp:  sp -186 / -135 / -201

Three changes landed since 3/8.

(1) remat-LEA — DEFAULT-ON, IR_REMAT_LEA=0 opts out. A frame-slot address of a
    local (&x) is a per-function constant, so the compiler recomputes it at each
    use instead of spilling and reloading it. It is gated to call-free functions
    and turned off on the byte-wise CPUs (808x/gbz80). This is the standout:
    interpbench drops 83 B AND 4.1% ticks (39.55M -> 37.92M) — the worst-loser
    bench improves on BOTH axes — and it drives the large ez80-sp -290.

(2) Constant-bound loop cleanups — two folds. A `for (i=0;i<K;i++)` with K a
    compile-time constant no longer builds K as a byte and then widens it
    (`ld a,K; ld l,a; ld h,0` becomes `ld hl,K`), and the compiler drops its dead
    zero-trip guard (`if (K==0) skip`). The guard uses a phantom BR_ZERO that
    keeps the CFG edge for the allocator but emits no code, so the allocation does
    not change and no row regresses. Together these give the broad ~-5 B on almost
    every bench (ptrbench -30, histbench -15, charbench -10).

(3) Correctness fixes — real bugs closed, no bench size win expected.
    - The call-split BC-interference bug across a flat-inverted inner loop
      miscompiled sieve on 808x/gbz80 (it returned 4000, not 1007). The byte-wise
      sp moves partly reflect the corrected codegen.
    - Direct volatile-global reads were folded together or over-read. They now
      read the correct count and width. The benches use no volatile globals, so
      no movement shows here.

Ticks: interpbench -4.1% from remat-LEA. Every other cell is faster or neutral,
with no tick regression. Other columns (sccz80/xcc/sdcc) are copied from the 3/8
table below.

Full regression green at 79fda1f2: long_ir 100/100 fp+sp, run-matrix all suites
fp+sp, IR_REMAT_LEA=0 byte-identical to the pre-flip default.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
3/8/2026 — 80cc-fp/sp re-measured: call-bounded live-range splitting DEFAULT-ON
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
80cc-fp/sp columns re-measured at commit f37bf27315 with the current compiler.
EVERY row shrinks vs the 1/8 table (Σ fp -1197 B, sp -1500 B over 230 rows).
Two distinct changes landed on the branch since then:

(1) IR_CALLSPLIT — call-bounded live-range splitting, now DEFAULT-ON. A spilled
                  reused width-2 value with a call-free span of >=3 READS is made
                  BC-resident inside that span and spilled (slot-homed) across the
                  calls it crosses: reload BC from the slot after a call, reuse it
                  (add hl,bc / ld e,c;ld d,b) for the >=3 in-span reads. Written-
                  in-span values use a WRITE-BOTH commit (an in-span def writes
                  both the slot and BC), so the slot stays coherent, no exit spill.
                  Opt out with IR_CALLSPLIT=0 (byte-identical to pre-flip).

     This is the LARGE per-row win, and ONLY on 6 benches x DEAR-slot CPUs (a
     frame-slot word access is dear on z80/z80n/z180/8080/8085/gbz80 — `ld hl,N;
     add hl,sp; …` — so BC reuse is a pure bytes+ticks win): strbench -85 fp
     (z80/z80n/z180); hashbench -42 fp / -58 sp; searchbench & maskbench -25 fp /
     -34 sp; matrixbench -41 fp / -12 sp; vecbench -11 fp / -5 sp; plus the same
     benches on 8080/8085/gbz80. CHEAP-slot CPUs (ez80/kc160/rabbit) get NO
     call-split change — the selection's dear-slot cost gate (g0_word_cost(SLOT,
     READ) - (BC,READ) >= 15) self-suppresses them. 0 regressed cells anywhere.

(2) Instruction-selection fixes (also new since 1/8) — the SMALL broad -1..-24 B
     on every OTHER bench and on the cheap CPUs: `ld hl,K` direct (not `ld de,K;
     ex de,hl`), `add hl,bc` / `sbc hl,bc` for a BC-resident operand, and the IVSR
     LFTR unsigned-bound clamp elision. All-CPU, not slot-gated (hence the cheap
     CPUs move here too); biggest on rle (-24) and the ALU-heavy benches.

  Corpus code_compiler (the honest density metric, codesize.sh z80) attributable
  to the split alone: the 16-bit bench set drops fp -195 B / sp -114 B (strbench
  -78 fp, hashbench -49 sp). The split win is inherently call-bounded — a call
  invalidates the register cache and forces the slot reload the split eliminates;
  call-free reuse is already served by the belief cache (whole-range homing gave a
  0-byte delta, not pursued).

  Full regression green (f37bf27315): long_ir 99/99 fp+sp (+ new callsplit.c
  regression), corpus benches behavioural fp+sp, sccz80, enigma RXSEC fp+sp,
  emu.c "On The Path" fp+sp, IR_CALLSPLIT=0 byte-identical to the pre-split
  baseline. Other columns (sccz80/xcc/sdcc) copied from the 1/8 table.

1/8/2026 (s8) — 80cc-fp/sp re-measured: frameless-via-sp COSTED FLIP default-on
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
80cc-fp/sp columns re-measured at commit 3a8da5eac3 with the current compiler.
Since the s6 table the frameless-via-sp flip (#13) was hardened and turned
DEFAULT-ON as a COSTED flip:

  IR_SPFLIP       a framed fn whose IX frame-pointer apparatus is (near-)dead is
                  re-lowered FRAMELESS in sp mode. Widened from the zero-cost case
                  (no (ix+-d) accesses) to costed flips: flip iff 2*N < 6 (N<=2
                  (ix+-d) data accesses = the measured near-clean corpus knee).
                  fp-mode only; opt out with IR_SPFLIP=0.
                  Also hardened: IR_SPFLIP=0 now disables (was a footgun that
                  read "0" as truthy); IR_IX_VERIFY gained the IY analog.

  EFFECT ON THIS TABLE:
   - fp column shrinks on every bench: -30..-51 B on z80/z80n/z180 (charbench -30,
     hashbench -48, interpbench -51, strbench -46, ptrbench -40; the ~-30 B floor
     is the shared framework test.c flipping, bench code on top).
   - sp column UNCHANGED (0 delta on every row, every CPU) — the flip only fires
     in fp mode, so sp is byte-identical to s6.
   - ticks: every valid-tick bench FASTER, zero regressions (a pure win both axes —
     the flip drops per-CALL frame setup/teardown from hot fns; e.g. z80 strbench
     -2.2%, ptrbench, hashbench).

  PER-CPU byte win (corpus code, fp): z80/z80n -1305, z180 -1298, rabbit r2ka -1399
  / r4k -1386, ez80 -745, kc160 -593; 8080/8085/gbz80 have no IX so are inert (fp
  == sp). kc160's cheap sp-addressing makes the z80-calibrated 2*N over-flip a few
  benches (+3 B each) but it still NETS -593 B, so it is taken (density-positive).

  Full regression green (3a8da5eac3): long_ir 54/54 fp+sp, emu behavioural fp+sp,
  enigma RXSEC fp+sp, sccz80 callee/callee2/fastcall, corpus x8 CPUs fp no
  require_slot aborts, IR_IX_VERIFY (IX+IY) 0 warnings on the flipped fns.
  Other columns (sccz80/xcc/sdcc) copied verbatim from the s6/27-7 tables.

  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  CODE DENSITY vs sdcc (code_compiler section, the HONEST metric — codesize.sh,
  z80; NOT the full-binary column above, which flatters 80cc by a ~1.5KB
  sdcc-printf/runtime handicap and shows 80cc ~10% SMALLER):

    corpus code   80cc-fp 17445  vs  sdcc 14153   = +23%
    emu.c  code   80cc-fp 24745  vs  sdcc 19641   = +25%  (IR_SPFLIP=0: 24811 = +26%)

  Trajectory (corpus): +35% -> +29% (symbol-remat) -> +23% (residency + this flip).
  sdcc totals unchanged from the documented baselines, so it is like-for-like.
  Per-bench: 80cc WINS switchbench -33%, recordbench -7%; near parity lexbench
  +4%, crc/int +11%, sort +15%; still behind on the allocator-bound loop/pointer
  benches — interpbench +86% (worst), strbench/matrixbench +50%, maskbench +53%,
  ptrbench +48%. Remaining gap is register-allocation quality there, NOT frame
  overhead (that lever is now largely spent). Goal: within ~10% of sdcc.

31/7/2026 (s6) — 80cc-fp/sp re-measured: residency features FLIPPED DEFAULT-ON
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
80cc-fp/sp columns re-measured at commit be18473d93 with the current compiler.
Since the 27/7 table (below) the following are now DEFAULT-ON (were opt-in/new):

  IR_DEADSTORE    dead byte-spill store elision (-1272 B corpus, both modes)
  IX callee-saved arc:
     A  native sp saves IX when it uses it (fixes a mixed-mode fp/sp ABI hazard)
     B  op_clobbers — a direct call preserves IX, like IY
     C  idx2 word homes ACROSS calls (sp mode, dear-slot z80/z180/z80n only)
  idxhalf         byte homes in index halves (sp, z80/z80n/ez80, net-byte gated)
  CTYPE_PRESERVE  ctype fastcalls __preserves_regs(b,c,d,e,ix,iy) — kept resident
                  across a ctype call instead of spill/reload
  (A-carry / HL-carry were already default-on at 30/7)

  Correctness fixes surfaced by enigma (real file, now in the gate): char->int
  fastcall-arg widen; call result committed to an IX/IY home across a BB edge;
  drop a stale scalar cache after `add iy,de`.

  Measured but HELD opt-in: idx3 (--reg-iy-half) — corpus -493 B / -1.41%t but
  enigma +96 B / +10.8%t (idx3<->idxhalf IY competition) — awaits a coordinated
  pair<->halves allocator. Also opt-in: IR_SPFLIP, IR_RANGED. Removed: IR_DEADSLOT.

  Full regression green (be18473d93): long_ir 47/47, corpus 23/23 behavioural,
  ctype 256/256, sccz80 22/22, enigma RXSEC, emu behavioural — all fp+sp.
  Other columns (sccz80/xcc/sdcc) copied from the 27/7 table.
